2591.col_2: The thin tail of a rat, often carried by young Lalafellin boys as a good-luck charm. Bait for ocean fishing.

2592.name: midge basket
2592.col_2: A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of biting midges. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2593.name: crab ball
2593.col_2: A ball of crabmeat and rye flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.

2594.name: butterworm
2594.col_2: If allowed to pupate, this bright-yellow larva will transform into a hideous moth which can devour an entire tunic in a single turn of the sun. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2595.name: bass ball
2595.col_2: A ball of dark bass and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for freshwater fishing.

2596.name: spoon worm
2596.col_2: Also colorfully known as a “fisherman's member,” the stench of this sea-dwelling creature when sliced up is perfect for attracting hungry fish. Live bait for ocean fishing.

2597.name: syrphid basket
2597.col_2: A tightly knitted wicker basket filled with a swarm of angry syrphids. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2598.name: herring ball
2598.col_2: A ball of Indigo herring and sunset flour paste. Processed bait for ocean fishing.

2599.name: honey worm
2599.col_2: The honeyfly will lay its eggs in beehives where, upon hatching, the larvae will feed on honey until pupation. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2600.name: sand leech
2600.col_2: A spineless creature which hides patiently under the desert─ofttimes for several moons─until a larger beast passes nearby. The leech will then attach itself to the new host's leg and proceed to drink deep of the beast's blood until its belly is full, after which it releases itself back to the desert to wait for its next victim. Live bait for dunefishing.

2601.name: stem borer
2601.col_2: This longhorn beetle larva can most commonly be found burrowed deep into the trunks of fallen logs. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2602.name: sand gecko
2602.col_2: When night falls, thousands of these tiny scalekin can be seen scampering about the Sagolii Desert in search of the beetles on which they dine. Live bait for dunefishing.

2603.name: glowworm
2603.col_2: It is not known why one end of these vilekin shines bright like a candle. It is, however, known that the light emitted by these creatures makes them a perfect target for hungry fish. Live bait for freshwater and ocean fishing.

2604.name: rolling stone
2604.col_2: When threatened, this tiny desert crustacean will curl itself into a ball which, to the untrained eye, will appear no more than a simple pebble. Live bait for dunefishing.

2605.name: hoverworm
2605.col_2: Unlike other vilekin larvae, the hoverworm is not confined to life on the ground. Filling its belly with air allows it to freely ride the thermals over the Sea of Clouds. Live bait for skyfishing.

2606.name: fistful of northern krill
2606.col_2: Microscopic shrimp which inhabit the colder sea currents hailing from the northern seas. Live bait for ocean fishing.

2607.name: caddisfly larva
2607.col_2: The fact they are extremely difficult to harvest from their underwater homes makes fishing with caddisfly larvae an option for only the most well-to-do anglers. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

2608.name: soil creeper
2608.col_2: Atypical of common caterpillars, this sand-dwelling species is covered in a rock-like outer skin which serves to prevent the loss of moisture to the hot desert sun. Live bait for dunefishing.

2609.name: balloon bug
2609.col_2: With wings too underdeveloped for flying, this beetle has adopted another method of locomotion about the Sea of Clouds─a second bladder it fills with a noxious lighter-than-air gas. This foul stench is known to attract larger, hungrier creatures. Live bait for skyfishing.

2610.name: chocobo fly
2610.col_2: A freshwater fishing lure made from a chocobo feather. The faint aroma of stable hay brings back memories of a simpler time.

2611.name: floating minnow
2611.col_2: A light plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Especially effective when used to land fish swimming close to the water's surface.

2612.name: brass spoon lure
2612.col_2: A polished brass lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.

2613.name: shrimp cage feeder
2613.col_2: A small metal cage packed with a pungent mixture of chopped shrimp. Fish are drawn to the area as pieces of shrimp break off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.

2614.name: crow fly
2614.col_2: A caddisfly-shaped lure crafted from a crow feather. Recommended for freshwater fly fishing novices.

2615.name: silver spoon lure
2615.col_2: A polished silver lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting fish. Especially effective in lakes.

2616.name: steel jig
2616.col_2: The weight of this steel lure allows for casting great distances, such as from coastlines.

2617.name: sinking minnow
2617.col_2: A heavy plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Effective in attracting fish from both surface and floor.

2618.name: snurble fly
2618.col_2: A freshwater fishing lure made from a snurble tuft.

2619.name: heavy steel jig
2619.col_2: The sheer weight of this steel lure allows for casting tremendous distances, such as from coastlines.

2620.name: spinner
2620.col_2: A metal river lure designed to resemble both a mayfly and a minnow, allowing for use in a variety of different situations.

2621.name: krill cage feeder
2621.col_2: A small metal cage packed with northern krill. Fish are drawn to the area as krill float off from the cage. Processed bait for ocean fishing.

2622.name: mythril spoon lure
2622.col_2: A polished mythril lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of lake and marsh life.

2623.name: wildfowl fly
2623.col_2: A freshwater lure made from a wildfowl feather. Its uncanny resemblance to a mayfly makes it irresistible to vilekin-feeding fish such as trout.

2624.name: topwater frog
2624.col_2: A light freshwater lure crafted to resemble a frog. Best suited for larger prey such as pikes and certain trout.

2625.name: rainbow spoon lure
2625.col_2: A shiny blacklip oyster shell lure shaped like a spoon so it will oscillate when dragged through the water, attracting all manner of aquatic life. Especially effective in lakes.

2626.name: spinnerbait
2626.col_2: Several small spinners joined together to resemble a school of fish. Especially effective in rivers.

2627.name: streamer
2627.col_2: A freshwater fly designed to sink below the water's surface, and by doing so, attract the larger carnivorous fish living near the floor.

2628.name: yumizuno
2628.col_2: A curved man-made lure used traditionally in the Far East, the name means literally “bow horn.” Increases chances of landing a big catch, even when casting from shore.

2651.name: Monoa mask
2651.col_2: A wooden mask used in Padjali ceremonies. A rough translation of the word monoa is “to sit silently on the land and speak.”

4555.name: vial of ether
4555.col_2: Processed via the alchemical extraction of aetheric essence occurring in elemental crystals, the contents of this vial instantly restore a small amount of MP.

4556.name: vial of hi-ether
4556.col_2: Processed via the alchemical extraction of aetheric essence occurring in elemental crystals, the contents of this vial instantly restore a fair amount of MP.

4558.col_2: Processed via the alchemical extraction of aetheric essence occurring in elemental crystals, the contents of this vial instantly restore a sizable amount of MP.

4559.name: bottle of elixir
4559.col_2: This special blend of herbal extracts and aetheric essence rejuvenates body and mind, instantly restoring HP and MP.

4560.name: bottle of hi-elixir
4560.col_2: This special blend of herbal extracts and aetheric essence rejuvenates body and mind, instantly restoring HP and MP.

4561.name: bottle of dusken draught
4561.col_2: Powdered coral gives this medicinal concoction the deep amber tone from which it gets its name. It is distributed to members of the Lominsan Armada during battle to provide quick recovery from physical wounds.

4562.name: bottle of kiss of the morning meadow
4562.description: bottles of kiss of the morning meadow
4562.col_2: When taken internally, this blend of rare forest herbs stimulates the mind, allowing for immediate recovery of MP. Conjurers serving alongside Gridania's Wood Wailers and the Gods' Quiver often use the potion in the field during battle when there is not enough time to recover naturally.

4563.name: vial of onyx tears
4563.col_2: This fragrant fusion of aromatic oils has long been used by the Brass Blades of Ul'dah to instantly rejuvenate both body and mind.

4564.name: bottle of antidote
4564.col_2: This alchemically crafted restorative instantly cures most instances of poison.

4565.name: bottle of eye drops
4565.col_2: This alchemically crafted restorative instantly cures most instances of blindness.

4566.name: bottle of echo drops
4566.col_2: This alchemically crafted restorative instantly cures most instances of silence.

4567.name: bottle of smelling salts
4567.col_2: This alchemically crafted restorative instantly rouses most sleeping targets.

4568.name: bottle of spine drops
4568.col_2: This alchemically crafted restorative instantly cures most instances of paralysis.

4569.name: gold needle
4569.col_2: The properties of this solid-gold needle include curing petrification and pricking fingers.

4570.name: tuft of phoenix down
4570.col_2: The billowy plumage of the fledgling Phoenix─a legendary bird that, upon each fiery death, is said to rise from its own ashes in a literal “blaze of glory.” When placed within fifteen yalms of one who is incapacitated, it will instantly revive the person. While some cultures insist that the tailfeather's restorative properties trump those of down, these claims have yet to be proven in any sort of scientific capacity.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Cannot be used during certain duties.

4571.name: bottle of company-issue expectorant
4571.col_2: This herbal concoction clears passageways blocked with blood or bile, allowing for easier breathing and quick recovery from unconsciousness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Cannot be used during battle.

4572.name: bottle of company-issue tonic
4572.col_2: This herbal concoction is guaranteed to clear passageways blocked with blood or bile, allowing for easier breathing and quick recovery from unconsciousness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Cannot be used during battle.

4573.name: over-aspected cluster
4573.col_2: A large crystalline manifestation of aetheric energy exhibiting an extreme elemental charge. When released, the energy has been known to restore the corporeal and spiritual state of those otherwise incapacitated.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Cannot be used during battle.

4766.col_2: A large, tender slab of meat taken from the shoulder of an aldgoat.

4767.name: cut of raptor shank
4767.col_2: An extra-lean, tough piece of meat taken from the leg of a raptor.

4768.name: cut of buffalo sirloin
4768.col_2: A cut of tender, lean meat taken from the rear back of a buffalo.

4769.name: eft tail

4770.name: orobon liver

4771.col_2: A fat megalocrab leg, bursting with sweet, juicy meat.

4772.name: chicken egg
4772.col_2: The egg of a domesticated chicken.

4773.name: dodo egg
4773.col_2: The heavy egg of a wild dodo.

4774.name: puk egg
4774.col_2: The lightweight egg of a puk.

4775.name: apkallu egg
4775.col_2: The large egg of a wild apkallu.

4776.name: strip of malm kelp
4776.col_2: This dark green variety of seaweed found in all five of Eorzea's seas has been known to grow up to a malm in length.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4777.name: wild onion
4777.col_2: A pungent bulb vegetable native to the Near East.

4778.name: Coerthan carrot
4778.col_2: A long orange root vegetable commonly grown in the rocky alpine soil of the Coerthas region.

4779.name: ogre pumpkin
4779.col_2: A bright-orange squash which sweetens in flavor when cooked.

4780.name: ruby tomato
4780.col_2: Though many botanists claim this tangy blood red specimen is more closely related to a fruit than a vegetable, it is widely accepted across Eorzea as the latter.

4781.name: alpine parsnip
4781.col_2: A long white root vegetable indigenous to the mountainous region of Coerthas.

4782.name: head of La Noscean lettuce
4782.col_2: A crisp leafy vegetable native to the plains of La Noscea.

4783.name: bunch of Cieldalaes spinach
4783.col_2: An iron-rich leafy vegetable native to the Cieldalaes.

4784.name: sprig of highland parsley
4784.col_2: Oft used as a garnish in other dishes, this pungent vegetable grows in abundance in the mountainous region of upper La Noscea.

4785.name: paprika
4785.col_2: A pepper which can be dried and ground to make a mild red spice. It is often used in medicines, as well as in cooking.

4786.name: pair of nopales
4786.col_2: An edible oval-leaved cactus brought back by explorers of the New World.

4787.name: popoto
4787.col_2: A starchy tuberous vegetable originally introduced to Eorzea by explorers from the distant western continent.

4788.name: wizard eggplant
4788.col_2: A firm purple-skinned vegetable indigenous to the mountains of the Near East. A common wives' tale claims if you eat too many of this vegetable, you will turn into one.

4789.name: head of midland cabbage
4789.col_2: A round leafy vegetable which prefers the steady climate of the Black Shroud.

4790.name: aloe leaf
4790.col_2: A thick spiny-leaved cactus indigenous to the southern continent of Meracydia. The Miqo'te are known to treat severe burns with the cool gel-like substance found inside the leaves.

4791.name: salt leek
4791.col_2: A long, pungent, leafy vegetable that lacks a bulb like that of its cousin, the onion.

4792.name: ramhorn zucchini
4792.col_2: This long, thin variety of squash earns its name from its resemblance to the horn of a mountain ram.

4793.name: maiden artichoke
4793.col_2: The leaf-like bud of an artichoke plant. Due to the roughness of its petals, only the fleshy lower portions can be consumed, as well as the center of the bud, commonly known as the “heart.”

4794.name: shriekshroom
4794.col_2: The underdeveloped sporeling of a funguar.

4795.name: chanterelle
4795.col_2: An edible mushroom known for its leaf-like appearance as well as its fruit-like fragrance.

4796.name: gil bun
4796.col_2: This tiny round mushroom has a cap which resembles a coin, and is known for its rich flavor and pungent aroma.

4797.name: button mushroom
4797.col_2: A small white mushroom commonly found in moist areas across Eorzea.

4798.name: white truffle
4798.col_2: A rare white mushroom that grows in the soil, rather than above it, making the specimen almost impossible to locate. It is treasured as a delicacy for its unique aroma.

4799.name: ratstool
4799.col_2: The underdeveloped “sporeling” of a myconid. Popular myth has that rats will use the chair-shaped fungus as a place to rest.

4800.name: black truffle
4800.col_2: A rare black mushroom that grows in the soil, rather than above it, making the specimen almost impossible to locate. It is treasured as a delicacy for its unique aroma.

4801.name: Dalamud nut
4801.col_2: The shell which encases this walnut is reminiscent of the (now fallen) lesser moon of its namesake.

4802.name: moon nut
4802.col_2: The ghostly white shell which encases this walnut is reminiscent of the celestial body of its namesake.

4803.name: kukuru bean
4803.col_2: This seed of the kukuru tree is the primary ingredient in chocolate.

4804.name: Cinderfoot olive
4804.col_2: The seed of an olive tree, often preserved in brine or pressed to make oil.

4805.name: Gridanian chestnut
4805.col_2: The seed of a chestnut tree, this savory nut is covered in a coat of prickly spikes.

4806.name: Gridanian walnut
4806.col_2: The seed of a walnut tree, this fragrant nut is covered by a thin, fleshy outer shell and a hard inner shell.

4807.name: iron acorn
4807.col_2: The seed of an oak tree, this small nut is covered by an extremely hard outer shell.

4808.name: bunch of lowland grapes
4808.col_2: A semisweet variety of grape which has adapted to the volcanic soil abundant on Vylbrand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4811.col_2: A sour citrus fruit indigenous to the Near East.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4812.name: branch of pixie plums
4812.col_2: A tart fruit commonly grown in mountain orchards in the Coerthas region.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4813.name: alligator pear
4813.col_2: A soft green fruit, also known as “Shroud butter.” Though not thought to be indigenous to Eorzea, it is not certain how the plant first came to the realm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4814.name: bunch of blood currants
4814.col_2: A tart red berry found growing throughout the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4815.name: rolanberry
4815.col_2: A tart fruit─one of few still found growing in the devastated region of Mor Dhona.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4816.name: prickly pineapple
4816.col_2: A sweet and tangy fruit covered in a thick, spike-laden skin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

4817.name: handful of sunflower seeds
4817.col_2: The fruit of a sunflower, this small seed is covered by a thin black shell.

4818.name: handful of buffalo beans
4818.col_2: A common variety of green bean recognizable by its long thin pods. Buffalo are said to be fond of the beans, and have been known to eat entire crops if left unchecked.

4819.name: box of sticky rice
4819.col_2: This grain is imported from a land far to the east. When cooked, it has a consistency slightly more glutinous than normal rice.

4820.name: pod of Lalafellin lentils
4820.col_2: Thin round beans resembling tiny convex lenses. Thought to have been introduced to Eorzea by the realm's first Lalafellin settlers.

4821.name: ear of millioncorn
4821.col_2: Hundreds of sweet yellow kernels adorn each cob of this vegetable native to the recently discovered New World.

4822.name: pod of jade peas
4822.col_2: Sweet green beans recognizable by their thin, crescent-shaped pods.

4823.name: sheaf of rye
4823.col_2: A dark variety of rye grass commonly found growing in the higher elevations of Mor Dhona and Coerthas.

4824.name: sheaf of sunset wheat
4824.col_2: A common variety of golden brown wheat eaten as a staple in many of Eorzea's city<hex:021F0103>states.

4828.name: stick of cinnamon
4828.col_2: The sweet-smelling bark of the cinnamon tree is often dried and ground into a spice used to add flavor to confectionaries, though it is also commonly used in medicines.

4829.name: bulb of Garlean garlic
4829.col_2: A pungent spice used to flavor many different varieties of dishes. It is also thought to ward off vampiric bats, but there is no evidence to substantiate that claim.

4830.name: pinch of black pepper
4830.col_2: An aromatic spice used in cooking as well as pickling.

4831.name: sprig of cloves
4831.col_2: A sweet-smelling spice made from the dried buds of the clove tree. It is used to flavor confectionaries, and as an essential oil.

4832.name: sprig of fresh marjoram
4832.col_2: A sweet-smelling herb used in cooking and in medicines.

4833.name: bundle of vanilla beans
4833.col_2: A sweet-smelling spice made from the dried pod of the rare vanilla plant. It is often used in the making of confectionaries as well as medicines.

4834.name: sprig of galago mint
4834.col_2: A leafy herb with a crisp, fragrant aroma. It is often used in cooking and in teas, as well as for its essential oil.

4835.name: pot of Ala Mhigan mustard
4835.col_2: When dried and ground into a fine powder, this yellow-tinged spice can add quite the kick to any dish.

4836.name: pearl ginger rootstock
4836.col_2: An exotic root vegetable native to the Far East that is often dried, ground, and used in cooking as well as in the creation of medicines.

4837.name: sprig of midland basil
4837.col_2: A fragrant herb used to flavor various meat and poultry dishes.

4838.name: dragon pepper
4838.col_2: A red-hot spice known to cause severe burns in the mouths of those who consume too many.

4839.name: handful of laurel leaves
4839.col_2: A savory spice made from the dried leaves of the laurel bush, or as it is known by some, the yanny bush.

4840.name: sprig of fresh mugwort
4840.col_2: The young leaves of the mugwort plant are used not only as a spice in cooking, but also as a curative agent in various unguents.

4841.name: bunch of thyme leaves
4841.col_2: A fragrant herb used to flavor various meat and poultry dishes.

4842.name: handful of almonds
4842.col_2: A tear-shaped nut which can be used to season exotic sweets, or pressed for its fragrant oil.

4843.name: bunch of desert saffron
4843.col_2: This spice made from the dried styles of the desert saffron flower gives a bright-yellow color to dishes.

4844.name: handful of nutmeg seeds
4844.col_2: A sweet-smelling seed that is ground into a powder and used to flavor pastries and tea. It is also widely used in Far Eastern medicines.

4845.name: sprig of Sagolii sage
4845.col_2: A savory herb often found growing in parched desert environments. It is used in cooking and various medicinal ointments and unguents.

4846.name: basket of Thanalan tea leaves
4846.col_2: These leaves, when dried and steeped in hot water, create a sweet-smelling tea known for its curative properties.

4847.name: pinch of table salt
4847.col_2: Finely ground salt used not only for flavoring foods, but for pickling and preserving as well.

4848.name: pot of maple sugar
4848.col_2: Crystallized sugar made from boiling down maple syrup.

4849.name: pot of maple syrup
4849.col_2: A sweet, dark liquid made by boiling down maple sap.

4850.name: pot of honey
4850.col_2: Bees make this sweet golden honey from the nectar of flowers.

4851.name: pinch of powdered sugar
4851.col_2: Sweet, snow-like sugar, perfect for dusting Starlight Celebration sweets.

4852.name: can of sweet cream
4852.col_2: The butterfat-rich layer skimmed off of buffalo milk. Widely used in confectionaries.

4853.name: stick of smooth butter
4853.col_2: A smooth, fatty cream made by churning buffalo milk.

4854.name: pot of kukuru butter
4854.col_2: A thick oil extracted from kukuru beans. Used in making chocolate.

4855.name: pinch of kukuru powder
4855.col_2: Roasted kukuru beans ground into a fine powder. Used in making chocolate.

4857.name: bottle of olive oil
4857.col_2: A fragrant light-green oil extracted from pressed olives.

4859.name: bottle of cider vinegar
4859.col_2: A fruity vinegar made from fermenting faerie apples.

4860.name: bottle of dark vinegar
4860.col_2: A high-quality distilled vinegar made from select lowland grapes.

4861.name: piece of pie dough
4861.col_2: Simple pie dough made of flour and butter.

4862.name: bottle of sour red
4862.col_2: Made from lowland grapes grown on arid soil, this vinegary wine is more suited to cooking than it is to drinking (though that does little to stop most Lominsan pirates from drowning their sorrows in the phenolic seepage).

4863.name: cube of gelatin
4863.col_2: A clear gelling agent extracted from animal skin and fish bones.

4864.name: pot of fish stock
4864.col_2: Broth created from boiling down the flesh and bones of various types of seafood.

4865.name: pot of tomato sauce
4865.col_2: A tangy sauce made from crushed tomatoes.

4866.name: serving of dodo stuffing
4866.col_2: A mixture of dried bread, nuts, and fruit, blended with several savory spices.

4867.name: bowl of chicken stock
4867.col_2: A clear golden broth made by boiling chicken bones.

4868.name: bunch of gysahl greens
4868.col_2: A leafy vegetable indigenous to the Near East. While too bitter for most people's tastes, chocobos are known to enjoy the flavor, and thus the greens are often used as fodder for the animals.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by offering multiple servings)

4869.name: Merlthor goby
4869.col_2: A vividly striped saltwater fish commonly found in the Strait of Merlthor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4870.name: Lominsan anchovy
4870.col_2: These small saltwater fish form massive schools resembling colossal sea creatures to discourage predators from approaching.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4871.name: finger shrimp
4871.col_2: A common saltwater shrimp found in the plankton-rich waters of the Sea of Jade.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4872.name: ocean cloud
4872.col_2: A semi-transparent jellyfish commonly found in the Strait of Merlthor, where it goes through nine separate stages of development before reaching adulthood.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4873.name: sea cucumber
4873.col_2: A purple, spiny, sluglike creature found in the shallows off of the island of Mazlaya, and treasured in the Far East as a delicacy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4874.name: harbor herring
4874.col_2: This particular variety of herring will gather in busy harbors to feed on the small sea creatures which consume the waste dumped from ships.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4875.name: vongola clam
4875.col_2: A tasty bivalve mollusk commonly found on and near the island of Bianaq.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4876.name: coral butterfly
4876.col_2: A colorful saltwater fish commonly found in the warm seas around the island of Bianaq. Not known for its flavor, the wavekin is most often kept as a pet.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4877.name: Moraby flounder
4877.col_2: A flat bottom-feeder commonly found in the relatively calm waters of Moraby Bay.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4878.name: pebble crab
4878.col_2: A small bluish grey crab found in tide pools along the La Noscean coast.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4879.name: tiger cod
4879.col_2: A striped saltwater fish indigenous to the cold northern waters of the Bloodbrine Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4880.name: helmet crab
4880.col_2: This saltwater wavekin, most commonly found in the shallows of the Strait of Merlthor, is protected by a hard shell resembling a helmet.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4881.name: Rothlyt oyster
4881.col_2: Also known as the milk of the sea, these tasty bivalve mollusks can be found on sea rocks all around Eorzea, but it is said the plumpest, most succulent grow in the nutrient-rich waters of the Rothlyt Sound.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4882.name: Navigator's dagger
4882.col_2: These thin, long saltwater fish will oft jump out of the water and glide for yalms across the surface, using their pectoral fins as ersatz wings.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4883.name: angelfish
4883.col_2: A small colorful fish native to the warmer waters of the seas near Meracydia. Since the Calamity, more and more have been caught off Eorzea's southern coastline.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4884.name: razor clam
4884.col_2: A long bivalve mollusk most commonly found buried in the beaches of islands situated in the Rhotano Sea. They are known to leap out of their burrows when surprised or agitated.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4885.name: blue octopus
4885.col_2: The somber blue tone of its skin does not make this variety of octopus any more docile than its crimson cousins. It is a crafty hunter who lurks in the shadows, snatching unwary prey and strangling it with its powerful eight arms before shredding it with its razor-sharp beak.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4886.name: blowfish
4886.col_2: A saltwater fish that, when provoked, blows up to three times its normal size to intimidate the would-be attacker. It is also known to have an organ which contains a potent silencing poison.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4887.name: saber sardine
4887.col_2: This tiny saltwater fish travels in giant schools through the Indigo Deep searching for food. Its razor-like fins have been known to cut straight through the strongest of fishing nets.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4888.name: ogre barracuda
4888.col_2: A large saltwater wavekin that roams the Rhotano Sea in small schools, preying on smaller fish such as anchovies or sardines.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4889.name: monkfish
4889.col_2: This deep-sea-dwelling wavekin attracts its prey with a tiny glowing appendage protruding forth from its disfigured head, and then swallows the poor victim whole with its unnaturally large mouth.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4890.name: sea bo
4890.col_2: When swimming upright, this strange sea creature closely resembles a riding chocobo, hence the name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4891.name: Bianaq bream
4891.col_2: A cherry-colored saltwater fish found in abundance in all of Eorzea's five seas, though it is said those caught near Bianaq are the largest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4892.name: black sole
4892.col_2: A flat bottom-feeder commonly found in the frigid waters of the Bloodbrine Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4893.name: hammerhead shark
4893.col_2: A ravenous shark with a hammer-shaped head it uses to quickly detect its prey. This wavekin is most commonly found living in small schools in the Strait of Merlthor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4894.name: sea pickle
4894.col_2: A blue, spiny, sluglike creature found in the shallows off of Vylbrand, and considered a delicacy by Sea Wolves.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4895.name: Indigo herring
4895.col_2: This blue-backed, white-bellied saltwater fish native to the Indigo Deep is known to migrate in large schools from north to south in the winter, and back again in the summer.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4896.name: ash tuna
4896.col_2: A large saltwater fish known to migrate between the Sea of Jade and the Sea of Ash. In recent years, overfishing by boats from the Far East has led to a significant drop in their numbers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4897.name: leafy seadragon
4897.col_2: Though once found all across the five seas, seadragon numbers are now but a mere fraction of what they once were, due in part to Ishgardian culling parties.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4898.name: fullmoon sardine
4898.col_2: A tiny saltwater fish native to the waters of Vylbrand. Unlike other wavekin, they feed only at night, their activity increasing as Menphina waxes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4899.name: Haraldr haddock
4899.col_2: A tasty saltwater fish indigenous to the cold waters of the Bloodbrine Sea. Its name comes from a legendary northern king who it was said would only eat the fatty flesh of this wavekin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4900.name: whitelip oyster
4900.col_2: A bivalve mollusk found on the cliffs and rocks lining the Rhotano Sea. On rare occasions, sand will become trapped inside the shell and gradually form into a pearl.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4901.name: lavender remora
4901.col_2: A violet-hued fish found in the warmer waters of Eorzea's southern seas.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4902.name: balloonfish
4902.col_2: A saltwater fish covered in scores of sharp spines, discouraging would-be predators from dining on this otherwise defenseless fry.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4903.name: silver shark
4903.col_2: A large, spindle-shaped shark commonly found in the Sea of Ash and known to attack without provocation.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4904.name: wahoo
4904.col_2: A razor-fanged saltwater fish known to migrate throughout the warm waters of the Sea of Ash, following the schools of shrimp on which it feeds.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4905.name: raincaller
4905.col_2: A deep-blue freshwater fish native to the lakes and swamps of the Black Shroud. They can be seen sticking their heads out of the water whenever it rains, leading people to believe it is the fish summoning the storm. However, naturalists have surmised that the fish are simply rising to the surface in search of food, mistaking the drops of water for insects.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4906.name: nautilus
4906.col_2: A giant cephalopod characterized by its spectacular whorling shell. Commonly found in the nutrient-rich Bay of Dha'yuz, the wavekin are thought by sailors and pirates to be the heralds of the Navigator, Llymlaen, and their shells are often carved into celebratory chalices.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4907.name: pike eel
4907.col_2: When stretched straight from head to tail, the longest of saltwater pike eels can measure more than a full yalm in length.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4908.name: mummer wrasse
4908.col_2: This saltwater fish's name comes from the odd lump on its head, thought to resemble a mummer's motley cap.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4909.name: plaice
4909.col_2: A bottom-feeding flatfish, the plaice is most commonly found blending into the sands covering the sea floor near the Isles of Umbra.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4910.name: sea devil
4910.col_2: Legends tell of giant sea devils emerging from the sea to wrap their many arms around ships and drag them to the abyss. This seems impossible today, as the largest catches in recent memory are little more than a yalm across.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4911.name: rock lobster
4911.col_2: A large crimson crustacean commonly found hiding in the rocks off the shores of islands dotting the Rhotano Sea. The rich, flavorful tails are regarded as a delicacy across Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4912.name: goosefish
4912.col_2: A large-mouthed saltwater glutton, thought to feed on most anything, from smaller fish, to seaweed, to the flesh of drowned sailors.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4913.name: little Thalaos
4913.col_2: Despite the modifier, the little Thalaos is anything but small; though compared to the Thalaos of legend, even the largest of sea serpents would be deemed “little.” Normally only found far offshore in the Indigo Deep, this rare wavekin can sometimes be found swimming near the eastern cliffs of La Noscea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4914.name: shall shell
4914.col_2: This enormous bivalve mollusk is easily recognizable by the unique wave pattern found on its outer shell.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4915.name: mahi-mahi
4915.col_2: This deep-sea predator is not only massive, but deceptively fast. Some sailors swear that a mahi-mahi can make the journey from Meracydia to the Cieldalaes in less than a fortnight, though knowing most sailors, that claim may be slightly exaggerated.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4916.name: halibut
4916.col_2: While similar to the sole or plaice in appearance and behavior, the halibut is much larger than both, and can feed a Lalafellin family of five for several turns of the sun.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4917.name: Mazlaya marlin
4917.col_2: A large saltwater fish found in the warm waters south of the Sea of Ash and known for its remarkable swimming speed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4918.name: coelacanth
4918.col_2: An ancient species of saltwater fish which appears to have flourished in times well before the Allagans built their empire.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4919.name: giant squid
4919.col_2: This rarely seen giant cephalopod makes an appearance in ancient Sea Wolf mythology as the creature on which the legendary whale Bismarck fed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4920.name: gigant octopus
4920.col_2: A legendary cephalopod feared by sailors young and old. Tales of these cyclopean creatures tearing up ships and dragging them down to the abyss can still be heard in alehouses and inns across Hydaelyn.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4921.name: sunfish
4921.col_2: Legends say this giant saltwater fish will help those stranded in the water by allowing them to ride it back to shore.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4922.name: dinichthys
4922.col_2: A legendary saltwater fish covered in thick armor and said to have once been worshipped by the Sahagin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4923.name: megalodon
4923.col_2: A legendary shark with a mouth so big and an appetite so large, it is said it can swallow an adult Roegadyn whole.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4924.name: titanic sawfish
4924.col_2: Legends say that this gargantuan saltwater fish once ripped a hundred-man galleon in two with its saw-like head.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

4925.name: crayfish
4925.col_2: A brown-carapaced freshwater crustacean commonly found in the rivers and lakes of Aldenard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4926.name: chub
4926.col_2: A common freshwater fish found in rivers across Eorzea. Prefers the slow-moving waters found near a river's mouth to the rapids found upstream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4927.name: striped goby
4927.col_2: A brightly striped freshwater fish native to the rivers and lakes of the Coerthas and Mor Dhona regions.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4928.name: dwarf catfish
4928.col_2: An undersized variety of catfish found in still, swampy waters across Aldenard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4929.name: bone crayfish
4929.col_2: A white-carapaced freshwater crustacean commonly found living in caves or deep lakes where sunlight is absent.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4930.name: princess trout
4930.col_2: Unlike other freshwater trout which make their habitat in swift-flowing rivers, the silver princess trout prefers the relative seclusion of inland lakes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4931.name: dusk goby
4931.col_2: A hardy species, the dusk goby can survive not only in freshwater, but also the mouths of rivers, where the tides can bring saltwater malms inland.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4932.name: pipira
4932.col_2: A fierce freshwater fish most commonly found in Gridania's Jadeite Flood and Black Tea Brook.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4933.name: crimson crayfish
4933.col_2: A crimson-carapaced freshwater crustacean commonly found in the streams and lakes of Vylbrand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4934.name: gudgeon
4934.col_2: Each night, this freshwater fish will use its fins to dig a shallow burrow in river or lake beds, where it will sleep, relatively safe from predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4935.name: brass loach
4935.col_2: This long, thin, brass-colored freshwater fish is most commonly found in the Yafaem Saltmoor and surrounding rivers and lakes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4936.name: maiden carp
4936.col_2: Large schools of these dark silver fish can be found in the White Maiden and her tributaries.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4937.name: Abalathian smelt
4937.col_2: A tiny freshwater fish native to the lakes and rivers fed by runoff from Abalathia's Spine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4938.name: blindfish
4938.col_2: Commonly found in the sea caves and grottoes of Vylbrand, the eyes of this freshwater fish regressed long ago, earning the specimen its name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4939.name: mudskipper
4939.col_2: An amphibious fish which can survive for bells out of water as long as its skin remains moist. When on land, the mudskipper uses its pectoral fins to “wander” about in search of shelter. Because of this trait, the fish is sometimes associated with the god Oschon.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4940.name: rainbow trout
4940.col_2: Found in the crystal-clear rivers and lakes of Mor Dhona and Coerthas, this fish's scales reflect all seven colors of the rainbow, making it difficult to locate in the water.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4941.name: river crab
4941.col_2: A tiny freshwater crustacean commonly found in rivers throughout Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4942.name: Ala Mhigan fighting fish
4942.col_2: A beautiful blue freshwater fish known for its violent disposition.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4943.name: faerie bass
4943.col_2: A common freshwater fish found in rivers and lakes in almost every corner of Eorzea. A staple for many of the realm's smallfolk.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4944.name: acorn snail
4944.col_2: Believed to have hitched a ride on the hull of a trade ship, the acorn snail is an invasive species originally from the New World, far to the west. As it has few natural predators in Eorzea, its numbers have exploded in recent years.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4945.name: dark sleeper
4945.col_2: A small freshwater fish originally from the eastern continent of Othard. It is said that the first dark sleeper was introduced to Eorzea by an exiled Lalafellin prince who wished to once again experience the luxuries of his homeland.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4946.name: La Noscean perch
4946.col_2: A fair-sized freshwater fish found distributed evenly throughout the lakes and rivers of lower Vylbrand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4947.name: moat carp
4947.col_2: This freshwater fish is found in lakes and marshes throughout the Black Shroud...but rarely in moats.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4948.name: copperfish
4948.col_2: The copperfish's dull orange scales─a hue rare in freshwater wavekin─make this species popular amongst Ul'dahn nobles, who apparently prefer even their fish to be the color of their coin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4949.name: bluebell salmon
4949.col_2: Hatched far up inland rivers, bluebell salmon will travel all the way downstream to the Indigo Deep where they will spend the majority of their adulthood. Then, however, when it comes time to spawn, they will return back upstream to the place of their birth.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4950.name: mudcrab
4950.col_2: As its name implies, the mudcrab spends most of its life in the muddy freshwater shallows of swamps and moors.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4951.name: tricolored carp
4951.col_2: Patches of gold, silver, and bronze cover this medium-sized freshwater fish's body, making it a favorite choice for the private garden pools of Ul'dahn nobles.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4952.name: eunuch crayfish
4952.col_2: The grip of this tiny freshwater crustacean's claw is so strong, it has been the end of many a Lalafell's fingers...and more. Take care when handling.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4953.name: jade eel
4953.col_2: Similar to salmon, this green-grey freshwater eel lives the majority of its life in the salty waters of the sea, returning to inland rivers to only spawn and die.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4954.name: pond mussel
4954.col_2: This bivalve freshwater mollusk with a tear-shaped shell can be found either clinging to the side of submerged boulders or simply lying half-buried in the mud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4955.name: warmwater trout
4955.col_2: This freshwater fish was once found only in the waters heated by the flows of lava coursing beneath the mighty volcano O'Ghomoro. After the Calamity, however, fishers began finding the wavekin in other warm locations such as Thanalan.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4956.name: glass perch
4956.col_2: With an almost completely transparent body, this variety of freshwater perch is coveted by naturalists wishing to study the inner workings of organs on a living specimen.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4957.name: four-eyed fish
4957.col_2: Four-eyed fish do not actually have four eyes, but two eyes that are divided into an upper and lower portion that allow the wavekin to see both above and below the water at the same time.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4958.name: black eel
4958.col_2: Black eels reach maturity in the Sea of Jade, at which point they return back up the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers to spawn.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4959.name: dark bass
4959.col_2: This freshwater fish, known for its voracious appetite, is originally native to the southern continent of Meracydia.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4960.name: aegis shrimp
4960.col_2: Whereas other shrimp shed their old exoskeletons each summer in favor of new ones, the aegis shrimp simply adds a new layer every year until the shell is so hard, not even a blow from a trained pugilist can break through it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4961.name: five-ilm pleco
4961.col_2: This freshwater fish commonly found in the rivers of the Black Shroud will often grow no larger than a mere five ilms.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4962.name: climbing perch
4962.col_2: Though not amphibious like the mudskipper, the climbing perch will jump from Black Shroud rivers onto low-lying tree branches in order to catch flies and beetles.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4963.name: shadow catfish
4963.col_2: A large whiskered fish that can be found in the calm marshes of the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4964.name: black ghost
4964.col_2: Native to the rivers and lakes of the Black Shroud, this freshwater fish uses electric receptors on its body to locate food.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4965.name: lamprey
4965.col_2: A long, ugly freshwater eel found in nearly every river and lake in Eorzea. Its toothy grin is enough to frighten children across the realm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4966.name: plaguefish
4966.col_2: This variety of freshwater fish has the queer habit of wearing the skulls of small drowned animals, though it is not known exactly why.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4967.name: Yugr'am salmon
4967.col_2: This freshwater fish matures in the salty waters of the Bloodbrine Sea, only to return up the Yugr'am River where it was born to spawn.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4968.name: spotted pleco
4968.col_2: Tiny white spots cover the body of this rare freshwater fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4969.name: ropefish
4969.col_2: As it has the tendency to coil up while inactive, this variety of freshwater eel is oft mistaken for lost boat rigging.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4970.name: Grip killifish
4970.col_2: A rare type of fish oft found in stagnant waters such as the isolated pools which collect in the basin of Empty Heart on the western finger of the Gods' Grip.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4971.name: bone cleaner
4971.col_2: A freshwater snail that survives solely on the carrion of animals that get caught and perish in the sucking mud of swamps and marshes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4972.name: root skipper
4972.col_2: A small fish that is found only in Rootslake in the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4973.name: bonytongue
4973.col_2: A single flat tooth on the bottom of this freshwater species' mouth gives the bonytongue its name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4974.name: mitten crab
4974.col_2: The claws of this freshwater crustacean are covered in myriad tiny bristles which provide the illusion that the crab is wearing mittens.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4975.name: monke onke
4975.col_2: A giant freshwater fish found in the tepid rivers and lakes of the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4976.name: seema
4976.col_2: The flesh of this freshwater trout native to central and northern Eorzea is a bright pink, leading to the common nickname, “cherry trout.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4977.name: sandfish
4977.col_2: An amphibious fish capable of breathing on land. This trait has allowed it to adapt to life in the deserts of Thanalan.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4978.name: silverfish
4978.col_2: As are copperfish and goldfish, freshwater silverfish are prized amongst well-to-do Ul'dahns, and often kept as pets.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4979.name: clown loach
4979.col_2: Bright patterns, similar to a clown's motley, cover this small freshwater fish from head to tail.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4980.name: armored pleco
4980.col_2: The rock-hard scales of the armored pleco are thought to protect the wavekin from injury when being dashed about swift-water rapids.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4981.name: giant bass
4981.col_2: Significantly larger than a dark bass, landing a giant bass can prove quite the challenge for even the most seasoned angler.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4982.name: Velodyna carp
4982.col_2: This scarlet cousin to the maiden carp can most commonly be found in the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4983.name: spotted puffer
4983.col_2: A cousin of the sea-dwelling balloonfish, spotted puffers are unique in that they can survive in the brackish waters of deltas and river mouths.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4984.name: golden loach
4984.col_2: Truly a prize, this bright-gold fish, though rare, can be found in rivers and lakes across Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4985.name: trader eel
4985.col_2: This freshwater eel native to the rivers and lakes of Thanalan will often display the unique trait of swapping its mate with other nearby eels when spawning.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4986.name: crimson trout
4986.col_2: A red-scaled trout commonly found in the rivers originating on Abalathia's Spine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4987.name: discus
4987.col_2: A colorful freshwater fish that can only survive in rivers located in more temperate climes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4988.name: Bronze Lake trout
4988.col_2: A species of trout native to Vylbrand's Bronze Lake.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

4989.name: ignus snail
4989.col_2: The fiery red shells of this freshwater snail are prized by the Amalj'aa, and are useful when bartering with the beast tribe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4990.name: loyal pleco
4990.col_2: This variety of striped freshwater fish earns its name from its tendency to gather by the legs of any man or beast who enters its habitat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4991.name: thunderbolt sculpin
4991.col_2: A rare freshwater fish decorated with a thunderbolt-like pattern down its back.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4992.name: fall jumper
4992.col_2: Fall jumpers are born with an inherent tendency to swim against the current. When they arrive at a falls, this leaves them with no option but to leap out of the water in an attempt to continue upstream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4993.name: knifefish
4993.col_2: The freshwater knifefish is named such due to its resemblance to a flat blade.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4994.name: oakroot
4994.col_2: A giant freshwater fish found in inland lakes and rivers. Its name is derived from its resemblance to a knotty oaken root.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4995.name: common sculpin
4995.col_2: This freshwater fish has highly developed fins and spines which not only protect the wavekin, but serve as weapons for hunting its prey.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4996.name: southern pike
4996.col_2: Though classified as a freshwater fish native to the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers, this particular wavekin can survive in the brackish delta where the waterways spill into the Sea of Jade.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4997.name: northern pike
4997.col_2: Though classified as a freshwater fish native to the White Maiden, this particular wavekin can survive in the brackish waters where the Maiden meets the Strait of Merlthor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

4998.name: kobold puffer
4998.col_2: Similar to the spotted puffer, the kobold puffer can also survive in the brackish waters of deltas and river mouths. Its spots, however, are replaced with a hideous coat of bristly spines which give it the appearance of a bedraggled kobold.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

4999.name: archerfish
4999.col_2: When feeding, the archerfish will lift its head ever so slightly above a lake's or river's surface and spit a stream of water up to a yalm to strike flies from low-lying branches into the water with remarkable accuracy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5000.name: goblin perch
5000.col_2: The goblins claim that they brought this variety of perch back from their years-long pilgrimage into Othard and Ilsabard...because it tasted so divine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5001.name: Agelyss carp
5001.col_2: A rare species of carp native to the Agelyss River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5002.name: assassin betta
5002.col_2: A violent species of freshwater fish from central Abalathia's Spine that will attack other assassin betta if they draw too near while feeding.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

5003.name: sludgeskipper
5003.col_2: Similar to its cousin the mudskipper, the sludgeskipper can also survive outside water for several bells. The sludgeskipper, however, is at home in highly polluted pools where other creatures would likely perish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

5004.name: boltfish
5004.col_2: This freshwater anomaly possesses high concentrations of lightning-aspected aetherial energy which can be used to inflict serious injury on any foolish enough to provoke the fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5005.name: garpike
5005.col_2: A hard-scaled freshwater fish native to southern Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5006.name: Ilsabardian bass
5006.col_2: Unlike its Eorzean cousins, the Ilsabardian bass is mean-tempered and quick to bite, attacking other species sharing the same lake until there are none left but its own.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5007.name: Paglth'an discus
5007.col_2: A brightly colored freshwater fish native to the warm waters in and around the Amalj'aa territory of Paglth'an.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5008.name: boxing pleco
5008.col_2: The largest pleco known to naturalists, this variety is known for violently flailing its fins at any unfortunate creature that happens to swim by.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5009.name: kissing trout
5009.col_2: Native to the freshwater rivers of Abalathia's Spine, the kissing trout is famous for its mating “dance” in which a male and female will face each other for several moments before proceeding to couple.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5010.name: angry pike
5010.col_2: While all species of freshwater pike are known to be violent, this particular variety has been recorded actually biting the ankles of wading fishers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5011.name: goldfish
5011.col_2: The brilliant luster of this freshwater fish native to the Far East has made it a popular addition to the aquariums and garden ponds of Ul'dahn patricians.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5012.name: vampire lampern
5012.col_2: Just as its name implies, the vampire lampern is indeed a sucker of blood, using its multiple rows of teeth to latch onto its prey, whether it be sea or land creature, and bore a hole from which to drink.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5013.name: wandering sculpin
5013.col_2: Legend states that this particular variety of sculpin is a favorite of Oschon, the Wanderer, and that the god will oft dine on this fish while on His journeys through the realm of man.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5014.name: cave cherax
5014.col_2: It is said that not even a fishing line made from adamantite wire can withstand the cutting force of this legendary giant crustacean's claws.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5015.name: coeurlfish
5015.col_2: Two front teeth of this freshwater fish are exceptionally long and therefore protrude from the mouth, giving them the appearance of coeurl fangs.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5016.name: giant donko
5016.col_2: A giant freshwater fish native to the rivers and swamps of La Noscea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5017.name: sundisc
5017.col_2: This freshwater fish has a bright-yellow sun-like pattern across its body, giving rise to the name “sundisc.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5018.name: alligator garfish
5018.col_2: A legendary freshwater fish said to have a head not unlike that of an alligator, complete with rows of razor-sharp teeth.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5019.name: wootz knifefish
5019.col_2: It is believed that after living in waters tainted with wootz ore for so long, this knifefish absorbed so much of the mineral that it began showing in its scales.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5020.name: giant catfish
5020.col_2: A giant freshwater fish found throughout Aldenard and known for the decidedly feline whiskers which it uses to detect the movement of prey.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5021.name: cadaver carp
5021.col_2: Neither dead nor necrophagous, the cadaver carp is called such because of where it chooses to live─some of the most tainted, noisome, and foul waters in all of Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5022.name: mushroom crab
5022.col_2: This amazing crab will rub its shell up against funguars to collect spores, which it will then grow on its back. Once the sporelings begin to sprout, the crab will use its claws to slice off the mushrooms and eat them.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5023.name: judgment staff
5023.col_2: Named after the primal Ramuh's signature weapon, this strange freshwater fish will only feed when the weather is rainy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5024.name: poxpike
5024.col_2: The rock-hard scales of this variety of freshwater garpike are spattered with scores of unhealthy-looking spots.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5025.name: emperor fish
5025.col_2: This giant freshwater fish lives out its adulthood feeding in the Indigo Deep before returning all the way back up to the head of the White Maiden to spawn.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5026.name: bowfin
5026.col_2: Record of the bowfin being caught in the Black Shroud dates back to the time of the first Elezen settlers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5027.name: heliobatis
5027.col_2: A flat freshwater bottom-feeder found predominantly in marshes and swamps, where it can hide under the blanket of organic detritus collected on the floor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5028.name: takitaro
5028.col_2: A legendary giant freshwater fish indigenous to the lands of the Far East. The takitaro found in Eorzea are thought to be the offspring of a specimen presented as a gift to an eccentric sultan who loosed the fish into a cenote when it grew too large to keep in the royal aquariums.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5029.name: pirarucu
5029.col_2: A legendary giant freshwater fish rumored to live in the bottomless swamps hidden deep within the unexplored regions of the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5030.name: morinabaligi
5030.col_2: A giant freshwater fish so shrouded in mystery that naught is known of it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5031.name: jungle catfish
5031.col_2: It is rumored that a jungle catfish can grow to become as large as an aurochs, and while there are sightings aplenty of these massive specimens, one that large has yet to be caught.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5032.name: sand bream
5032.col_2: A tiny sand-dwelling fish which can spend its whole life out of the water.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5033.name: desert catfish
5033.col_2: A large variety of air-breathing catfish. Its near-frictionless scales allow it to “swim” through the desert as a normal fish would through the water.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5034.name: dustfish
5034.col_2: When threatened, this sand-dwelling fish will beat the ground with its fins, kicking up a cloud of dust and allowing it the opportunity to escape unscathed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5035.name: storm rider
5035.col_2: These sand-dwelling fish will skip across the desert unless they are fortunate enough to stumble across a sandstorm, in which case they will spread their fins and ride the storm great distances.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

5036.name: antlion slug
5036.col_2: This sand-dwelling slug is able to maintain its mucous coating by absorbing the moisture from prey it catches at the bottom of conical pits not unlike the ones antlions are known to dig.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5037.name: dune manta
5037.col_2: Remarkably smooth skin allows the dune manta to glide through desert sand as if it were the sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5038.name: cloud jellyfish
5038.col_2: Cloud jellyfish aimlessly drift about the Sea of Clouds, tentacles spread out below them, searching for the small birds on which they feed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

5039.name: skyfish
5039.col_2: One of the more common creatures found living on the thermal currents above the Sea of Clouds, from a distance, the skyfish appears to be no more than a simple rod outfitted with three sets of transparent wings.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5040.name: cloud cutter
5040.col_2: The swiftest inhabitants of the Sea of Clouds, cloud cutters will fly straight in a single direction for malms before quickly turning at some unthinkable angle and darting off in another direction.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5041.name: blind manta
5041.col_2: The blind manta is thought to navigate the Sea of Clouds in a manner similar to how bats keep their bearings─using sound and echoes to determine the location of cliff faces and other creatures.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5042.name: rift sailor
5042.col_2: The rift sailor uses the light elastic webbing between its wings to catch the roiling winds of the Sea of Clouds and glide across the rifts.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

5043.name: Sagolii monkfish
5043.col_2: When hunting, the Sagolii monkfish uses a method similar to its sea-bound cousin─attracting potential prey to its location with a glowing appendage situated directly above its gaping maw.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5044.name: saucerfish
5044.col_2: Lacking feet or wings to propel itself from the ground, only death awaits the saucerfish that is foolish enough to leave the Sea of Clouds.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5045.name: caravan eel
5045.col_2: After maturing in the Grand Wake, caravan eels will form long lines in the sand and make their way back to the Sagolii Desert to spawn and die.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

5046.name: rhamphorhynchus
5046.col_2: Its massive lance-shaped nose makes this legendary denizen of the Sea of Clouds a formidable nuisance for airships passing through the area.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

5047.name: tricorn
5047.col_2: A legendary amphibian with a boomerang-like head said to be powerful enough to split a harpoon in two.

5048.name: young Indigo herring
5048.col_2: A large fish native to the Indigo Deep. When packed in salt, it can be preserved for up to a year.

5049.name: Navigator's ear
5049.col_2: This medium-sized oyster is high in nutrients, making it optimal for use in medicines and rations.

5050.name: Allagan snail
5050.col_2: A giant snail believed to have been bred for consumption during the reign of the Great Allagan Empire.

5051.name: tree toad
5051.col_2: A giant green toad found in nearly all of the lakes and swamps of Aldenard.

5052.name: box turtle
5052.col_2: A common, thick-shelled turtle found in wetlands throughout Eorzea.

5053.name: nether newt
5053.col_2: An amphibious type of scalekin found in the wetlands of Vylbrand. Its body is covered with colorful markings which some of Limsa Lominsa's more superstitious folk believe are burns the creature received when crawling its way through each of the seven hells before arriving on the face of Hydaelyn.

5054.name: dart frog
5054.col_2: This tiny frog found in the swamps and lakes of the Black Shroud secretes a powerful poison known to induce paralysis.

5055.name: lava toad
5055.col_2: This giant red toad, native to the swamps of Vylbrand but now found throughout Aldenard, earns its name from the red firerock which once spewed forth from the now-dormant volcano, O'Ghomoro.

5885.name: Oschon's finger charm

6001.name: chocobo whistle
6001.col_2: A small hand-carved whistle that emits a unique, high-pitched tone discernible only by a chocobo trained from birth to recognize and respond to the sound. Use to summon your personal chocobo.

6002.name: goobbue horn
6002.col_2: This polished horn emits a deep, bellowing tone that creates subtle vibrations in the land that carry for malms. While undetectable by most, goobbues can sense these mini tremblors which they often mistake for mating calls.

6003.name: cherry bomb
6003.col_2: Summons a miniature recreation of a voidsent bomb, created via the thaumaturgical rendering of umbrally charged aetherial energy. Guaranteed never to self-destruct, or your gil back.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the cherry bomb minion.

6004.name: mammet #001

6005.name: wayward hatchling

6006.name: legacy chocobo whistle
6006.col_2: A small hand-carved whistle that emits a unique, high-pitched tone discernible only by a chocobo trained from birth to recognize and respond to the sound. Use to summon your legacy chocobo.

6007.name: coeurl bell

6008.name: armor identification key

6009.name: voidal resonator
6009.col_2: A metal tuning fork that, when struck, emits a low tone which opens a temporary rift in the void, allowing your personal ahriman─and your personal ahriman only─to pass through to this plane.
