19901.name: bottle of enchanted koppranickel ink
19901.col_2: Ink fortified with koppranickel sand to improve aetherial conductivity.

19902.name: bottle of enchanted durium ink
19902.col_2: Ink fortified with durium sand to improve aetherial conductivity.

19903.name: bottle of enchanted palladium ink
19903.col_2: Ink fortified with palladium sand to improve aetherial conductivity.

19904.name: bottle of growth formula eta
19904.col_2: This alchemically formulated potation accelerates the growth of foliage.

19905.name: bottle of growth formula theta
19905.col_2: This alchemically formulated potation accelerates the growth of foliage.

19906.name: lump of beetle glue
19906.col_2: An adhesive substance created by grinding down the chitinous carapaces of beetles and mixing it with heated pine resin.

19907.name: Ala Mhigan salt crystal
19907.col_2: These pinkish crystals grow naturally on the shores of Loch Seld.

19908.name: pot of pine resin
19908.col_2: A sticky substance secreted by pine trees when their limbs are cut.

19909.name: pot of persimmon tannin
19909.col_2: A translucent liquid extracted from persimmon wood by steeping it in hot water. Used in the tanning of raw animal hides.

19910.name: pinch of Gyr Abanian alumen
19910.col_2: A brownish variety of the mineral used by leatherworkers to tan animal hides. It is only found in the mountains of Eastern Aldenard.

19911.name: bunch of Yanxian parsley
19911.col_2: This Far Eastern perennial has a biting aroma that even many Othardians find off-putting.

19912.name: stalk of alyssum
19912.col_2: This annual is coveted by perfumers for its honey-sweet aroma.

19913.name: sprig of Nagxian cudweed
19913.col_2: Though recognized as a weed, this winter annual is edible and will oft be harvested in the late months for use in various Doman and Hingan dishes.

19914.name: sprig of chickweed
19914.col_2: Though recognized as a weed, this winter annual is edible and will oft be harvested in the late months for use in various Doman and Hingan dishes.

19915.name: sprig of nipplewort
19915.col_2: Named for the protruding buds from which its bright-yellow flowers bloom, nipplewort is a common winter annual whose leaves are gathered for use in Othardian cuisine.

19916.name: basket of windtea leaves
19916.col_2: When steeped in boiling water, the leaves of this rare perennial change color, turning a bright bluish green.

19917.name: sprig of holy basil
19917.col_2: A herb with an aroma so heavenly, it will cleanse both your soul and your palate of ill flavors (or so say merchants who would see you buy their stock).

19918.name: sprig of hallowed basil
19918.col_2: A herb with an aroma so heavenly, the gods themselves must have blessed it (or so say merchants who would see you buy their stock).

19919.name: muud suud horn
19919.col_2: The curved horn of a muud suud.

19920.name: gazelle horn
19920.col_2: The twisted horn of a gazelle.

19921.name: dzo horn
19921.col_2: The massive ebon horn of a steppe dzo.

19922.name: handful of moth scales
19922.col_2: The powdery scales of a giant moth's wing.

19923.name: bombfish spine
19923.col_2: A single adult bombfish can have as many as a thousand of these lightweight-yet-sturdy spines jutting from its body.

19924.name: rhino beetle carapace
19924.col_2: The thick chitinous head of a rhino beetle, complete with eyes, antennae, and mandibles.

19930.name: beech log
19930.col_2: A rough-cut log of beech timber.

19931.name: larch log
19931.col_2: A rough-cut log of larch timber.

19932.name: persimmon log
19932.col_2: A rough-cut log of persimmon timber.

19933.name: zelkova log
19933.col_2: A rough-cut log of zelkova timber.

19934.name: torreya log
19934.col_2: A rough-cut log of torreya timber.

19935.name: pot of scarlet urushi
19935.col_2: This glossy red coating, made from the sap of the lacquer tree, is used to both color and preserve wooden crafts.

19936.name: beech branch
19936.col_2: The thick branch of a beech tree.

19937.name: torreya branch
19937.col_2: The thick branch of a torreya tree.

19938.name: koppranickel nugget
19938.col_2: A small nugget of impure koppranickel.

19939.name: high steel nugget
19939.col_2: A small nugget of impure high steel.

19941.name: high steel ingot
19941.col_2: An ingot of smelted high steel.

19942.name: durium nugget
19942.col_2: A small nugget of impure durium.

19943.name: oroshigane ingot
19943.col_2: An ingot of Doman iron, smelted using Far Eastern techniques.

19945.name: tama-hagane ingot
19945.col_2: An ingot of Doman steel, smelted using Far Eastern techniques.

19946.name: palladium nugget
19946.col_2: A small nugget of impure palladium.

19950.name: handful of koppranickel sand
19950.col_2: Amber-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of koppranickel.

19951.name: chunk of koppranickel ore
19951.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal koppranickel.

19952.name: handful of durium sand
19952.col_2: Jade-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of durium.

19953.name: chunk of Doman iron ore
19953.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal Doman iron (also known as mochi iron for its resemblance to the Far Eastern rice cakes).

19954.name: chunk of durium ore
19954.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal durium.

19955.name: handful of Doman iron sand
19955.col_2: Metallic sand consisting of tiny grains of Doman iron.

19956.name: handful of palladium sand
19956.col_2: Silver-colored sand consisting of tiny grains of palladium.

19957.name: chunk of molybdenum ore
19957.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal molybdenum.

19958.name: chunk of palladium ore
19958.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal palladium.

19959.name: chunk of chromite ore
19959.col_2: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the metal chromium.

19960.name: pinch of Domacoat
19960.col_2: Not to be outdone by their Near Eastern counterparts who perfected the aurum regis-hardening agent, Raziqcoat, several Far Eastern alchemists have joined together to create Domacoat─a substance capable of hardening palladium.

19961.name: pinch of bone charcoal
19961.col_2: Not actually created from bones, this hot-burning fuel is the result of baking coal in an airless furnace at an extremely high temperature.

19966.name: piece of imperial jade
19966.col_2: Also known as “true jade,” this milky green stone is coveted by the Far Eastern elite.

19968.name: raw triphane
19968.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be triphane.

19969.name: raw kyanite
19969.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be kyanite.

19970.name: raw star spinel
19970.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be star spinel.

19971.name: raw azurite
19971.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be azurite.

19972.name: piece of raw imperial jade
19972.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be imperial jade.

19973.name: raw rhodonite
19973.col_2: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be rhodonite.

19974.name: bolt of bloodhempen cloth
19974.col_2: Several yalms of undyed, bright-red bloodhempen cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.

19975.name: spindle of bloodhempen yarn
19975.col_2: Coarse yarn spun from bloodhemp fiber.

19976.name: tuft of bloodhemp
19976.col_2: A common grass found growing throughout Othard. From its stalks, bloodhempen yarn is created.

19977.name: bolt of ruby cotton cloth
19977.col_2: Several yalms of undyed ruby cotton cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.

19978.name: spindle of ruby cotton yarn
19978.col_2: Light yarn spun from ruby cotton.

19979.name: ruby cotton boll
19979.col_2: The fibrous flower of a rare cotton plant that only grows <hex:021A020203>under<hex:021A020103> the Ruby Sea. As such, Eorzean scholars insist that the flora is in no way related to normal cotton, and is instead a unique variety of sea kelp.

19980.name: bolt of kudzu cloth
19980.col_2: Several yalms of undyed kudzu cloth wrapped around a short wooden distaff.

19981.name: spindle of kudzu thread
19981.col_2: Thick, fibrous yarn spun from kudzu vines.

19982.name: kudzu vine
19982.col_2: If allowed to grow unchecked, a single kudzu plant can cover an acre of forest in less than a single summer, blocking the sun from the plants it envelops. A large swath of the outer Black Shroud currently finds itself being slowly suffocated by the invasive weed.

19983.name: bolt of steppe serge
19983.col_2: Several yalms of undyed steppe serge wrapped around a short wooden distaff.

19984.name: spindle of worsted yarn
19984.col_2: Soft, water-absorbent yarn spun from multiple varieties of hair sheared from beastkin of the Azim Steppe.

19985.name: halgai mane
19985.col_2: The regal mane of a halgai.

19986.name: length of manzasiri hair
19986.col_2: The long brown hair of a steppe manzasiri.

19987.name: bolt of twinsilk
19987.col_2: Though exhibiting a similar luster as normal silk, twinsilk is far more durable and resistant to discoloring.

19988.name: spindle of twinthread
19988.col_2: A thin lustrous thread woven from countless silken strands pulled from a rare highland twincoon.

19989.name: twincoon
19989.col_2: A massive cocoon spun by not one, but multiple highland erucas.

19990.name: bolt of rhea cloth
19990.col_2: Cloth woven from the plant rhea. Due to the complexity of the spinning process, there are very few clothcrafters in the world who can produce this weave, making it extremely rare. Most known samples are in the possession of Far Eastern royalty.

19991.name: stalk of rhea
19991.col_2: A variety of ramie better suited to the climes of Far Eastern Othard.

19992.name: bolt of Doman weave
19992.col_2: Hempen cloth woven using age-old methods passed down for countless generations by Doman clothiers.

19993.name: circle of gagana leather
19993.col_2: A large piece of cured gagana skin.

19994.name: circle of gyuki leather
19994.col_2: A large piece of cured gyuki hide.

19995.name: circle of tiger leather
19995.col_2: A large piece of cured tiger skin.

19996.name: circle of marid leather
19996.col_2: A large piece of cured marid hide.

19997.name: circle of gazelle leather
19997.col_2: A large piece of cured gazelle hide.

19998.name: circle of true griffin leather
19998.col_2: A large piece of cured true griffin hide.

19999.name: gagana skin
19999.col_2: The rough skin of a majestic gagana.

20000.name: gyuki hide
20000.col_2: The smooth hide of a devilish gyuki.

20001.name: tiger skin
20001.col_2: The striped skin of a ferocious tiger.

20002.name: marid hide
20002.col_2: The thick hide of a mammoth marid.

20003.name: gazelle hide
20003.col_2: The bristly hide of a steppe gazelle.

20004.name: true griffin hide
20004.col_2: The downy hide of a true griffin.

20005.name: lump of forbidden wax
20005.col_2: Forbidden in many markets for the nefarious means with which it is extracted, this wax is cherished by leatherworkers for the luster it brings to tanned hides when applied.

20006.name: sack of diatomite
20006.col_2: Geological scholars claim that this sedimentary stone is actually comprised of the shells of thousands upon thousands of tiny sea creatures.

20007.name: slab of slate
20007.col_2: Unlike other sedimentary stone, slate has been compressed under the weight of mountains for so long that it is surprisingly hard, making it ideal for whetstones and grinding stones.

20008.name: slate whetstone
20008.col_2: A whetstone carved from slate. Used for sharpening metal or stone blades.

20009.name: chunk of schorl
20009.col_2: A blackish mineral possibly containing trace amounts of the precious stone tourmaline.

20010.name: chunk of perlite
20010.col_2: A strange, pearlescent volcanic rock that expands tenfold upon heating in a kiln or forge.

20011.name: chunk of almandine
20011.col_2: A garnet-like mineral that, due to its extreme hardness, is used in grinding wheels.

20012.name: chunk of Doman yellow
20012.col_2: A soft, clay-like soil believed to be formed of compacted yellow dust carried on the wind from faraway lands.

20013.name: handful of dusklight aethersand
20013.col_2: The elementally aspected remnants of aetherially reduced matter. This fine sand emits a weak glow indiscernible at gloaming.

20014.name: handful of dawnlight aethersand
20014.col_2: The elementally aspected remnants of aetherially reduced matter. This fine sand emits a weak glow indiscernible at dawn.

20015.name: handful of everbright aethersand
20015.col_2: The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.

20016.name: handful of everborn aethersand
20016.col_2: The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.

20017.name: handful of everdeep aethersand
20017.col_2: The elementally aspected remnants of highly concentrated aetherially reduced mineral matter.

20018.name: liopleurodon
20018.col_2: Though king of the five seas and beyond, scholars classify the liopleurodon with scalekin rather than wavekin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

20019.name: Ala Mhigan ribbon
20019.col_2: A freshwater fish named for its long, ribbon-like fins that it uses to both attract prey and distract predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20020.name: Yanxian barramundi
20020.col_2: This large carnivorous specimen is native to the southeastern reaches of the One River where the waters run slow and deep.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20021.name: seraphim
20021.col_2: The beauty of this small freshwater fish native to Yanxia is oft compared to the angels of ancient eastern scripture.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20022.name: blackfin snake eel
20022.col_2: Like most saltwater eels, the blackfin snake eel of the Ruby Sea is a nocturnal hunter.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20023.name: Tail Mountains minnow
20023.col_2: These tiny fish commonly found in the many shallow tributaries feeding into the upper One River rarely grow beyond a few ilms in length.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20024.name: sweatfish
20024.col_2: Despite their small size, sweatfish prefer the swift rapids of the One River's northern tributaries for the cover it provides them from predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20025.name: rock saltfish
20025.col_2: By no means the most winsome of wavekin, the rock saltfish has adapted to survival in the saline waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20026.name: comet minnow
20026.col_2: Near the bottom of the food chain, swift-swimming comet minnows serve as food for many of the larger fish that swim the waters of the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20027.name: Doman grass carp
20027.col_2: This common variety of freshwater carp is found up and down the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20028.name: samurai fish
20028.col_2: Named after the Hingan warriors whose grace and elegance in battle resemble the means by which this wavekin swims the turbid depths of the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20029.name: golden cichlid
20029.col_2: This bright-yellow fish is native to Gyr Abania and found in both the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers, sometimes as far west as East End.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20030.name: Hak bitterling
20030.col_2: A small-yet-plump fish most commonly found in Hak Khaal, one of the One River's many narrow steppe tributaries.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20031.name: Yat goby
20031.col_2: The Yat goby is an eel-like bottom dweller named after the Azim Steppe tributary in which it is most commonly found.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20032.name: ruby meagre
20032.col_2: Similar to a bass in appearance and flavor, the similarities end there, with this variety of meagre preferring the coastal waters of the Ruby Sea and the Glass Ocean to fresher rivers and lakes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20033.name: greenstream loach
20033.col_2: This distant relative to the carp can be found hunting the waters of the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20034.name: tawny wench shark
20034.col_2: Some say this Ruby Sea shark earned its name from sailors long out of port who, upon seeing the shark's pale skin cresting above the waves, would reminisce of their favorite pleasure boat courtesan.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20035.name: whitehorse
20035.col_2: This queer horse-like wavekin swims upright, using two tiny fins near its head to slowly swim through the waters of extreme salinity it calls home.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20036.name: killifish
20036.col_2: This freshwater specimen of minuscule proportions can be found in almost any river and lake from central to eastern Othard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20037.name: coeurl snake eel
20037.col_2: Scholars are divided as to whether this wavekin native to the Ruby Sea and Glass Ocean is in fact a snake or an eel.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20038.name: Zekki grouper
20038.col_2: Groupers gather in swift currents of the Ruby Sea and the Rasen Kaikyo to feed on the abundant life drawn to the area.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20039.name: saltshield snapper
20039.col_2: This violent scalekin has the jaws of a carpenter's vise. Many a careless fisher has lost a fingertip or three when navigating the snapper-rich waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20040.name: sculptor
20040.col_2: Remarkably similar in appearance to a shark, it is believed this salt lake fish periodically exposes its dorsal fin above the water's surface to frighten land predators such as bears.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20041.name: pearl-eye
20041.col_2: Prehistoric drawings of this salt lake fish have been discovered on cave walls throughout Gyr Abania, suggesting that this particular species has endured at least six umbral eras.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20042.name: Abalathian bitterling
20042.col_2: The Abalathian bitterling's ivory white skin easily distinguishes it from its silver cousins also found in the freshwater rivers and lakes of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20043.name: steelshark
20043.col_2: One of only a few freshwater sharks discovered in Eorzea, the steelshark can primarily be found in the rivers and lakes of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20044.name: Tao bitterling
20044.col_2: Though a cousin to the Hak bitterling, the waters of Tao Khaal have taken the Tao bitterling on a slightly different evolutionary path.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20045.name: idle goby
20045.col_2: This large goby uses its natural black and brown mottling to conceal itself in the sandy bed of the Slow Wash.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20046.name: river barramundi
20046.col_2: Called “akame” or “red eye” in the Far East for the unique color of this freshwater fish's optical organs.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20047.name: mirage chub
20047.col_2: This freshwater fish is known to change the color of its skin come spawning season.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20048.name: harutsuge
20048.col_2: This saltwater fish has a distinct crimson coloring that makes it popular amongst aquarium owners.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20049.name: steelhead trout
20049.col_2: A delicious, fatty freshwater fish native to the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20050.name: heather charr
20050.col_2: A unique variety of freshwater charr found only in the waters near Heather Falls.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20051.name: silken koi
20051.col_2: A plump freshwater wavekin with pearlescent scales and a name that sounds better than the fish tastes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20052.name: yellow prismfish
20052.col_2: The pale yellow glow emitted by this freshwater fish is believed to be caused by unbalanced levels of aspected aether in the wavekin's humours.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20053.name: blue prismfish
20053.col_2: The pale blue glow emitted by this freshwater fish is believed to be caused by unbalanced levels of aspected aether in the wavekin's humours.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20054.name: hanatatsu
20054.col_2: Similar to the sea horse, the hanatatsu swims “standing,” though instead of resembling a beast of burden, this saltwater fish has taken on the appearance of a sprig of coral.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20055.name: broken crab
20055.col_2: A wildly misnamed freshwater crab with a highly durable carapace.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20056.name: Gyr Abanian trout
20056.col_2: This succulent pink-fleshed fish commonly found in the Hathoeva and Velodyna rivers will oft command a high price in local markets.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20057.name: bloodsipper
20057.col_2: This freshwater crustacean is widely found in lakes and marshes across the Three Great Continents.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20058.name: Miounnefish
20058.col_2: This feisty freshwater fish is found throughout the Black Shroud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20059.name: monk betta
20059.col_2: This freshwater betta is native to the lakes and marshes of eastern Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20060.name: electric catfish
20060.col_2: This massive whiskered wavekin can be found lurking in the calm, turbid lakes and marshes of eastern Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20061.name: pagan pirarucu
20061.col_2: Though only ever seen by fishers who spend more time telling tales in taverns than actually fishing, the pagan pirarucu can supposedly be found in the highland lakes and swamps of eastern Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20062.name: temple carp
20062.col_2: A freshwater fish commonly found in the lakes and marshes dotting the eastern end of Abalathia's Spine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20063.name: gilfish
20063.col_2: The Far Eastern gilfish was first introduced to Eorzea by Othardian merchants hoping their platinum sheen would make them attractive to wealthy nobles. Now the freshwater fish can be found in rivers and lakes across the realm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20064.name: balloon frog
20064.col_2: A hardy amphibian found in the relatively warm-watered lakes of eastern Abalathia's Spine. The plump legs make for a fine meal.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20065.name: lantern marimo
20065.col_2: A rare type of luminescent moss found in the lightless depths of lakes, as well as in caves. Slight currents cause the moss to form into a ball as it grows.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20066.name: death loach
20066.col_2: This particular variety of loach can be found in the lakes, rivers, and swamps of northern Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20067.name: Grymm crab
20067.col_2: A succulent freshwater crab remarkably found only in the Peaks lake of Grymm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20068.name: Enid shrimp
20068.col_2: A succulent freshwater shrimp remarkably found only in the Peaks lake of Enid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20069.name: invisible crayfish
20069.col_2: The pristine white shell of this freshwater crustacean makes it nigh invisible when the wavekin is hiding amongst rocks or sand of a similar hue.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20070.name: rapids jumper
20070.col_2: A lifetime of swimming against strong-yet-slow river currents has left this freshwater fish bereft of most fatty flesh.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20071.name: Abalathian salamander
20071.col_2: An amphibian commonly found living in the myriad lakes and swamps of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20072.name: adamantite bichir
20072.col_2: A freshwater fish native to the wetlands of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20073.name: meditator
20073.col_2: Possessed of the unique ability to survive for extended periods out of water, the meditator will periodically “bathe” on the banks of the rivers and lakes in which it resides.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20074.name: deemster
20074.col_2: A freshwater fish so enormous, even the legends sung of the elusive wavekin do not do it justice.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20075.name: stonytongue
20075.col_2: This distant cousin to the Coerthan bonytongue can be found dwelling in the freshwater lakes and rivers of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20076.name: Bull's bite
20076.col_2: A small carnivorous fish found solely in the isolated Gyr Abanian pond known as the Bull's Bath.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20077.name: peeping pisces
20077.col_2: This freshwater fish is possessed of an eye on both the top and bottom of its head, allowing it to simultaneously spy threats above and below the water, should the need arise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20078.name: scimitarfish
20078.col_2: Not a swordfish, but a sword-like fish found in the rivers of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20079.name: gigant bass
20079.col_2: An aptly named freshwater fish native to the rivers of Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20080.name: Nhaama's boon
20080.col_2: One of the rare fish found in the Nhaama Desert's even rarer freshwater oases.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20081.name: cave killifish
20081.col_2: These small fries found primarily in the caves of Gyr Abania rarely grow to more than one or two ilms.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20082.name: bone melter
20082.col_2: This lake snail feeds by attaching itself to the bones of drowned animals.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20083.name: fallen leaf
20083.col_2: The still waters of Dimwold are teeming with these fish who, to the untrained eye, appear naught more than fallen leaves.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20084.name: falling star
20084.col_2: This glowing orb is actually a colony of rare luminescent algae found in the caves of eastern Gyr Abania.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20085.name: capsized squeaker
20085.col_2: This odd, whiskered fish is found only in the sheltered waters of the Comet's Tail.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20086.name: nirvana crab
20086.col_2: The backs of these freshwater crabs are adorned with colorful colonies of water-resistant fungus.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20087.name: Velodyna grass carp
20087.col_2: This variety of grass carp is most often found in the northeastern Eorzean river from which it earns its name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20088.name: black Velodyna carp
20088.col_2: One of several varieties of carp found in the Velodyna River, this particular species is immediately recognizable from its pitch-black skin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20089.name: Rhalgr's bolt
20089.col_2: This eel-like freshwater fish has been blessed with the capacity to emit an electric charge that can prove deadly to smaller wavekin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20090.name: highland perch
20090.col_2: Once common throughout the Gyr Abanian highlands, overfishing has relegated the remainder of the species to Mirage Creek.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20091.name: gravel gudgeon
20091.col_2: This freshwater fish will bury itself deep in the gravel-littered beds of rivers, making it a difficult catch.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20092.name: grinning anchovy
20092.col_2: These small saltwater fish swim in massive schools, using their sheer numbers to ensure that even if a few stragglers are swallowed, the species will endure.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20093.name: Glass herring
20093.col_2: This common silver fish will travel back and forth between the Ruby Sea and the Glass Ocean searching for food.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20094.name: hellyfish
20094.col_2: The abundance of these translucent amorphs to the volcanic island of Hells' Lid was an invitation to an ill-conceived moniker, most likely given by a rum-soaked pirate.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20095.name: piece of ruby coral
20095.col_2: A piece of sharp crimson coral, widely found throughout the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20096.name: piece of sapphire coral
20096.col_2: A piece of sharp azure coral, widely found throughout the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20097.name: piece of bone coral
20097.col_2: A piece of sharp milky white coral, widely found throughout the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20098.name: butterfly fish
20098.col_2: One of few brightly colored fish native to the Ruby Tide.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20099.name: dafu
20099.col_2: Its sheer dominance over other life in the Ruby Sea has earned this sizable wavekin the title “dafu,” or literally, the top dog...er, fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20100.name: swordfish
20100.col_2: Fishers seeking to land ocean-dwelling swordfish must take care not to accidentally impale themselves on the wavekin's serrated bladelike maw.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20101.name: leaf tatsunoko
20101.col_2: At a glance, one might mistake this queerly shaped denizen of the Ruby Sea for an errant piece of seaweed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20102.name: Glass flounder
20102.col_2: This flat bottom dweller spends most of its life skittering about the floors of the Glass Ocean, but can also be found in the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20103.name: Zekki gator
20103.col_2: This giant shark regularly hunts the waters of the coast of the Isle of Zekki, and has been known to attack the pirates and fishers who frequent its strands.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20104.name: daio squid
20104.col_2: A rarely seen giant squid, thought to be the inspiration for 35% of all pirate chanties sung on the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20105.name: koromo octopus
20105.col_2: A highly elusive giant octopus, so rarely seen that not a single pirate chanty sung on the Red Sea mentions the poor cephalopod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20106.name: gliding fish
20106.col_2: A unique saltwater fish that will jump from the water to evade predators, using its pectoral fins to glide across the ocean surface.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20107.name: globefish
20107.col_2: A saltwater fish that will puff its spike-laden body to bursting to protect itself when provoked.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20108.name: fan clam
20108.col_2: The shell of this bivalve mollusk is ribbed like the “uchiwa” hand fans used by Hingan festival-goers in summer.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20109.name: blockhead
20109.col_2: A saltwater fish as stubborn as its name suggests. It is pure coincidence that it also has a hard bony plate protecting its tiny brain.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20110.name: Glass tuna
20110.col_2: One of the most popular ingredients in Hingan sushi, the giant Glass tuna are thought to follow the strong ocean currents for thousands of malms in their lifetime.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20111.name: Doman crayfish
20111.col_2: These tiny freshwater crustaceans can be found in relative abundance in the flooded rice paddies of Yanxia.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20112.name: ruby shrimp
20112.col_2: One of the most common shrimp found in the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20113.name: striped fugu
20113.col_2: Similar to the globefish, the fugu will puff up its body to frighten away potential predators. Those who do not heed the wavekin's warning and devour it anyway will most certainly succumb to the lethal poison found in the fugu's flesh.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20114.name: raitonfish
20114.col_2: A large freshwater fish named for the levin-manipulating technique mastered by the ninja of Doma.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20115.name: blank oscar
20115.col_2: The body of this rare freshwater fish is entirely void of pigment.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20116.name: dragonfish
20116.col_2: Despite the insistence of Yanxian villagers, the freshwater dragonfish is ten parts fish, zero parts dragon.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20117.name: lordly salmon
20117.col_2: Just as do the salmon of Eorzea, the steely blue salmon of the Far East spend their lives in the sea before returning to the freshwater rivers where they were born to spawn and die.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20118.name: Yanxian koi
20118.col_2: A mottled freshwater carp of middling size native to the southern reaches of the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20119.name: kotsu zetsu
20119.col_2: A large, slow-swimming freshwater fish found primarily in Yanxia's Plum Spring.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20120.name: longhair catfish
20120.col_2: Though named for its lengthy whiskers, this catfish's most ready feature is not its mustache, but the wavy scale-like patterns on its back.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20121.name: plum gazer
20121.col_2: Those seeking to land a plum gazer must travel to the secluded Plum Spring, hidden deep in Yanxia's Gensui Chain.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20122.name: pandamoth
20122.col_2: This regal freshwater fish has a distinct white and black mottling which, while giving the wavekin an air of majesty, also makes it easy to spot by predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20123.name: Doman trout
20123.col_2: An extremely common fish found throughout Yanxia, and a popular dish amongst the realm's residents.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20124.name: Doman eel
20124.col_2: A thin freshwater eel that can be found living amongst the reeds growing in the Valley of the Fallen Rainbow.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20125.name: brassfish
20125.col_2: This brightly colored freshwater fish of Far Eastern origin is a favorite amongst aquarium owners.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20126.name: Othardian trout
20126.col_2: A freshwater fish found in rivers across the entire Othardian continent.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20127.name: zagas khaal
20127.col_2: A freshwater fish extremely common to many of the One River's northern tributaries. Its name literally translates to “river fish.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20128.name: steppe skipper
20128.col_2: A swift freshwater fish that, when swimming near the surface of the One River tributaries in which it is commonly found, appears to skip through the rivers' reeds.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20129.name: dry steppe skipper
20129.col_2: A small freshwater fish found in the arid southern grasslands bordering the Nhaama Desert.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20130.name: sun bass
20130.col_2: This violent fish native to the Azim Steppe prefers the calm waters of a lake or wetland to the swift-moving currents of a river.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20131.name: skytear
20131.col_2: The skytear can be found in the quick-flowing shallow rapids near a river's source rather than in the deeper, slow-moving waters downstream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20132.name: dawn crayfish
20132.col_2: A red-shelled freshwater crustacean found in abundance in the lakes and rivers of the Azim Steppe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20133.name: dusk crayfish
20133.col_2: A white-shelled freshwater crustacean found in abundance in the lakes and rivers of the Azim Steppe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20134.name: bowfish
20134.col_2: This swift-moving freshwater fish can be found up and down the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20135.name: jade sculpin
20135.col_2: Highly developed scales and spines set this sculpin apart from its western counterparts.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20136.name: Padjali loach
20136.col_2: A horn-shaped fish native to the dark bogs of Dimwold.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20137.name: nogoi
20137.col_2: A common variety of koi found in almost every region on Othard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20138.name: curtain pleco
20138.col_2: This freshwater fish has a billowy, curtain-like dorsal fin that it uses to confuse predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20140.name: hardscale
20140.col_2: A freshwater cousin of the lightscale with scales as hard as its name suggests.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20141.name: eastern pike
20141.col_2: The massive eastern pike is technically classified as a freshwater fish. The breed, however, can survive the brackish waters of the Hathoeva and Velodyna river deltas.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20142.name: wraithfish
20142.col_2: This freshwater fish native to the bogs of Dimwold will oft conceal itself beneath the planks of the Wraithwalk for protection.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20143.name: little Perykos
20143.col_2: As is the case with the little Thalaos, the little Perykos is anything but small. Though normally only found in the Indigo Deep, this lord of the North Isle of Endless Summer can sometimes be found swimming in the five seas and beyond...yet for what reason, no one knows.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20144.name: wentletrap
20144.col_2: A tiny Ruby Sea mollusk with a beautiful spiral shell that is sought by jewelry makers across the Far East.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20145.name: black boxfish
20145.col_2: This saltwater cousin to the puffers changes color several times during its development, and it is only in the final years of adulthood that it bears the hue from which it earns its moniker.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20146.name: Glass manta
20146.col_2: This denizen of the Glass Ocean is one of the largest fish of its type ever recorded.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20147.name: regal silverside
20147.col_2: According to Hingan fishers, it was not until the past twenty summers that the regal silverside began appearing in their nets. It is popular opinion that the fish may have been introduced via bilge water dumped by foreign trade bulks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20148.name: snowflake moray
20148.col_2: A saltwater fish that exhibits a peculiar symbiotic relationship with spiny lobsters.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20149.name: hoppfish
20149.col_2: While “hopping” out of the water will aid this saltwater species in escaping larger fish, the action attracts flocks of hungry seagulls that will harry the schools for entire turns of the sun.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20150.name: lightscale
20150.col_2: A freshwater cousin of the hardscale with scales as light as its name suggests.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20151.name: grass fugu
20151.col_2: This highly poisonous saltwater fish can survive for long periods of time in freshwater rivers, and can, on occasion, be found as far as ten malms upstream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20152.name: giant eel
20152.col_2: An eel's size is proportional to the amount it eats. The giant freshwater eels of the One River eat...a lot.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20153.name: kamina crab
20153.col_2: While abundant in the sea, hermit crabs are quite rare in fresh water, possibly due to the lack of available homes. The kamina crab is one example.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20154.name: spider crab
20154.col_2: The spider crab's spindly legs carry the deep-sea crustacean hundreds of malms across their migratory routes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20155.name: little dragonfish
20155.col_2: The elongated forehead of this saltwater species is compared to the nose of a tengu─a legendary birdlike creature of Far Eastern legend.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20156.name: black fanfish
20156.col_2: This saltwater wavekin uses both the size and color of its fins to its advantage, allowing it to, for all intents and purposes, disappear in the darker depths of the sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20157.name: zebra shark
20157.col_2: Unlike those of the mystical zebra, the pronounced “stripes” upon this wavekin's back are more accurately compared to a tiger's spots.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20158.name: Nophica's comb
20158.col_2: The sharp, bone-like protrusions on this carnivorous mollusk's massive shell give it the comb-like appearance from which it earns its name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20159.name: warty wartfish
20159.col_2: This sluggardly wartfish native to the One River somehow has more warts than a common wartfish, if that can be believed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20160.name: common whelk
20160.col_2: It would not be called a common whelk if this whelk was not found as abundantly as it is across the whole of Othard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20161.name: hairless barb
20161.col_2: This impossibly monstrous freshwater fish grew impossibly monstrous despite a diet of mostly river grasses.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20162.name: hatchetfish
20162.col_2: The Ruby Sea hatchetfish earns its name from its overgrown head which, if you squint hard enough, might appear similar to the head of a timberlord's hatchet.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20163.name: threadfish
20163.col_2: This spindly saltwater fish spurns the colder currents of the north in favor of the warm waters along Othard and Ilsabard's southern coasts.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20164.name: garden eel
20164.col_2: Garden eels spend most of their lives buried in sandy sea bottoms, emerging only to hunt and to mate.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20165.name: Eastern sea pickle
20165.col_2: Named for its shape and not its flavor, this repugnant sluglike mass is found throughout the Glass Ocean and Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20166.name: brindlebass
20166.col_2: This enormous saltwater bass can be highly territorial, devouring anything and everything that passes through its chosen demesne.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20167.name: demon stonefish
20167.col_2: A saltwater wavekin commonly avoided by fishers due to the extreme amount of toxins found in its flesh.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20168.name: armored crayfish
20168.col_2: A deep-red relative of the Doman crayfish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20169.name: bighead carp
20169.col_2: A dark-scaled carp found in the One River, easily identified by its queer downward-pointing eyes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20170.name: zeni clam
20170.col_2: Named after an ancient Far Eastern currency, this bivalve mollusk is most commonly found in the lakes and rivers of Yanxia.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20171.name: corpse-eater
20171.col_2: A large carnivorous wavekin that dwells in the warm currents of the southern seas.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20172.name: ronin trevally
20172.col_2: This large variety of trevally is given the name ronin for its tendency to journey the warm southern seas in solitude.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20173.name: toothsome grouper
20173.col_2: The most delicious of saltwater groupers...if the merchants selling it for thrice the price of a regular grouper are to be believed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20174.name: horned turban
20174.col_2: The shell of this warm-water sea mollusk is twisted like the turbans worn by the dhalmel drivers of Thavnair.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20175.name: Ruby Sea star
20175.col_2: These spiny five-limbed invertebrates survive by feeding on the flesh of dead fish fallen to the sea floor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20176.name: gauntlet crab
20176.col_2: These giant crabs hide themselves amongst the plants that grow on a river's bed, the moss growing on their claws used as camouflage.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20177.name: hermit goby
20177.col_2: A decent-sized fish found in the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20178.name: skythorn
20178.col_2: An ancient breed of freshwater fish found with little frequency in the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20179.name: swordtip
20179.col_2: One of the most widespread squid species on Hydaelyn.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20180.name: false scad
20180.col_2: A common saltwater fish doing its best scad impression.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20181.name: snow crab
20181.col_2: Snow crabs live in deep waters, scurrying hither and thither across the ocean floor in search of carrion.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20182.name: red-eyed lates
20182.col_2: A saltwater fish found in both the Glass Ocean and the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20183.name: common bitterling
20183.col_2: This freshwater fish is found on both the Othardian east coast and in Shishu─the Hingan island upon which sits Kugane.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20184.name: fifty-summer cod
20184.col_2: This long-living freshwater cod is commonly found in the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20185.name: Nagxian mullet
20185.col_2: A thin, eel-like fish native to Nagxia, but found throughout the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20186.name: redcoat
20186.col_2: A large, reddish orange fish with distinctively enormous eyes to help it see in the murky depths of the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20187.name: Yanxian tiger prawn
20187.col_2: This Far Eastern crustacean has not only the stripes, but also the ferocity of a Yanxian tiger.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20188.name: tengu fan
20188.col_2: The tengu fan, named for its round, flat shape, will emit electric shocks from its body when threatened. Though the shocks cannot kill, they do stun, affording the fish ample opportunity to flee.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20189.name: star turban
20189.col_2: When viewed from the side, this sea mollusk's shell looks like a turban; however, when viewed from above, its radiating spines give it the appearance of a twinkling star.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20190.name: blue-fish
20190.col_2: A delicious freshwater fish with the most jejune moniker of all the One River's aquatic denizens.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20191.name: steppe bullfrog
20191.col_2: Steppe bullfrogs can be found across both Yanxia and Nagxia and are easily identifiable by their deep, bellowing mating croaks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20192.name: cavalry catfish
20192.col_2: This large, aggressive freshwater fish will “charge” most anything moving, regardless of its size.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20193.name: redfin
20193.col_2: Second only to the blue-fish in mediocrity of monikers, the freshwater redfin of the One River─unsurprisingly─has bright-red fins.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20194.name: moondisc
20194.col_2: A cousin of the sundisc, the moondisc also features celestial patterns upon its body, though its are decidedly brighter to serve as camouflage in the white-bedded waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20195.name: bleached bonytongue
20195.col_2: Similar to most wavekin that have taken up residence in Loch Seld, the bleached bonytongue is almost entirely white.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20196.name: salt shark
20196.col_2: The salt shark has an elongated body that it can bend like an eel, allowing it to navigate Loch Seld's obstacle-strewn lakebed in search for prey.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20197.name: king's mantle
20197.col_2: Very few species of octopus have been discovered in Loch Seld, but those that have─such as the king's mantle─are magnificently monstrous.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20198.name: sea lamp
20198.col_2: This variety of sea anemone emits a soft green glow when its tentacles are disturbed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20199.name: amberjack
20199.col_2: This large saltwater predator can be found in the waters off both the eastern and western coasts of Hingashi.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20200.name: cherry salmon
20200.col_2: Though dubbed a salmon, this particular variety does not journey downstream to the sea, spending its entire life in the river where it was born.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20201.name: yu-no-hana crab
20201.col_2: Hingan folklore has that all hot springs were once dug from the ground by these hardy crustaceans.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20202.name: Dotharli gudgeon
20202.col_2: This freshwater fish commonly found in the upper One River is also known as the Mol gudgeon, the Kahkol gudgeon, the Dataqi gudgeon, the Horo gudgeon, and after whichever other Xaela tribe that insists their ancestors first caught the species.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20203.name: river clam
20203.col_2: A small bivalve mollusk found living in the sands of the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20204.name: grass shark
20204.col_2: Grass sharks are massive, their size rivaling that of even the Glass Ocean's greatest predators─an amazing feat considering grass sharks live their entire lives in the confines of the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20205.name: typhoon shrimp
20205.col_2: The typhoon shrimp is one of only a few shrimp species that can survive the toxically salty waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20206.name: rock oyster
20206.col_2: This bivalve mollusk grows in abundance on boulders and statues submerged in Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20207.name: salt urchin
20207.col_2: The white coloring of the salt urchin's spines make them difficult to see on Loch Seld's colorless lakebed. Those who choose to wade through the shallows should always take care to protect their feet.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20208.name: carpenter crab
20208.col_2: A carpenter crab's claws are powerful enough to cut through solid wood. Whether or not a carpenter crab has ever constructed something from that wood remains unconfirmed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20209.name: spiny lobster
20209.col_2: This massive crustacean found in both the Ruby Sea and the Glass Ocean is considered a delicacy in the Far East, and is a luxury oft too extravagant for any but the richest of nobles to partake in.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20210.name: mitsukuri shark
20210.col_2: There is no doubt that the mitsukuri shark's most defining feature is its katana-like mouth and the tales it has spawned of poor fishers being impaled.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20211.name: Doman bubble eye
20211.col_2: A variety of bubble eye goldfish selectively bred by Doman royalty for innumerable generations.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20212.name: dragon squeaker
20212.col_2: There are many theories as to why this remarkable breed of One River squeaker swims tail first, yet most have been dismissed as feeble attempts to explain what simply cannot be explained, such as why the sky is blue or why tides come in and the tides go out.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20213.name: dawn herald
20213.col_2: Though smaller than the dusk herald, the dawn herald is as commonly found in the waters of the One River as its close cousin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20214.name: salt cellar
20214.col_2: An ashen-shelled snail found throughout Loch Seld. Cooking the gastropods in their shells with garlic and herbs is the preferred method of consumption.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20215.name: white sturgeon
20215.col_2: The white sturgeon is believed by some scholars to simply be normal sturgeons exhibiting albinism─a rare trait that became common once all the darker sturgeons were poached from Loch Seld on account of them being easy to see.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20216.name: tithe collector
20216.col_2: One of Loch Seld's largest native species.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20217.name: bashful batfish
20217.col_2: The unique shape and coloration of the batfish makes this denizen of the Ruby Sea a highly sought-after specimen amongst collectors.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20218.name: river bream
20218.col_2: Unlike sea breams, this quirky cousin will travel back and forth 'twixt the brackish waters of a river's delta and the fresher waters upstream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20219.name: snipe eel
20219.col_2: The snipe eels of the One River will never grow plumper than an ilm or two in diameter, but can stretch to several yalms in length.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20220.name: cherubfish
20220.col_2: A rare freshwater fish native to Yanxia and the Azim Steppe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20221.name: dusk herald
20221.col_2: The dusk herald is a fair-sized fish commonly found in the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20222.name: glaring perch
20222.col_2: This freshwater perch is found up and down the One River.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20223.name: Abalathian pipira
20223.col_2: While given the modifier Abalathian, this particular pipira will not be found in the Spine's western or even central regions, preferring the biting salty waters of the Lochs.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20224.name: steel loach
20224.col_2: The steel loach's scintillant silver body reflects sunlight in a manner that makes the fish difficult to spot in its native Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20225.name: ivory sole
20225.col_2: The whitish grey skin of this large flatfish allows it to hide itself on the bottom of Loch Seld with such efficiency that for years Ala Mhigans thought the species extinct.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20226.name: motley beakfish
20226.col_2: A striped carnivore that hunts the Ruby Sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20227.name: thousandfang
20227.col_2: A rare, sea-dwelling scalekin infamous for its gaping maw lined with multiple rows of bladelike teeth, though official observations by scholars put the fang count at no more than a few score.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20228.name: ichthyosaur
20228.col_2: Let not its dolphin-like appearance fool you. The ichthyosaur is a ravenous scalekin that feeds on squid, fish, and the occasional man overboard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20229.name: sailfin
20229.col_2: A unique freshwater fish featuring astonishingly overgrown dorsal and anal fins.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20230.name: fangshi
20230.col_2: An extremely rare freshwater fish whose face is covered in countless whisker-like protrusions.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20231.name: flamefish
20231.col_2: This large freshwater fish's skin features brilliant streaks of fiery yellow and orange.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20232.name: fickle krait
20232.col_2: Special glands within the fickle krait's body create a deadly poison feared by fishers and coveted by assassins.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20233.name: eternal eye
20233.col_2: This tiny species' skin exhibits a violet hue rarely seen in freshwater fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20234.name: soul of the stallion
20234.col_2: A rare white freshwater fish believed to harbor the soul of a once-proud steppe stallion.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20235.name: flood tuna
20235.col_2: The descendants of sea tuna believed by scholars to have arrived in Loch Seld during the great flood that ended the Fifth Astral Era.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20236.name: mercenary crab
20236.col_2: This heavily armored crab is one of few species adapted to the hypersalinated waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

20237.name: ashfish
20237.col_2: A pigmentless fish found solely in Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20238.name: silken sunfish
20238.col_2: A rare breed of sunfish that can survive only in waters exhibiting extreme salinity.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20239.name: mosasaur
20239.col_2: An aggressive scalekin native to the saline waters of Loch Seld.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20260.name: regional folklore trader's token A
20260.col_2: A note of promise granted for the delivery of tomes of regional folklore.

20270.name: bolt of Nagxian silk
20270.col_2: A light, billowy silk woven using traditional methods of the Nagxian people.

20271.name: basket of ratanhia leaves
20271.col_2: Leaves of a low-growing shrub native to the plains of Nagxia. The leaves contain high concentrations of tannin, an ingredient necessary in tanning leather.

20272.name: bolt of Taoist's wool
20272.col_2: Despite supposedly being woven countless generations past, this cloth appears as it was crafted yesterday.

20273.name: circle of Nagxian leather
20273.col_2: A beastkin hide tanned using traditional Nagxian methods.

20275.name: chivalrous armor coffer (IL 290)
20275.col_2: A banded chest containing a complete set of chivalrous armor, an antiquated Galatyn, and an antiquated Evalach.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 70. IL: 290. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

20276.name: pacifist's attire coffer (IL 290)
20276.col_2: A banded chest containing a complete set of pacifist's attire and a pair of antiquated Sudarshana Chakra.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 70. IL: 290. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

20277.name: brutal armor coffer (IL 290)
20277.col_2: A banded chest containing a complete set of brutal armor and an antiquated Farsha.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 70. IL: 290. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

20278.name: storyteller's attire coffer (IL 290)

20307.name: morin khuur
20307.col_2: A traditional instrument of the Azim Steppe's nomadic Xaela tribes, the morin khuur has two strings (the “male” and the “female”) woven together from the tail hair of a stallion and a mare, respectively.

20308.name: veteran's Clan mark log
20308.col_2: A list of elite marks slain by the log's owner─a hunter so dedicated, that it is said she tracked prey until the ripe age of one hundred and seventy-two summers, dying of natural causes after slaying her thirtieth king behemoth.

20521.name: Sassho-seki fragment
20521.col_2: Literally the “killing stone,” this curiosity is said to bring death to all who touch it. Handle with care.

20524.name: castaway chocobo chick
20524.col_2: Currently without a name. “Wilson” recommended.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the castaway chocobo chick minion.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20525.name: odder otter
20525.col_2: Is there anything odder than an otter who lives out of water?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the odder otter minion.

20526.name: fox kit
20526.col_2: His devotion toward you will prove fair and balanced.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the fox kit minion.

20527.name: Tora-jiro
20527.col_2: His name suggests that this tiny tiger cub has an older brother. His parents deny everything.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the Tora-jiro minion.

20528.name: tiny tatsunoko
20528.col_2: If the Hingan word for sea horse is tatsunoko, would that make this a sea pony? <hex:021A020203>Your<hex:021A020103> little sea pony?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the tiny tatsunoko minion.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20529.name: bombfish
20529.col_2: He will give you an offer that can't be defused.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the bombfish minion.

20530.name: Bom Boko
20530.col_2: An adorable raccoon dog pup with a big heart and even bigger testicles.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the Bom Boko minion.

20531.name: road sparrow
20531.col_2: This house sparrow's home is on the road. Sparrow.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the road sparrow minion.

20532.name: wind-up Lyse
20532.col_2: Most certainly not a repurposed wind-up Yda.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Lyse minion.

20533.name: dress-up Yugiri
20533.col_2: One Yugiri is never enough.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the dress-up Yugiri minion.

20534.name: wind-up Gosetsu
20534.col_2: Wanted by the Empire...and good little boys and girls across Othard.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Gosetsu minion.

20535.name: wind-up Yotsuyu
20535.col_2: Now she can be the bane of <hex:021A020203>your<hex:021A020103> existence! A font of <hex:021A020203>your<hex:021A020103> misery!<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Yotsuyu minion.

20536.name: mock-up Grynewaht
20536.col_2: Bwahahahaha!<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the mock-up Grynewaht minion.

20537.name: wind-up Namazu
20537.col_2: Half cat. Half fish. All fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Namazu minion.

20538.name: Ivon Coeurlfist doll
20538.col_2: Technically “Coeurl<hex:021A020203>paw<hex:021A020103>.” <hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the Ivon Coeurlfist minion.

20539.name: wind-up chimera
20539.col_2: Crafted by piecing together the remnants of unsold automata.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up chimera minion.

20540.name: wind-up meateater
20540.col_2: Watch out boys, he'll (literally) chew you up.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up meateater minion.

20541.name: magitek avenger F1
20541.col_2: Avenger, assembled!<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the magitek avenger F1 minion.

20542.name: Ghido
20542.col_2: There is most likely a logical explanation as to why this aged turtle can navigate the skies. Most likely.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the Ghido minion.

20543.name: wind-up Exdeath
20543.col_2: Most maniacal tree beings bent on world domination are usually not intimidated by turtles. This one is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Exdeath minion.

20544.name: wind-up Khloe
20544.col_2: Because there is nothing wrong with a fully automated mechanical reconstruction of a young girl of three and ten summers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Khloe minion.

20545.name: wind-up Susano
20545.col_2: If the Kojin believe that within every item resides a deity, then who exactly resides inside this automaton?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Susano minion.

20546.name: wind-up Lakshmi
20546.col_2: Your, your, your serpentine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Lakshmi minion.

20547.name: wind-up Bismarck
20547.col_2: The hairiest whale you will see this fortnight.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Bismarck minion.

20548.name: Falcon ignition key
20548.col_2: This ignition key winds the gears of the Falcon-class airship.

20549.name: blissful kamuy fife
20549.col_2: The sweet song of this stout flute is said to summon a kamuy blessed by Lakshmi herself.

20550.name: reveling kamuy fife
20550.col_2: The powerful tones emitted by this stout flute are said to summon a kamuy blessed by Susano himself.

20551.name: magitek predator identification key
20551.col_2: A thin, rectangular piece of what appears to be cermet. Placing it near your magitek predator will magically bring the machine to life.

20552.name: battle lion horn
20552.col_2: An iron-banded horn used to summon your battle lion mount...to battle!

20553.name: battle bear horn
20553.col_2: A simple horn used to summon your battle bear─a towering mount certain to strike fear into the hearts of your foes.

20554.name: battle panther bell
20554.col_2: A brass bell used to summon your battle panther mount. How only your panther answers the summons, and not the panthers of hundreds of other adventurers with similar summoning bells is a mystery for the ages.

20555.name: yol whistle
20555.col_2: A rough-hewn whistle whose clear tone summons your loyal yol mount.

20556.name: Alte Roite prism
20556.col_2: A multifaceted prism that, when held aloft, refracts light in a way that can be seen only by your Alte Roite mount─a being who possesses the uncanny ability to hide in plain sight until summoned.

20557.name: Centurio tiger horn
20557.col_2: The horn of a beast felled on a legendary Hunt used to summon a legendary tiger gifted to you by the Clan Centurio.

20613.col_2: The ruby red eggs of salmon returning upriver to spawn. Bait for freshwater fishing.

20614.name: nightcrawler
20614.col_2: These fat earthworms that feed above ground in the small hours of the night have been known to grow up to two full fulms in length. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

20615.name: midge larva
20615.col_2: The bright-red coloring of this undeveloped midge makes it an easy target for sharp-eyed fish. Live bait for freshwater fishing.

20617.name: live shrimp
20617.col_2: A tiny, twitching sea shrimp. Live bait for ocean fishing.

20618.name: bream lure
20618.col_2: A lure for bream made by attaching rubber fins to a heavy lead ball.

20619.name: suspending minnow
20619.col_2: A plug lure made to resemble a minnow. Effective in attracting freshwater fish from both surface and floor.

20637.name: Ixion clarion
20637.col_2: It is said the legendary Ixion can be tamed by no man. With this horn, however, can the steed be calmed enough for one to mount his back.

20777.name: Gold Saucer consolation prize
20777.col_2: Because at the Gold Saucer, everyone goes home a winner.

20779.col_2: Items necessary to ensure the Ala Mhigan Resistance can keep fighting the good fight.

20780.name: handful of starcrack sand
20780.col_2: A metallic sand which simpleminded smallfolk believe contains pieces of the very comet Rhalgr tore from the heavens.

20781.name: Shishu koban
20781.col_2: This oblong gold coin once saw heavy circulation throughout Hingashi and the eastern provinces of Othard.

20782.name: Cotter Dynasty relic
20782.col_2: A lavishly decorated ornament dated to the rule of Gyr Abanian king Cotter.

20783.name: lump of Peaks pigment
20783.col_2: Extracted from natural sources in the Gyr Abanian highlands, this clay-based substance can be dried and ground, then prepared with water and oil to create a colorful dye.

20784.name: yellow kudzu root
20784.col_2: This variety of kudzu not only exhibits the curative properties of its more common cousin, it has been observed growing almost twice as fast. It has also been observed withering and dying twice as fast.

20785.name: Gyr Abanian chub
20785.col_2: A freshwater fish most commonly found in the Velodyna and Hathoeva rivers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20786.name: coral horse
20786.col_2: This rare specimen of sea horse has a body that so closely resembles coral that it can be almost impossible to locate amongst the reefs it calls home.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20787.name: maiden's heart
20787.col_2: It is believed that only one in every thousand marimo is born blood red instead of the more common green. An exact count has yet to be conducted.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

20788.name: Velodyna salmon
20788.col_2: Similar to Aldenard's other salmon species, this salmon also spends its entire life in the sea, until returning to the Velodyna to spawn...and die.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

20789.name: purple buckler
20789.col_2: There was a time that these snapping turtles were caught for their nigh-impenetrable shells which were used as shields by the ancient Gyr Abanian highland clans.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

21054.col_2: A nondescript horn that emits a harrowing drone which, for reasons unknown, summons an overgrown korpokkur known playfully as the “kolossus.”

21055.name: wind-up Hien
21055.col_2: Be proud, my new owner. Be proud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Hien minion.

21056.name: wind-up Kojin
21056.col_2: Is it green? Is it blue? Or...is it neither?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Kojin minion.

21057.name: wind-up Ravana
21057.col_2: Low on low he stands, gazing up to see.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Ravana minion.

21058.name: mameshiba
21058.col_2: Who let the newborn miniature Far Eastern canine specimen out? Who, who, who, who, who!?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the mameshiba minion.

21059.name: tengu doll
21059.col_2: And you know what they say about the size of a doll's nose.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the tengu doll minion.

21060.name: wind-up Matanga
21060.col_2: This is not Matanga. Matanga is graceful.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Matanga minion.

21061.name: wind-up Ramza
21061.col_2: Stands ready to fight for truth, justice, and the Ivalician way.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Ramza minion.

21062.name: wind-up Ixion
21062.col_2: A horse is a horse, of course. Except when it is Ixion.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the wind-up Ixion minion.

21063.name: axolotl eft
21063.col_2: Because there truly is nothing more adorable than an oddly Lalafellin face on the body of a moist, frilled salamander.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the axolotl eft minion.

21064.name: koala joey
21064.col_2: Shows no signs of stress or crotch rot, so hug away.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use item to acquire the koala joey minion.

21065.name: wind-up Shinryu

21773.col_2: It is unknown by whom or for what purpose this wooden idol carved in the likeness of the auspice Byakko was created.
