29702.name: Edenchoir bracelet coffer (IL 500)
29702.col_2: A banded chest containing an Edenchoir accessory.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 80. IL: 500. Bracelet type determined by current job or class at time of opening. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

29703.name: Edenchoir ring coffer (IL 500)
29703.col_2: A banded chest containing an Edenchoir accessory.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 80. IL: 500. Ring type determined by current job or class at time of opening. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

29704.name: Flower Basket card
29704.col_2: A common (★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 269

29705.name: Qitari card
29705.col_2: A common (★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 270

29706.name: Gnoll card
29706.col_2: An uncommon (★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 271

29707.name: Lizbeth card
29707.col_2: An uncommon (★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 278

29708.name: Batsquatch card
29708.col_2: A rare (★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 272

29709.name: Forgiven Obscenity card
29709.col_2: A rare (★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 273

29710.name: Huaca card
29710.col_2: A rare (★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 274

29711.name: Unknown card
29711.col_2: A rare (★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 275

29712.name: Ruby Weapon card
29712.col_2: An epic (★★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 276

29713.name: Therion card
29713.col_2: A legendary (★★★★★) card used in the game Triple Triad.<hex:02100103>Card No. 277

29714.name: ragworm
29714.col_2: A marine worm that slithers about in the rocks dotting the ocean floor. Effective for luring small fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in Ocean Fishing.

29715.name: krill
29715.col_2: A species of krill commonly found in the Rhotano Sea. Effective for luring medium-sized fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in Ocean Fishing.

29716.name: plump worm
29716.col_2: A species of worm that grows fat on the nutrients swirling about in the currents of the Rhotano Sea. Effective for luring large fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in Ocean Fishing.

29717.name: versatile lure
29717.col_2: A lure developed by the Fishermen's Guild specifically for novice anglers. Can be used on land or at sea.

29718.name: tossed dagger
29718.col_2: Often seen skimming the waves, shimmering like a blade in flight.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29719.name: jasperhead
29719.col_2: Sought for the gemlike objects that form in their stomachs, not in their heads, as the name might suggest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29720.name: Merlthor lobster
29720.col_2: As ubiquitous as they are delicious. A staple of seafood cuisine across Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29721.name: Heavenswimmer
29721.col_2: Easily spotted from afar due to their bright coloration, although sightings in the oceans surrounding Eorzea are scarce due to their unusual migratory patterns.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29722.name: ghoul barracuda
29722.col_2: Despite its considerable size, this ocean-dweller chooses to feast on the flesh of the dead rather than expend effort pursuing live prey.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29723.name: leopard eel
29723.col_2: As per its namesake, it occupies a position fairly close to the top of the food chain, but is still forced to flee from larger and more dangerous predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29724.name: marine bomb
29724.col_2: Known more for its tendency to explode with rage in a figurative sense rather than a literal one, as its name might suggest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29725.name: Momora Mora
29725.col_2: Unlike the Lalafell from whom its name derives, this ocean-drifter is far from diminutive.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29726.name: Merlthor butterfly
29726.col_2: Highly sought by aquarium owners for its vivid coloration, this increasingly rare species is arguably worth its weight in gold.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29727.name: gladius
29727.col_2: A fish named after a sword─or was the sword named after the fish?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29728.name: Rhotano wahoo
29728.col_2: Though it seems harmless enough at first glance, this fish has been rendered all but inedible by its highly poisonous diet. The taste is said to be exquisite by those brave enough to try it, however.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29729.name: Rhotano sardine
29729.col_2: Usually seen traveling in large schools, these rather plain fish possess the group mentality of a flock of sheep─that is, to follow whoever is in front and, lacking that, just keep moving forward until something with big teeth appears. Then all hells break loose.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29730.name: deep plaice
29730.col_2: The name provides a useful hint as to the areas of the ocean this creature usually inhabits.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29731.name: crimson monkfish
29731.col_2: An angler never forgets the first time they reel in one of these deep-sea demons, no matter how hard they try.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29732.name: lampfish
29732.col_2: Sought more for its roe than its meat. Thankfully its lack of muscular mass in comparison to the size of its body makes for an easy catch.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29733.name: ogre eel
29733.col_2: Even when it finds itself dangling from an angler's line, its only thought is to consume as much flesh as possible, which causes many a fisher to cast it back into the sea in sheer panic.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29734.name: cyan octopus
29734.col_2: Hunted for the copious amounts of ink it produces, the vast majority of which is spilled upon its capture. As a result, anglers with bright blue hands are a common sight around Galadion Bay.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29735.name: chrome hammerhead
29735.col_2: Differentiated from similar species by its unique coloration, which gives it a certain metallic sheen.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29736.name: floefish
29736.col_2: This small, almost entirely defenseless fish forms an important link in the food chain─one quite near to the bottom.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29737.name: megasquid
29737.col_2: One does not earn a name like “megasquid” by being small and unassuming, which this aquatic abomination certainly is not.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29738.name: Oschon's stone
29738.col_2: Seemingly living up to its namesake, this heavy and largely immobile wavekin spends most of its life on the ocean floor. It feeds by opening its mouth and waiting for curious prey to swim inside. <hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29739.name: La Noscean jelly
29739.col_2: It was named as part of a movement to expunge the word “fish” from “jellyfish,” for reasons pertaining to consistency and accuracy, although this has met with little success thus far.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29740.name: shaggy seadragon
29740.col_2: Almost indistinguishable in appearance from the seaweed on which it feeds. It must take care not to overeat and thereby destroy its own hiding place from predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29741.name: net crawler
29741.col_2: Unlike most crabs, the main source of edible meat is found in the legs. The torso is often discarded as it mostly consists of hard gristle and unappetizing...matter.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29742.name: dark nautilus
29742.col_2: Known for its ability to survive on aether alone, researchers are willing to part with huge sums of gil for live samples.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29743.name: elder dinichthys
29743.col_2: Swims about the Strait of Merlthor as though it owns the place─a claim which few of the other inhabitants are in any position to dispute.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29744.name: drunkfish
29744.col_2: If you had a face like this, you'd look sad, too.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29745.name: little Leviathan
29745.col_2: Even a greatly scaled-down (pun very much intended) version of the Lord of the Whorl is more than a match for all but the most experienced fishers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29746.name: sabaton
29746.col_2: Strangely for a mollusk, its body is covered in hard scales in addition to the more common shell. Many predators will steer clear of them simply because they are a bother to eat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29747.name: shooting star
29747.col_2: One's chances of seeing an actual shooting star are greater than that of being able to observe one of these rare wavekin in its natural habitat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29748.name: hammerclaw
29748.col_2: While most wavekin object quite strongly to being caught on a hook, these crustaceans make life especially difficult for anglers in retaliation. If they are not pinching fingers, they are flailing wildly with their heavy claws, both of which most fishers should and do go to great lengths to avoid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29749.name: heavenskey
29749.col_2: Due to being highly poisonous, it is believed to send those who eat of its flesh to the heavens. Compared to the seven hells, this may prove a more desirable destination.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29750.name: ghost shark
29750.col_2: According to certain sources, it is able to appear spontaneously from any body of water. Such stories, however, are probably best ignored.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29751.name: quicksilver blade
29751.col_2: While there may be larger and deadlier wavekin roaming the oceans, few can claim to be as hideous as this aberration of nature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29752.name: Navigator's print
29752.col_2: This denizen of the deep can proudly claim to take its name from a goddess, even if the tale behind it does involve being stepped on by said goddess.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29753.name: casket oyster
29753.col_2: While there are several theories surrounding the origin of its name, the general consensus is that it is as hard to open as a casket that has been nailed shut. However, it is nothing a brief spell in a pot of boiling water cannot solve.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29754.name: fishmonger
29754.col_2: Known for its habit of seeking out a variety of fish, though unlike its namesake, these are purely for its own consumption.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29755.name: mythril sovereign
29755.col_2: Known for its beautifully shimmering scales, which are in contrast to its rather lackluster meat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29756.name: nimble dancer
29756.col_2: Coveted by keepers of exotic fish for the mesmerizing manner in which its trailing fins catch the light.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29757.name: sea nettle
29757.col_2: Not the most welcome of catches, as it tends to deliver a nasty sting to those whose hands wander too close.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29758.name: great grandmarlin
29758.col_2: More often than not, this hulking yet deceptively quick wavekin escapes the angler's hook, usually by severing the line with its bladelike bill.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29759.name: shipwreck's sail
29759.col_2: This wavekin is so broad and flat that it has been compared to the sail of a ship left to float on the tide. In actuality, it is waiting for seabirds to pick the parasites from its flanks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29760.name: Azeyma's Sleeve
29760.col_2: Many artist's impressions of Azeyma depict Her with flowing, bell-adorned sleeves, not unlike the elegant silhouette of this wavekin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29761.name: hi-aetherlouse
29761.col_2: An aetherially charged wavekin that has a habit of appearing when one least expects or wants it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29762.name: floating saucer
29762.col_2: Far less welcome at a mess hall table than an actual saucer, as these odd creatures taste rather like a sailor's subligar. Apparently.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29763.name: aetheric seadragon
29763.col_2: Framed in fabulous frond-like fins, this ferocious fish frequently frightens off foes who would fight for its feed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29764.name: coral seadragon
29764.col_2: Dedicates its life to looking─and behaving─as much like coral as possible.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29765.name: roguesaurus
29765.col_2: Named after the river rather than the traditional Lominsan profession. Those unfortunate enough to encounter one will testify that to describe it as roguish would be an understatement, and that “murderous,” “man-eating,” and “malevolent” would all be more applicable adjectives.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29766.name: merman's mane
29766.col_2: Though the existence of mermen is much debated, if any were to exist, they would no doubt object to the comparisons drawn between their long locks and the tentacles of this grotesque cephalopod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29767.name: sweeper
29767.col_2: Its habit of moving its head from side to side while searching the seabed for food has earned it this unusual moniker.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29768.name: silencer
29768.col_2: While technically edible, it is not without side effects. Temporary loss of speech being the most noticeable, though there may be others that are harder to detect.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29769.name: deep-sea eel
29769.col_2: As may be inferred from the less-than-spectacular name, this eel resides in the sea. The deep part.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29770.name: executioner
29770.col_2: Goes out of its way to make life as difficult as possible for those who enter its territory, including sawing holes in hulls and tearing through nets.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29771.name: wild urchin
29771.col_2: A creamy center encased in horrendously sharp spines. Only those who acquire the knack of eating one without impaling themselves can acquire the decidedly acquired taste.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29772.name: true barramundi
29772.col_2: This slow-moving, ponderous wavekin manages to avoid the attention of predators by being so unremarkable as to hardly warrant attention in the first place.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29773.name: mopbeard
29773.col_2: Lifting it above the waterline causes it to transform from an elegant oceanic beauty to something resembling...well, a mop.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29774.name: slipsnail
29774.col_2: While it may seem harmless enough, it has a nasty surprise in store for unwitting predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29775.name: aronnax
29775.col_2: Its remarkable speed is matched only by its unfathomable clumsiness, the combination of which often leads it straight into the waiting nets of fishers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29776.name: coccosteus
29776.col_2: Revered by the Sahagin and reviled by practically everyone else. Its proclivity for biting fingers means that most who catch one end up wishing they hadn't.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29777.name: Bartholomew the Chopper
29777.col_2: Suspected by some to be the reincarnation of an unhinged murderer, although it is also known to have a more amiable side. Well, about as amiable as one can expect from a wavekin that revels in killing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29778.name: prowler
29778.col_2: While the word “prowl” may suggest the slow, deliberate movement of one tracking its prey, this particular wavekin is simply slow by nature, mainly as a result of sheer indolence.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29779.name: charlatan survivor
29779.col_2: At first glance, the charlatan survivor may appear to be a well-armored crustacean, but the outer shell is merely a purloined disguise concealing a much smaller creature beneath. Luckily, predatory wavekin are quite easily deceived and often choose to leave it alone in order to pursue less chitinous prey.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29780.name: prodigal son
29780.col_2: Rather than follow the standard migratory patterns of his brethren, this wandering wavekin swims to the beat of his own drum, and comes and goes as he pleases.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29781.name: gugrusaurus
29781.col_2: Spends most of its life attempting to slaughter anything and everything that it catches sight of. Considering the ample opportunities to practice such skills, it has become rather good at it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29782.name: funnel shark
29782.col_2: Its gaping maw draws in all manner of ocean life, along with a range of less-than-edible objects.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29783.name: the Fallen One
29783.col_2: Believed by some to have descended from the heavens, and judging by the way it nervously flits about the ocean, it wishes it could return to whence it came. Few wavekin look less comfortable in their habitat than this unfortunate creature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29784.name: spectral megalodon
29784.col_2: Due to the fact that most of its prey are petrified upon catching sight of this ominously glowing predator, it has rather an easy time finding a steady supply of food.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29785.name: spectral discus
29785.col_2: This aetherially infused wavekin gathers rather a lot of unwanted attention, and it has no natural defenses to fend off curious predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

29786.name: spectral sea bo
29786.col_2: Its strange blue glow seems to have done wonders for its self-confidence, and it can be seen doing the underwater variation of strutting like a peacock...or whatever the chocobo equivalent of a peacock is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

29787.name: spectral bass
29787.col_2: This most ordinary of fish has become rather extraordinary thanks to being bathed in otherworldly aether, giving it a fetching blue tinge.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 3 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

29788.name: Sothis
29788.col_2: It is unclear how this species of turtle came to have a shell covered in glittering crystal, though it does give oceanic hunters pause for thought before they attempt to bite down on it. This could be considered a form of unnatural protection.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29789.name: coral manta
29789.col_2: Few creatures can claim to have an entire ecosystem on their back, although this appears to afford the host no practical benefits whatsoever.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29790.name: stonescale
29790.col_2: The thick covering of rock-like substance does little to improve this shark's mobility. Being an apex predator means it has little need of excessive armor plating.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 4 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29791.name: elasmosaurus
29791.col_2: In the harsh, unforgiving open sea, few creatures have proven a more valuable ally to mankind than the elasmosaurus. Though they are most often known to tow ships and carry out courageous acts of self-sacrifice, these gentle giants can also be lethally dangerous when angered.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

29792.name: length of grade 2 skybuilders' plywood
29792.col_2: While this could be combined with a few bricks to create a makeshift bench, that may fall somewhat short of the skybuilders' rather more lofty aspirations.

29793.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' alloy
29793.col_2: Even in its current state, it would make a functional, if not especially elegant, murder weapon.

29794.name: grade 2 skybuilders' steel plate
29794.col_2: To some, it may seem a shame to ruin such a beautifully square piece of metal by battering it with a hammer.

29795.name: grade 2 skybuilders' ingot
29795.col_2: These would make a suitable substitute for house bricks were it not for their natural propensity to conduct cold, which is less than ideal in the freezing climes of Ishgard.

29796.name: circle of grade 2 skybuilders' leather
29796.col_2: Considered to be particularly valuable, especially by the creature to which it originally belonged.

29797.name: length of grade 2 skybuilders' rope
29797.col_2: Perfectly suited to pulling heavy objects. Less well suited to pushing them.

29798.name: bottle of grade 2 skybuilders' ink
29798.col_2: While some may question the skybuilders' need for a specific type of ink, it is believed that this particular variety is more resistant to the cold. After all, frozen ink does not lend itself well to fine penmanship, or any sort of penmanship, for that matter.

29799.name: bottle of grade 2 skybuilders' hemp milk
29799.description: bottles of grade 2 skybuilders' hemp milk
29799.col_2: While the layman may question exactly how one goes about milking a plant, the process is much the same as milking anything else: you give it a damned good squeeze and hope for the best.

29800.name: grade 2 skybuilders' crate
29800.col_2: Despite much of the work in the Firmament involving taking supplies <hex:021A020203>out of<hex:021A020103> boxes, the need occasionally arises to put them <hex:021A020203>into<hex:021A020103> boxes instead. Suggestions that the skybuilders simply reuse the boxes they already have were immediately shot down, presumably by someone who stands to profit from the production of new containers.

29801.name: handful of grade 2 skybuilders' nails
29801.col_2: Never was the description “tough as nails” more apt, because they are, in fact, nails.

29802.name: handful of grade 2 skybuilders' rivets
29802.col_2: Despite their name, discussions on these commonplace metal studs tend to be anything but riveting.

29803.name: handful of grade 2 skybuilders' rings
29803.col_2: Attempting to impress a potential spouse by presenting one of these mass-produced metallic circles will generally end in failure, and perhaps even a slap in the face for good measure.

29804.name: bundle of grade 2 skybuilders' leather straps
29804.description: bundles of grade 2 skybuilders' leather straps
29804.col_2: Some may wonder whether this leather was in fact more useful before it was cut into long strips. It could have been used to make a nice coat, for example.

29805.name: bolt of grade 2 skybuilders' cloth
29805.col_2: As the popular Coerthan adage attests, “One can never have too much cloth.”

29806.name: phial of grade 2 skybuilders' plant oil
29806.description: phials of grade 2 skybuilders' plant oil
29806.col_2: Not only is it used by chefs, but also masseuses. Unfortunately, there is not much call for such work in Ishgard, as the general consensus is that clothes are best kept on at all times unless absolutely necessary.

29807.name: loaf of grade 2 skybuilders' bread
29807.col_2: While it is true that man cannot live on bread alone, a little bit here and there certainly does not go amiss.

29808.name: grade 2 skybuilders' grindstone
29808.col_2: Clearly, the expression “nose to the grindstone” was not meant to be taken literally, though some have chosen to find this out the hard way.

29809.name: grade 2 skybuilders' hammer
29809.col_2: Tenderizing pork with this craftsman's tool does not, as one might be forgiven for thinking given the name, turn it into ham.

29810.name: grade 2 skybuilders' still
29810.col_2: This bizarre contraption is coveted by alchemists and culinarians alike. When asked for what purpose, the response is generally along the lines of, “Mumble, mumble, steam, mumble, mumble.”

29811.name: grade 2 skybuilders' embroidery frame
29811.col_2: A firm favorite among ladies of leisure, oft held mid-stitch as they gaze wistfully from the window of their opulent bedchamber, high in their metaphorical─and in some cases, actual─ivory tower.

29812.name: grade 2 skybuilders' rug
29812.col_2: Some things are best swept under one of these.

29813.name: grade 2 skybuilders' broom
29813.col_2: Those expecting this perfectly ordinary broom to start speaking backwards or sweeping floors of its own accord will be disappointed to find it does neither, unless a passing witch is in the mood for a couple of incantations.

29814.name: pot of grade 2 skybuilders' dye
29814.col_2: Those thinking about using this colorful dye for their own purposes should put such thoughts aside, as it is strictly for skybuilder use only. After all, one can hardly expect them to go about their work deprived of the ability to turn something purple at a moment's notice.

29815.name: cup of grade 2 skybuilders' tea
29815.col_2: Skybuilders have garnered a reputation for punctuating their work with frequent tea breaks. The number of cups drunk by a laborer over the course of a single day can easily reach double digits.

29816.name: grade 2 skybuilders' stepladder
29816.col_2: Unlike most other items requested by the skybuilders, this one actually seems to serve some practical purpose. It can even be carried on one shoulder, allowing the bearer to pivot quickly, which leads to all sorts of hilarity as their colleagues attempt, often in vain, to avoid having their skull cracked.

29817.name: grade 2 skybuilders' crosscut saw
29817.col_2: The sound it makes as it cleaves through timber is akin to that of a person snoring. One particular linguist even went so far as to investigate a possible connection between the words “sawing” and “snoring,” and to no one's surprise but her own, discovered that nothing of the sort exists.

29818.name: grade 2 skybuilders' mesail
29818.col_2: Perfect for protecting one's face from the accusing glares of innocent bystanders during daylight robberies and so forth, although the skybuilders have a far more pedestrian use in mind.

29819.name: grade 2 skybuilders' stone
29819.col_2: A strong contender for the heaviest item requested by the skybuilders. How the volunteers are expected to transport these without an exceedingly sturdy cart is anyone's guess.

29820.name: pair of grade 2 skybuilders' longboots
29820.col_2: As the name implies, these boots are what some might consider long, although longer still are the grade 2 skybuilders' longlongboots.

29821.name: pair of grade 2 skybuilders' gloves
29821.col_2: Keepers of hounds with the tendency to bite the hand that feeds will be delighted to receive a pair of these fine gloves. The smooth lining allows the wearer to slip out easily, leaving said dog with a mouthful of tough leather, which it will soon learn makes a poor substitute for proper food.

29822.name: bar of grade 2 skybuilders' soap
29822.col_2: When combined with an empty stocking, can be used as a makeshift weapon. In Ishgard, this appears to be the most common use, since many residents have discovered that the need to wash is largely mitigated by the wearing of multiple layers of thick clothing, which does little to prevent bodily odor, but does cause it to take longer to seep through and reach the nostrils of those in the immediate vicinity.

29823.name: grade 2 skybuilders' all-purpose infusion
29823.col_2: There may be uncertainty surrounding its exact effects, although one thing is clear: it definitely tastes as if it does one good. That is to say, revolting.

29824.name: grade 2 skybuilders' bed
29824.col_2: As it stands only a few ilms off of the floor, any things that go bump in the night will have trouble squeezing under this particular bed.

29825.name: grade 2 skybuilders' oven
29825.col_2: Complete with raging fire and billowing smoke, which, while impressive, does make it rather troublesome to transport.

29826.name: grade 2 skybuilders' lamppost
29826.col_2: Those with high ceilings in their chambers may wish to employ this as a rather extravagant bedside reading light.

29827.name: grade 2 skybuilders' brazier
29827.col_2: Any meat fried on this outdoor brazier produces smoke with the uncanny ability to find its way into the eyes of those foolish enough to wander too near.

29828.name: set of grade 2 skybuilders' overalls
29828.col_2: Designed to be worn on top of other, nicer clothes. Ideal for those who like to muck out their chocobo stables immediately before going for afternoon tea with an overbearing but wealthy aunt.

29829.name: grade 2 skybuilders' gazebo
29829.col_2: Purpose-built for picnics in the great outdoors, protecting those beneath from any untimely precipitation. Unfortunately, the snow in most parts of Coerthas tends to fall in a rather sideways fashion, thus rendering this gazebo entirely pointless.

29830.name: phial of grade 2 skybuilders' alchemic
29830.col_2: The joy gained from sampling its fragrance─reminiscent of summer meadows─normally only lasts until the caustic vapors burn the skin from the inside of one's nostrils.

29831.name: pot of grade 2 skybuilders' stew
29831.col_2: The term “potluck” applies perfectly to this particular dish, as it is traditionally assembled from whatever the chef can dig up from an often poorly lit pantry. The fact that rats tend to squeak and wriggle a fair bit when picked up is probably all that prevents them from being added to the mix. The dead ones, on the other hand...

29832.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wardrobe
29832.col_2: If, for any reason, one has the need to hide inside, such as the unexpected return of one of the residents and so on, the air holes provided should prevent untimely suffocation. Not that there is such a thing as “timely suffocation.”

29833.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' chandelier
29833.col_2: Most of the diamonds are actually imitations, but thankfully, chandeliers are usually positioned high enough that no one will notice.

29834.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' fireplace
29834.col_2: The ideal place to put a fire, hence the clever name. Well, the last part, that is.

29835.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' bathtub
29835.col_2: In mankind's ongoing quest to keep “water” and “not water” ever separate, few inventions have done more to further the cause than the humble bathtub.

29836.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' overcoat
29836.col_2: If dapperness could be captured, refined, and made into a wearable material, that is what this fine garment would be made from. Until then, cloth and leather will have to suffice.

29837.name: sheet of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wallpaper
29837.description: sheets of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wallpaper
29837.col_2: Generally less messy than covering walls with paint, although its natural tendency to tear and wrinkle with the slightest provocation is enough to make a saint swear.

29838.name: set of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' remedies
29838.description: sets of grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' remedies
29838.col_2: It is assumed that each of these glass phials contains something useful, as none of them are labeled. Identification by taste is probably best left to a professional or someone who is not opposed to being lightly poisoned.

29839.name: grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' quiche
29839.col_2: In cases such as these, “artisanal” actually means “so complex that even the chef doesn't remember what went into it,” hence the impossibility of replicating the recipe.

29840.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' switch
29840.col_2: A sharp rap across the back of the thigh in the cold, crisp Ishgardian morning air with one of these light and flexible branches is a surefire way to blow away the proverbial cobwebs of any workers caught yawning.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29841.name: tuft of approved grade 2 skybuilders' hemp
29841.description: tufts of approved grade 2 skybuilders' hemp
29841.col_2: One can only hope that whatever purpose the skybuilders have in mind for this hardy plant was worth depriving some herbivorous creature of its leafy goodness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29842.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' ore
29842.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' ore
29842.col_2: Something of a mixed bag of metallic elements, but as everyone knows, smithies love a good surprise. Just not when they're swinging a hammer dangerously close to their fingers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29843.name: pinch of approved grade 2 skybuilders' copper sand
29843.description: pinches of approved grade 2 skybuilders' copper sand
29843.col_2: A special place in one of the seven hells exists for those who attempt to fob off the skybuilders by mixing in regular sand with the copper, or so the skybuilders would have one believe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29844.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' maple log
29844.col_2: The sap slowly leaking from the logs tends to attract ants, which even the skybuilders have yet to find a use for. This may come as a surprise considering the plethora of bizarre items they request, and it may only be a matter of time until some bright spark invents ant sandwiches.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29845.name: pot of approved grade 2 skybuilders' maple sap
29845.description: pots of approved grade 2 skybuilders' maple sap
29845.col_2: Any insect foolhardy enough to attempt sampling its delight will invariably find itself trapped within this glutinous substance, preserved for future generations to study and possibly experiment on. Still, there are worse ways to go than being enveloped in one's favorite sweet treat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29846.name: clump of approved grade 2 skybuilders' flax
29846.description: clumps of approved grade 2 skybuilders' flax
29846.col_2: Included in a surprising number of recipes and concoctions despite its only notable property being “it smells nice.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29847.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' zinc ore
29847.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' zinc ore
29847.col_2: Zinc is said to prevent a number of common ailments. However, it must be noted that attempting to ingest it in its current state may actually <hex:021A020203>cause<hex:021A020103> problems such as broken teeth and stomachache, usually in that order.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29848.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' rock salt
29848.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' rock salt
29848.col_2: There are few dishes that cannot be improved with a sprinkling of salt. Strangely, this even includes a number of desserts, which flies in the face of all common logic.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29849.name: pinch of approved grade 2 skybuilders' iron sand
29849.description: pinches of approved grade 2 skybuilders' iron sand
29849.col_2: In the event that one somehow accidentally mixes this with normal sand, the two can be separated by waving a magnet nearby. This knowledge may─or more likely, may not─save your life one day.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29850.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' teak log
29850.col_2: Although such logs are the perfect material for fashioning rafts and canoes, the distinctly frozen bodies of water that surround Ishgard scupper the locals' chances of enjoying the pleasures of boating.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29851.name: sprig of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mistletoe
29851.description: sprigs of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mistletoe
29851.col_2: Any ancient myths describing darts made from a sprig of mistletoe neglect to mention the fact that when thrown, it displays the airborne grace of a drunken, one-winged chicken.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29852.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' beehive
29852.col_2: A bee colony will often respond to the presence of intruders by swarming their intended target and using their own body heat to cook it alive. The skybuilders have discovered that this can be utilized to keep their hands warm, although the fact that said bees are still very much capable of stinging does present a minor flaw in this otherwise brilliant idea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29853.name: bundle of approved grade 2 skybuilders' straw
29853.description: bundles of approved grade 2 skybuilders' straw
29853.col_2: In some parts of Eorzea, straw is used to weave hats with wide peaks to keep the sun from the wearer's eyes. Fortunately─or perhaps unfortunately─for Ishgardians, there is seldom enough sunlight to warrant such headwear, and the vicious winds would prevent the owner from remaining behatted for more than a few scant moments.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29854.name: basket of approved grade 2 skybuilders' tea leaves
29854.description: baskets of approved grade 2 skybuilders' tea leaves
29854.col_2: For Ishgardians, discussing the virtues of various blends of tea is almost as much of a pastime as actually drinking the stuff. This fine selection of choice leaves could be placed in the center of a table to serve to facilitate stimulating conversation, while the skybuilders continue to labor away in the bitter cold outside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29855.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' cobalt ore
29855.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' cobalt ore
29855.col_2: A lot less blue than one might expect, although it tastes about right.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29856.name: lump of approved grade 2 skybuilders' pigment
29856.description: lumps of approved grade 2 skybuilders' pigment
29856.col_2: While some of the skybuilders were in favor of naming this substance “purple stuff,” the need to follow a more sensible naming convention eventually prevailed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29857.name: pot of approved grade 2 skybuilders' asphaltum
29857.description: pots of approved grade 2 skybuilders' asphaltum
29857.col_2: Plans to use this sticky, black substance to cover the streets of Ishgard were vehemently opposed, as it would ruin the uniformly grey aesthetic─which on most days includes the sky itself.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29858.name: pinch of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mythril sand
29858.description: pinches of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mythril sand
29858.col_2: The bright hue of this valuable substance does make it stand out from the surrounding rocks and so forth, but only under the condition that one is able to find the damnable stuff in the first place.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29859.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mica
29859.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mica
29859.col_2: “Mica” would make rather a nice name for a person, if it were not already taken by this rather unremarkable rock.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29860.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' oak log
29860.col_2: The tiny acorn that grew into this mighty oak had its life cut tragically short by the cruel axe of a woodsman (or possibly woodslady). If there is any justice in the world, it will be born anew as a nice dresser or an attractive hat stand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29861.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' feather
29861.col_2: While even Ishgard's finest ornithologist would be hard-pressed to identify the bird from which this came, one thing is certain: there are more where this came from, unless said bird only ever possessed a single feather.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29862.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' vine
29862.col_2: Careless owners of high-walled castles in faerie tales often allow these to grow over said walls, thereby allowing dashing heroes to infiltrate the premises to steal jewels, damsels in distress, scones from the pantry, and so forth.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29863.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' toad
29863.col_2: One skybuilder was heard to claim that to assign grades to living creatures is degrading. The response was, “No, taking the grade away from it would be called degrading.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29864.name: clump of approved grade 2 skybuilders' barbgrass
29864.description: clumps of approved grade 2 skybuilders' barbgrass
29864.col_2: According to local legend, a night raid on a Temple Knights encampment was foiled when the assailants wandered into a patch of barbgrass. Nothing gives the game away quite like pained squeals of, “Oh, my poor bottom!”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29865.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mythrite ore
29865.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' mythrite ore
29865.col_2: Due to the fact it is almost identical in appearance to mythril ore, it is sometimes known as “fool's mythril.” Conversely, actual mythril is often referred to as “fool's mythrite.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29866.name: bottle of approved grade 2 skybuilders' spring water
29866.description: bottles of approved grade 2 skybuilders' spring water
29866.col_2: Despite the potentially misleading name, it can also be collected in summer and autumn. Winter, however, is generally out of the question, for obvious reasons.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29867.name: pinch of approved grade 2 skybuilders' alumen
29867.description: pinches of approved grade 2 skybuilders' alumen
29867.col_2: Were the skybuilders less exacting in their demands, the standard alumen found in market stalls across Eorzea would be more than sufficient. Many volunteers suspect that such tasks are set merely to test their patience.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29868.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' rock
29868.col_2: If you think this rock is uninteresting, you should see the grade 1 skybuilders' rock, which is so plain that it can blend into any background by virtue of its sheer dullness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29869.name: sack of approved grade 2 skybuilders' silex
29869.description: sacks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' silex
29869.col_2: The name makes it sound far more sinister than it actually is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29870.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' walnut log
29870.col_2: Think of all the walnuts that could have grown on this tree had it not been cut down! Walnuts for breakfast, walnuts for elevenses, walnuts for luncheon... The possibilities were endless.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29871.name: lump of approved grade 2 skybuilders' resin
29871.description: lumps of approved grade 2 skybuilders' resin
29871.col_2: Resin this pure, this beautiful is far too good for the skybuilders. Perhaps you should keep it all to yourself. They need never know.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29872.name: sheaf of approved grade 2 skybuilders' wheat
29872.description: sheaves of approved grade 2 skybuilders' wheat
29872.col_2: There is a possibility that some grade 1 wheat slipped in by mistake.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29873.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' cotton boll
29873.col_2: One of the skybuilder's children asked, “Is this what sheep are made from?” The answer was a resounding, “I'm not sure. Possibly.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29874.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' adder
29874.col_2: Venomous, but not fatally so. Perfect for practical jokes and party tricks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29875.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' darksteel ore
29875.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' darksteel ore
29875.col_2: Has the potential to be made into something very scary indeed, like spiked pauldrons or an enormous battleaxe. In all likelihood, however, it will probably become a slightly extravagant kettle or decorative letter opener.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29876.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' crystal-clear rock salt
29876.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' crystal-clear rock salt
29876.col_2: With a name that long, one might be forgiven for expecting it to be some sort of miraculous super-salt, capable of turning even the blandest dish into a festival of flavor. Sadly, this is not the case, although it is nonetheless rather good as far as salt goes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
29876.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Skybuilders' Crystal-clear Rock Salt

29877.name: bottle of approved grade 2 skybuilders' cloud drop water
29877.description: bottles of approved grade 2 skybuilders' cloud drop water
29877.col_2: Most people realize “cloud drop” is just a fancy way to say “rain.” Not many customers would be willing to pay for mere rainwater, but cloud drop water, on the other hand...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
29877.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Skybuilders' Cloud Drop Water

29878.name: pinch of approved grade 2 skybuilders' lutinite
29878.description: pinches of approved grade 2 skybuilders' lutinite
29878.col_2: Said to be blessed by cloud spirits, which may or may not be a good thing. Still, “blessed” is infinitely preferable to “cursed.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29879.name: chunk of approved grade 2 skybuilders' basalt
29879.description: chunks of approved grade 2 skybuilders' basalt
29879.col_2: Basalt actually has very little in common with salt, despite its name being approximately two-thirds the same.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29880.name: approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' log
29880.col_2: As the skybuilders prefer to use wooden planks of standardized dimensions, this log is already cut to be exactly the length they require, to minimize the carpenters' workload. One can only hope they appreciate the extra effort by throwing a few more scrips your way.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29881.name: lump of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' hardened sap
29881.description: lumps of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' hardened sap
29881.col_2: Although the practical applications of a piece of hardened sap are somewhat unclear, it is at least considerably less sticky than unhardened sap, which helps to keep it free of impurities such as loose hairs, bits of pocket fluff, and so on.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29881.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Hardened Sap

29882.name: sheaf of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wheat
29882.description: sheaves of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' wheat
29882.col_2: What about this wheat makes it artisanal? Those in the know claim it is massaged daily and fed beer, which is the reason for the delicious marbled texture. Or perhaps they were talking about some sort of cow?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29883.name: approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cotton boll
29883.description: approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cotton bolls
29883.col_2: To the untrained eye, this may appear to be no different from any other cotton boll. Those with <hex:021A020203>trained<hex:021A020103> eyes, however, will notice that it is pink, not the usual white.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29883.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Cotton Boll

29884.name: approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' dawn lizard
29884.description: approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' dawn lizards
29884.col_2: Those wondering what separates this from a non-artisanal dawn lizard need only observe the way it devours its prey. For a carnivorous, slavering scalekin, it has the most impeccable table manners, or more precisely, “blood-spattered patch of ground manners.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29884.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Dawn Lizard

29885.name: chunk of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
29885.description: chunks of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
29885.col_2: Believed to be a piece of fossilized cloud.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29886.name: chunk of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' rock salt
29886.description: chunks of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' rock salt
29886.col_2: It seems there are almost as many varieties of rock salt as there are varieties of rock, if the skybuilders' somewhat arbitrary system of assigning names is to be believed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29886.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Rock Salt

29887.name: bottle of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
29887.description: bottles of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
29887.col_2: Rather than simply being free of impurities, this water actually possesses the ability to preemptively destroy any impurities that dare to come near it. As such, only those pure of heart can drink of it without being killed instantly, or so it is rumored.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29887.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Spring Water

29888.name: pinch of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' aurum regis sand
29888.description: pinches of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' aurum regis sand
29888.col_2: One of the few substances known to be both edible and highly explosive. While some spicy ingredients are said to be capable of blowing one's head off, in this case, it is no exaggeration.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29888.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Artisanal Skybuilders' Aurum Regis Sand

29889.name: chunk of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' jade
29889.description: chunks of approved grade 2 artisanal skybuilders' jade
29889.col_2: In the Brume, to be “jaded” means to have a large piece of jade thrown at the back of one's head. Thankfully, the prohibitive pricing of this precious substance means that such incidents are rare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29890.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' umbral galewood log
29890.description: approved grade 2 skybuilders' umbral galewood logs
29890.col_2: Carried on raging winds, charged with potent aether. Probably the most powerful log in existence.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral tempest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
29890.col_3: Approved Grade 2 Skybuilders' Umbral Galewood Log

29891.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' umbral earthcap
29891.col_2: Charged with aether drawn from the earth. In actual fact, most mushrooms possess some earth-aspected aether, but this particular species is especially greedy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral duststorm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29892.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' umbral flarestone
29892.col_2: Red-hot to the touch, which makes it a bastard to carry.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral flare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29893.name: approved grade 2 skybuilders' umbral levinshard
29893.col_2: If you thought catching lightning in a bottle was difficult, catching it in a crystal fragment is even trickier. At least a bottle comes with a handy cap to keep in said lightning when caught, whereas crystal relies on nothing more than the bolt's willing cooperation.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during umbral levin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

29894.name: grade 2 skybuilders' switch
29894.col_2: A sharp rap across the back of the thigh in the cold, crisp Ishgardian morning air with one of these light and flexible branches is a surefire way to blow away the proverbial cobwebs of any workers caught yawning.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29895.name: tuft of grade 2 skybuilders' hemp
29895.col_2: One can only hope that whatever purpose the skybuilders have in mind for this hardy plant was worth depriving some herbivorous creature of its leafy goodness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29896.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' ore
29896.col_2: Something of a mixed bag of metallic elements, but as everyone knows, smithies love a good surprise. Just not when they're swinging a hammer dangerously close to their fingers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29897.name: pinch of grade 2 skybuilders' copper sand
29897.description: pinches of grade 2 skybuilders' copper sand
29897.col_2: A special place in one of the seven hells exists for those who attempt to fob off the skybuilders by mixing in regular sand with the copper, or so the skybuilders would have one believe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29898.name: grade 2 skybuilders' maple log
29898.col_2: The sap slowly leaking from the logs tends to attract ants, which even the skybuilders have yet to find a use for. This may come as a surprise considering the plethora of bizarre items they request, and it may only be a matter of time until some bright spark invents ant sandwiches.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29899.name: pot of grade 2 skybuilders' maple sap
29899.description: pots of grade 2 skybuilders' maple sap
29899.col_2: Any insect foolhardy enough to attempt sampling its delight will invariably find itself trapped within this glutinous substance, preserved for future generations to study and possibly experiment on. Still, there are worse ways to go than being enveloped in one's favorite sweet treat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29900.name: clump of grade 2 skybuilders' flax
29900.col_2: Included in a surprising number of recipes and concoctions despite its only notable property being “it smells nice.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29901.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' zinc ore
29901.description: chunks of grade 2 skybuilders' zinc ore
29901.col_2: Zinc is said to prevent a number of common ailments. However, it must be noted that attempting to ingest it in its current state may actually <hex:021A020203>cause<hex:021A020103> problems such as broken teeth and stomachache, usually in that order.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29902.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' rock salt
29902.description: chunks of grade 2 skybuilders' rock salt
29902.col_2: There are few dishes that cannot be improved with a sprinkling of salt. Strangely, this even includes a number of desserts, which flies in the face of all common logic.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29903.name: pinch of grade 2 skybuilders' iron sand
29903.description: pinches of grade 2 skybuilders' iron sand
29903.col_2: In the event that one somehow accidentally mixes this with normal sand, the two can be separated by waving a magnet nearby. This knowledge may─or more likely, may not─save your life one day.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29904.name: grade 2 skybuilders' teak log
29904.col_2: Although such logs are the perfect material for fashioning rafts and canoes, the distinctly frozen bodies of water that surround Ishgard scupper the locals' chances of enjoying the pleasures of boating.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29905.name: sprig of grade 2 skybuilders' mistletoe
29905.col_2: Any ancient myths describing darts made from a sprig of mistletoe neglect to mention the fact that when thrown, it displays the airborne grace of a drunken, one-winged chicken.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29906.name: grade 2 skybuilders' beehive
29906.col_2: A bee colony will often respond to the presence of intruders by swarming their intended target and using their own body heat to cook it alive. The skybuilders have discovered that this can be utilized to keep their hands warm, although the fact that said bees are still very much capable of stinging does present a minor flaw in this otherwise brilliant idea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29907.name: bundle of grade 2 skybuilders' straw
29907.col_2: In some parts of Eorzea, straw is used to weave hats with wide peaks to keep the sun from the wearer's eyes. Fortunately─or perhaps unfortunately─for Ishgardians, there is seldom enough sunlight to warrant such headwear, and the vicious winds would prevent the owner from remaining behatted for more than a few scant moments.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29908.name: basket of grade 2 skybuilders' tea leaves
29908.description: baskets of grade 2 skybuilders' tea leaves
29908.col_2: For Ishgardians, discussing the virtues of various blends of tea is almost as much of a pastime as actually drinking the stuff. This fine selection of choice leaves could be placed in the center of a table to serve to facilitate stimulating conversation, while the skybuilders continue to labor away in the bitter cold outside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29909.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' cobalt ore
29909.description: chunks of grade 2 skybuilders' cobalt ore
29909.col_2: A lot less blue than one might expect, although it tastes about right.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29910.name: lump of grade 2 skybuilders' pigment
29910.col_2: While some of the skybuilders were in favor of naming this substance “purple stuff,” the need to follow a more sensible naming convention eventually prevailed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29911.name: pot of grade 2 skybuilders' asphaltum
29911.col_2: Plans to use this sticky, black substance to cover the streets of Ishgard were vehemently opposed, as it would ruin the uniformly grey aesthetic─which on most days includes the sky itself.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29912.name: pinch of grade 2 skybuilders' mythril sand
29912.description: pinches of grade 2 skybuilders' mythril sand
29912.col_2: The bright hue of this valuable substance does make it stand out from the surrounding rocks and so forth, but only under the condition that one is able to find the damnable stuff in the first place.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29913.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' mica
29913.col_2: “Mica” would make rather a nice name for a person, if it were not already taken by this rather unremarkable rock.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29914.name: grade 2 skybuilders' oak log
29914.col_2: The tiny acorn that grew into this mighty oak had its life cut tragically short by the cruel axe of a woodsman (or possibly woodslady). If there is any justice in the world, it will be born anew as a nice dresser or an attractive hat stand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29915.name: grade 2 skybuilders' feather
29915.col_2: While even Ishgard's finest ornithologist would be hard-pressed to identify the bird from which this came, one thing is certain: there are more where this came from, unless said bird only ever possessed a single feather.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29916.name: grade 2 skybuilders' vine
29916.col_2: Careless owners of high-walled castles in faerie tales often allow these to grow over said walls, thereby allowing dashing heroes to infiltrate the premises to steal jewels, damsels in distress, scones from the pantry, and so forth.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29917.name: grade 2 skybuilders' toad
29917.col_2: One skybuilder was heard to claim that to assign grades to living creatures is degrading. The response was, “No, taking the grade away from it would be called degrading.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29918.name: clump of grade 2 skybuilders' barbgrass
29918.col_2: According to local legend, a night raid on a Temple Knights encampment was foiled when the assailants wandered into a patch of barbgrass. Nothing gives the game away quite like pained squeals of, “Oh, my poor bottom!”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29919.name: chunk of grade 2 skybuilders' mythrite ore
29919.description: chunks of grade 2 skybuilders' mythrite ore
29919.col_2: Due to the fact it is almost identical in appearance to mythril ore, it is sometimes known as “fool's mythril.” Conversely, actual mythril is often referred to as “fool's mythrite.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29920.name: bottle of grade 2 skybuilders' spring water
29920.description: bottles of grade 2 skybuilders' spring water
29920.col_2: Despite the potentially misleading name, it can also be collected in summer and autumn. Winter, however, is generally out of the question, for obvious reasons.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29922.col_2: If you think this rock is uninteresting, you should see the grade 1 skybuilders' rock, which is so plain that it can blend into any background by virtue of its sheer dullness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29923.col_2: The name makes it sound far more sinister than it actually is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29924.col_2: Think of all the walnuts that could have grown on this tree had it not been cut down! Walnuts for breakfast, walnuts for elevenses, walnuts for luncheon... The possibilities were endless.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29925.name: lump of grade 2 skybuilders' resin
29925.col_2: Resin this pure, this beautiful is far too good for the skybuilders. Perhaps you should keep it all to yourself. They need never know.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29926.col_2: There is a possibility that some grade 1 wheat slipped in by mistake.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29928.col_2: Venomous, but not fatally so. Perfect for practical jokes and party tricks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
