31060.col_2: “The more exotic the beast, the more likely someone has tanned its hide to make a spellbook. This one is archaeoskin, doubly bound.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31061.name: rarefied archaeoskin codex
31061.col_2: Some scholars will spare no expense─nor fantastic beast─to obtain protective covers for their tomes. <hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31062.name: bottle of rarefied dissolvent
31062.col_2: When the rarest of artifacts must be cleansed of impurities, only the rarest of dissolvent will suffice.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31063.name: rarefied dhalmelskin codex
31063.col_2: Hopefully the rest of the dhalmel didn't go to waste.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31064.name: rarefied max-potion
31064.col_2: What theoretical maximum could a max-potion reach if a max-potion could theoretically be maximized?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31065.name: rarefied book of aurum regis
31065.col_2: There are “noble” metals, and then there's aurum regis. Some collectors need to be the king.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31066.name: rarefied koppranickel index
31066.col_2: “I'd <hex:021A020203>like<hex:021A020103> to put it down before I eat, but I seem to have impaled a finger...”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31067.name: bottle of rarefied reisui
31067.col_2: Try not to lose it amongst the regular bottles of reisui─that's an amateur's mistake.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31068.name: rarefied tigerskin grimoire
31068.col_2: Though crafted with materials of indisputable quality, many quietly consider the quill clasp on the back cover to be its greatest feature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31069.name: bottle of rarefied growth formula
31069.col_2: When the pumpkin-growing crown is at stake, sometimes you need that little extra edge.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31070.name: rarefied gazelleskin codex
31070.col_2: An elegant and sturdy volume, with attachments to store both quill and ink. Practical!<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31071.name: rarefied bottle of alkahest
31071.col_2: “Dissolvent and reisui are all very well and good, but a true professional settles for nothing less than the highest quality alkahest.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31072.name: rarefied gliderskin grimoire
31072.col_2: Cracking open this tome is akin to swinging wide the gate to a lush garden of secrets.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31073.name: rarefied bluespirit codex
31073.col_2: “I almost regret buying this one. It feels like all the other books are jealous.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31074.name: dose of rarefied syrup
31074.col_2: For when you absolutely, positively must not mess up that synthesis.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31075.name: serving of rarefied dhalmel gratin
31075.col_2: Made with the choicest cuts and creamiest of sauces. Try not to burn your tongue.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31076.name: rarefied Sohm Al tart
31076.col_2: This most mountainous of tarts will satisfy even the most famished of dragonslayers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31077.name: serving of rarefied sauteed porcini
31077.col_2: This fragrantly perfect dish would take pride of place next to the greatest trophies of war...if it weren't for that inconvenient rotting business.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31078.name: serving of rarefied royal eggs
31078.col_2: You don't have to be royal to enjoy this delectable breakfast, but being friends with the royal culinarian might help.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31079.name: serving of rarefied peperoncino
31079.col_2: The extra spicy kick in these noodles will propel you through a difficult battle...or an afternoon with your future spouse's parents.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31080.name: serving of rarefied marron glace
31080.col_2: You might think a chestnut soaked in any other honey would taste as sweet...but this is even sweeter.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31081.name: serving of rarefied baklava
31081.col_2: In the words of a famous djinn, “How 'bout a little more Baklava?”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31082.name: serving of rarefied shorlog
31082.col_2: A tantalizing skewer of dzo meat fit for a khan.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31083.name: rarefied tempura platter
31083.col_2: It's the lightly fried batter which makes this platter better.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31084.name: serving of rarefied persimmon pudding
31084.col_2: A single bite of this steamed dessert will reaffirm your belief in the divine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31085.name: serving of rarefied chirashi-zushi
31085.col_2: Commonly eaten during celebrations, it is this dish which will be celebrated by salivating gourmands.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31086.name: serving of rarefied grilled rail
31086.col_2: You wonder if some culinary critic awaits this succulent delight, table set and waiting by the nearest convenient aetheryte...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31087.name: serving of rarefied spaghetti al nero
31087.description: servings of rarefied spaghetti al nero
31087.col_2: “So tired of golden noodles, I want them to turn black.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31088.name: serving of rarefied popotoes au gratin
31088.description: servings of rarefied popotoes au gratin
31088.col_2: Popotoes? Mash 'em, boil 'em, stick them in a pot with a distinctive cream cheese sauce.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31089.name: cup of rarefied espresso con panna
31089.description: cups of rarefied espresso con panna
31089.col_2: “Do not speak to me before I've had my espresso con panna.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31090.name: bottle of weathering agent
31090.col_2: This corrosive concoction rusts and breaks down metal. Judicious application is key if it is to be used for aesthetic purposes.

31091.name: bolt of seacloth
31091.col_2: So named for its origin among the isles of the southern seas, this fabric's unique loose weave has yet to be replicated elsewhere.

31101.name: length of oddly specific cedar lumber
31101.description: lengths of oddly specific cedar lumber
31101.col_2: Must be cut within twenty paces of a lark's call, beneath a double rainbow.

31102.name: box of oddly specific iron nails
31102.description: boxes of oddly specific iron nails
31102.col_2: Each and every nail must produce a sound akin to a Starlight Celebration chime when dropped from a height of precisely fourteen and a half ilms.

31103.name: handful of oddly specific mythril rings
31103.description: handfuls of oddly specific mythril rings
31103.col_2: The requirement that each ring be the same size does not seem to be especially odd or specific at first, but such opinions soon change upon realizing they must be crafted while blindfolded.

31104.name: oddly specific silver nugget
31104.col_2: Each specimen must have precisely the correct amount of nuggetiness.

31105.name: spool of oddly specific gaganaskin strap
31105.description: spools of oddly specific gaganaskin strap
31105.col_2: The entire strap must be made from a single piece of skin, and being over a malm in length, is something of a tall order. Or long order, to be more precise.

31106.name: piece of oddly specific cloth
31106.col_2: Though the Skysteel Manufactory staff were oddly specific regarding the material itself, this odd level of specificity did not extend to its name, which is oddly unspecific.

31107.name: block of oddly specific glue
31107.col_2: Most glues are designed to be used on certain types of material, whereas this sort is specifically meant to glue everything to everything else, including any container one may choose to place it in. This can make transporting it somewhat troublesome.

31108.name: bottle of oddly specific oil
31108.col_2: While the instructions relating to the oil itself were not particularly specific, the bottle must be made from glass expertly crafted in the light of a full moon and blessed by forest spirits. Luckily, those conditions cannot be easily verified, and can therefore be ignored.

31109.name: oddly specific cedar plank
31109.col_2: One may be forgiven that an entire plank of anything is probably too much raw material for any sort of artisan's tool.

31110.name: oddly specific iron ingot
31110.col_2: The exact number of hammer blows used in its forging was specified by the Skysteel Manufactory's staff, but an extra tap here and there will likely go unnoticed.

31111.name: sheet of oddly specific mythril plate
31111.description: sheets of oddly specific mythril plate
31111.col_2: The instructions regarding the exact dimensions of each sheet were annoyingly specific, though one should be thankful that they did not request plates of mythril sheet, which are considerably more troublesome to craft.

31112.name: oddly specific silver ingot
31112.col_2: Considering that this ingot will inevitably be melted and hit repeatedly with hammers and so forth, the effort spent on making it look pretty seems rather pointless.

31113.name: circle of oddly specific gagana leather
31113.description: circles of oddly specific gagana leather
31113.col_2: The gagana itself must come from good stock, supposedly, though such wild creatures are not in the habit of keeping detailed records of their lineage.

31114.name: bolt of oddly specific undyed woolen cloth
31114.description: bolts of oddly specific undyed woolen cloth
31114.col_2: Given the number of steps needed for the wool to reach this state, the possibility of a near-endless list of oddly specific instructions would be enough to deter all but the most stalwart of artisans. In the end, however, the Skysteel Manufactory staff asked only that it be “free from any artificial colorings,” which is presumably what the “undyed” part of its name implies.

31115.name: chunk of oddly specific rubber
31115.col_2: The procurement of this rubbery specimen did not differ significantly from that of lesser varieties, though the manner in which it is handled before use tends to raise eyebrows. It must be thrown against a wall with an overarm motion, and then bounce exactly three and a half times before being caught in a bowl of hot porridge.

31116.name: pinch of oddly specific paste
31116.col_2: Great pains must be taken while mixing to ensure the paste does not end up as a semi-liquid, or even worse, a liquid.

31117.name: oddly specific cedar log
31117.col_2: Must include the initials of star-crossed lovers carved into the bark. The Skysteel engineers will know if you have carved them yourself, especially if you use your own initials.

31118.name: chunk of oddly specific Coerthan iron ore
31118.description: chunks of oddly specific Coerthan iron ore
31118.col_2: As if specifying the location from which it is mined was not enough, the Skysteel engineers have also asked that you carry it about your person while walking an entire lap around Ishgard, so that it may soak up the local atmosphere.

31119.name: pinch of oddly specific mythrite sand
31119.description: pinches of oddly specific mythrite sand
31119.col_2: Each pinch must contain mythrite and only mythrite, which in the grand scheme of things, seems perfectly reasonable.

31120.name: chunk of oddly specific silver ore
31120.description: chunks of oddly specific silver ore
31120.col_2: The ore requested must be “similar in appearance to gold, but with more of a light-grey tinge to it.” Silver, in other words.

31121.name: oddly specific gagana skin
31121.col_2: Each gagana must be treated with the utmost care and allowed to live a life of uninterrupted bliss, right up until the moment they are brutally slaughtered.

31122.name: basket of oddly specific fleece
31122.col_2: The fleece must be soft enough that one can put their hand into the basket and not be able to feel a thing─except for the inside of said basket.

31123.name: pot of oddly specific sap
31123.col_2: Before use, it should be shaken, stirred, shaken again, and then poured down a gagana's gullet and regurgitated, as tradition dictates.

31124.name: portion of oddly specific aloe
31124.col_2: Should only be harvested after being lightly dusted by the scales of an endangered species of moth, which also has its own set of oddly specific requirements.

31125.name: oddly specific dark chestnut log
31125.col_2: Oddly enough, all of the specific requirements relate to the wood's aroma, which is strange considering it will most likely be covered in several layers of varnish, thereby obfuscating the original scent.

31126.name: pinch of oddly specific leafborne aethersand
31126.description: pinches of oddly specific leafborne aethersand
31126.col_2: The original request was simply for green sand, which does not actually leave that many options.

31127.name: chunk of oddly specific schorl
31127.col_2: Schorl is already in and of itself rather a specific thing to request, and it is somewhat surprising to find that it would play a significant part in improving an artisan's tool of the trade.

31128.name: pinch of oddly specific landborne aethersand
31128.description: pinches of oddly specific landborne aethersand
31128.col_2: While sand that is “borne by the land” is actually rather commonplace, the part about it being aetherially charged does make its procurement quite a challenge.

31129.name: petal shell
31129.col_2: Sometimes mistaken for underwater flowers, though sadly, the aroma they produce is far less pleasant.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be caught when equipped with a dragonsung fishing rod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

31130.name: oddly specific primordial log
31130.col_2: The last remains of a great arboreal pillar, as old as time, that once towered over the earliest forms of life at the world's beginning. Smells a bit funny.

31131.name: lump of oddly specific primordial resin
31131.description: lumps of oddly specific primordial resin
31131.col_2: The passing of time has rendered this once translucent jewel of the forest as opaque as obsidian. In fact, it may very well be an ordinary stone.

31132.name: chunk of oddly specific primordial ore
31132.description: chunks of oddly specific primordial ore
31132.col_2: Even among its rocky brethren, this specimen is especially ancient, having weathered the passing of ages, and is regarded as the grandfather of all stones. Well, not literally, that would be impossible for reasons far too complex to explain here. Or anywhere, for that matter.

31133.name: pot of oddly specific primordial asphaltum
31133.description: pots of oddly specific primordial asphaltum
31133.col_2: The perfect substance for scalekin to dive into and enjoy a good frolic. Of course, it is all fun and games until someone gets dragged down and preserved for future generations to excavate.

31134.name: Allagan hunter
31134.col_2: Its aggressive temperament have ensured its place near the top of the food chain, although much of this aggression is directed at its own species. In a sense, the Allagan hunter is its own worst enemy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be caught when equipped with an augmented dragonsung fishing rod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

31136.name: sack of workshop materials
31136.col_2: Even in their present state, this mishmash of materials exudes a decidedly workshop-like aroma, meaning it smells like puddles of grease and sweaty armpits.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31137.name: crate of workshop supplies
31137.col_2: Contains vital pieces of the puzzle that is Ronitt's workshop. Unfortunately, you are not privy to the details surrounding their assembly, though rather than being some closely guarded secret, it is largely due to the fact that Ronitt is hopeless when it comes to adequately explaining anything.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31138.name: sack of brewery materials
31138.col_2: These raw materials represent the first stage of a rather lengthy and complicated process by which the production of ale somehow expedites the completion of a series of war machines. Rather than stopping to consider the many, many flaws in this plan, you would be better off blindly obeying orders, or so your dwarven companions have conditioned you to believe.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31139.name: crate of brewery supplies
31139.col_2: A selection of parts and materials needed to build a brewery in the traditional Gogg style. That is to say, immediately adjacent to a place where heavy engineering takes place, thereby enabling the workers to drink themselves silly whenever it pleases them.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31140.name: sack of crystal cannon materials
31140.col_2: As great oaks from little acorns grow, so too do crystal cannons from little sacks full of random junk grow. All it takes is a little bit of elbow grease.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31141.name: crate of crystal cannon supplies
31141.col_2: The various components and concoctions contained within this crate will one day go on to form some of the most advanced weaponry in Norvrandt. No doubt the crate itself will look back on this time as one of the highlights of its career.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31142.name: sack of workshop expansion materials
31142.col_2: One would be forgiven for thinking that the materials needed to expand the workshop would be exactly the same as those used to build it in the first place, but apparently not. Heavens forbid that Ronitt make anyone else's life easy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31143.name: crate of workshop expansion supplies
31143.col_2: While it seems that the production of the supplies within this crate could have been delegated to any one of the skilled engineers of Watts's Anvil, you alone have been chosen for this most prestigious of positions. Most prestigious among Ronitt's lackeys, that is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31144.name: sack of automaton worker materials
31144.col_2: If all goes according to plan, the contents of this sack may go on to join such illustrious company as the Megasonic Frogboy or the Fetchomatic Mechatoad, royalty among automata.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31145.name: crate of automaton worker supplies
31145.col_2: Do automata dream of electric frogs? Those made from the contents of this crate certainly will not, as their every “thought” will be devoted only to the production of tank after tank, never to so much as rest, let alone dream.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31146.name: set of armament repair kit materials
31146.description: sets of armament repair kit materials
31146.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for putting together a specialized armament repair kit.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31147.name: armament repair kit
31147.col_2: This repair kit contains specialized items for the maintenance and mending of soldierly equipment.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31148.name: set of grooming kit materials
31148.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for preparing a grooming kit for dwarven beards.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31149.name: grooming kit
31149.col_2: This grooming kit contains items essential to a dwarf's beardcare routine.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31150.name: set of core tank component materials
31150.description: sets of core tank component materials
31150.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a vitally important tank component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31151.name: core tank component
31151.col_2: This vitally important tank component is sure to impress even the most demanding dwarven engineer.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31152.name: set of axle component materials
31152.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating an axle component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31153.name: axle component
31153.col_2: A component that can make the axles of the bulkiest tank turn as quietly as a mouse.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31154.name: set of blueprint materials
31154.col_2: Blueprints are generally simple to get started, but the dwarves of the Anvil demand materials of the highest quality.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31155.name: set of blueprint supplies
31155.col_2: Blueprints are among the most prized possessions in the Anvil, and many dwarves will guard their own designs as jealously as they would a tankard of ale.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31156.name: set of steel plate component materials
31156.description: sets of steel plate component materials
31156.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a steel plate component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31157.name: steel plate component
31157.col_2: The production of steel plates involves much more than an ingot and some fire, as can be plainly seen by the complexity of this component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31158.name: set of cask component materials
31158.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a cask component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31159.name: cask component
31159.col_2: Only the choicest of materials are used in these casks, for many dwarves would rather see their own blood spilt than a single drop of ale.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31160.name: set of engine component materials
31160.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating an engine component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31161.name: engine component
31161.col_2: The engine is the heart of a tank, and must be maintained with as much care as the heart of any living, breathing being.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31162.name: sack of filtration materials
31162.col_2: Filtration is a delicate science; one which often requires a long process of trial and error and, as a consequence, sacks and sacks of materials.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31163.name: set of filtration supplies
31163.col_2: Science can only be perfected through a long series of experiments, which require a steady stream of supplies. Or in this case, a parcel of them.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31164.name: set of cooling device component materials
31164.description: sets of cooling device component materials
31164.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a cooling device component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31165.name: cooling device component
31165.col_2: An overheated tank is no use to anyone.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31166.name: sack of tavern supplies
31166.col_2: Everything required to make a tavern worthy of the most discerning lush.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31167.name: set of tavern materials
31167.col_2: Even dwarven taverns face plenty of competition, so every material used in its construction must be of the utmost quality.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31168.name: set of heat-resistant component materials
31168.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a heat-resistant tank component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31169.name: heat-resistant component
31169.col_2: A tank component capable of withstanding high temperatures.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31170.name: set of bespoke barter item materials
31170.description: sets of bespoke barter item materials
31170.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a bespoke barter item pleasing to the Mord.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31171.name: bespoke barter item
31171.col_2: This creation is tailor-made to capture the heart─and lower the prices─of a Mord merchant.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31172.name: set of test-fire target dummy materials
31172.description: sets of test-fire target dummy materials
31172.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a test-fire target dummy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31173.name: test-fire target dummy
31173.col_2: This target dummy is destined for destruction by tank cannon test-firing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31174.name: set of experimental plating component materials
31174.description: sets of experimental plating component materials
31174.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating experimental armor plating components.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31175.name: experimental plating component
31175.col_2: An experimental component designed to strengthen a tank's armor plating.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31176.name: set of Unfailing Eye Opener materials
31176.description: sets of Unfailing Eye Opener materials
31176.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating the Unfailing Eye Opener.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31177.name: Unfailing Eye Opener
31177.col_2: A special “tool” designed to jolt the recipient into wakefulness with a one hundred percent success rate.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31178.name: set of eye-catching custom option materials
31178.description: sets of eye-catching custom option materials
31178.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating an eye-catching custom option for a tank's exterior appearance.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31179.name: eye-catching custom option
31179.col_2: An attention-seeking custom option designed to distinguish a tank's exterior appearance.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31180.name: set of automaton repair component materials
31180.description: sets of automaton repair component materials
31180.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating an automaton repair component.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31181.name: automaton repair component
31181.col_2: A component needed for the repairs of a badly damaged automaton drudge.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31182.name: set of low-profile custom option materials
31182.description: sets of low-profile custom option materials
31182.col_2: Assorted materials necessary for creating a low-profile custom option for a tank's exterior appearance.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31183.name: low-profile custom option
31183.col_2: A stealth-enhancing custom option designed to camouflage a tank's exterior appearance.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Only for use in dwarf society quests.

31184.name: length of grade 3 skybuilders' plywood
31184.col_2: Some pieces of plywood have a thin veneer covering the surface to give the impression of being made from actual wood. This specimen, however, harbors no such pretensions and is every bit as cheap as it looks.

31185.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' alloy
31185.col_2: The favored alloy of the hoi polloi.

31186.name: grade 3 skybuilders' steel plate
31186.col_2: Despite the name, this is not a robust, metallic piece of tableware. The main reason it is unsuited to such a purpose is that there is nothing to stop peas from rolling off the edge.

31187.name: grade 3 skybuilders' ingot
31187.col_2: Though ingots are fairly ubiquitous in most forms of metalworking, far less commonly seen is a variation known as an outgot, which is exactly the same but upside down.

31188.name: circle of grade 3 skybuilders' leather
31188.col_2: When choosing the name, the skybuilders were far more concerned with assigning a grade than specifying the animal from which the leather originally came. It does smell a bit like goat, if that is anything to go by.

31189.name: length of grade 3 skybuilders' rope
31189.col_2: This is what string wants to be when it grows up.

31190.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' ink
31190.col_2: “If you took away my paper, I would write on my heart. If you took away my ink, I would write on the wind.<hex:02100103>...It wouldn't be an ideal way to work.”<hex:02100103>─Unknown author, dreamweaver, visionary, plus actor

31191.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' hemp milk
31191.description: bottles of grade 3 skybuilders' hemp milk
31191.col_2: Being made from plant extracts, this refreshing beverage stretches the definition of what is normally considered to be milk. Then again, if seahorses and starfish are anything to go by, names can often be misleading.

31192.name: grade 3 skybuilders' crate
31192.col_2: With all the crates scattered around the Firmament, the skybuilders have need of a means of storing them. It is for this exact purpose that this particular container was designed. Calls for it to be renamed the “crate crate” have been largely ignored.

31193.name: handful of grade 3 skybuilders' nails
31193.col_2: Even a simple table leg can be transformed into a deadly bludgeon by hammering a few of these nails into the end. Perfect for adventurers on a tight budget.

31194.name: handful of grade 3 skybuilders' rivets
31194.col_2: Some may argue that rivets are nothing more than nails without the pointy bit.

31195.name: handful of grade 3 skybuilders' rings
31195.col_2: These metal rings can apparently be joined and unjoined at will, though the only people capable of such a feat are sleight of hand artists. The skybuilders, however, are reluctant to employ such unscrupulous characters for fear of them fleecing the other workers, leaving these rings in a decidedly unjoined state.

31196.name: bundle of grade 3 skybuilders' leather straps
31196.description: bundles of grade 3 skybuilders' leather straps
31196.col_2: When times are hard, many of the poor resort to eating leather to survive. Cutting said material into strips beforehand makes it somewhat easier to digest, or at the very least, easier to chew.

31197.name: bolt of grade 3 skybuilders' cloth
31197.col_2: In most regions, people dress according to their personal preferences. In Ishgard, people dress according to their need to not freeze to death. Cloth such as this is as essential to survival as basic sustenance, if not more, as the cold will kill you faster than an empty stomach.

31198.name: phial of grade 3 skybuilders' plant oil
31198.description: phials of grade 3 skybuilders' plant oil
31198.col_2: The people of Ishgard have endless uses for plant oil, though the local climate is less than ideal for the cultivation of said plants, or anything to cook using said oil, for that matter.

31199.name: grade 3 skybuilders' sesame cookie
31199.col_2: In order to be classed as grade 3, each cookie must contain a certain number of sesame seeds. Needless to say, counting them is one of the most tedious tasks undertaken by the skybuilders, though it works remarkably well as a cure for insomnia.

31200.name: grade 3 skybuilders' grinding wheel
31200.col_2: Primarily used for filing down the various materials used in goldsmithing, as well as providing an effective─though not especially portable─means of keeping fingernails short.

31201.name: grade 3 skybuilders' pickaxe
31201.col_2: Useful not only for clearing rocks and debris, but also for dispatching any creatures that may emerge. In the case of Copperbell Mines, however, such creatures are often armed with pickaxes of their own.

31202.name: grade 3 skybuilders' cookpot
31202.col_2: Can also be used as a makeshift bathtub by Lalafells, provided they refrain from sloshing water everywhere by making the pot sway back and forth.

31203.name: grade 3 skybuilders' embroidery frame
31203.col_2: Though there is little discernible difference between the grade 2 and grade 3 embroidery frames, the name alone strongly implies that this version is infinitely superior.

31204.name: grade 3 skybuilders' leather sack
31204.col_2: If one of the workers in the Firmament is given one of these sacks, it should be taken as meaning “pack up your things and leave.” Ishgard maintains the tradition of literally giving someone the sack when their employment has been terminated.

31205.name: grade 3 skybuilders' broom
31205.col_2: Those who believe the tales of witches flying around on broomsticks have obviously never tried flying one for themselves. They take to the air about as well as a heavily armored Temple Knight takes to water, which is to say, not very.

31206.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' holy water
31206.description: bottles of grade 3 skybuilders' holy water
31206.col_2: Believed to cure zombification. Grade 3 is claimed to grant a full recovery, whereas grade 2 only delays the onset of the symptoms, and grade 1 merely replaces the need to feast on the flesh of the living with a craving for copious amounts of bacon.

31207.name: cup of grade 3 skybuilders' tea
31207.col_2: A grade 3 cup is stirred using a figure of eight motion, rather than the traditional circular movement used for the grade 2 variety. Claims that this has any discernible effect on the flavor are largely regarded as nonsense, however.

31208.name: grade 3 skybuilders' stepladder
31208.col_2: Perhaps when man and dragon have formed a stronger bond of trust, the skybuilders may take to the air on dragonback to perform all manner of tasks at higher altitudes. Until that day, mankind will just have to rely on good, old-fashioned stepladders.

31209.name: grade 3 skybuilders' crosscut saw
31209.col_2: Extremely effective at producing sawdust. Also cuts wood.

31210.name: grade 3 skybuilders' mesail
31210.col_2: This would be perfect for protecting one's eyes from flying sparks while performing metalwork─the task it was primarily designed for─were it not for the large eyeholes.

31211.name: grade 3 skybuilders' stone
31211.col_2: Despite its abundance in Coerthas, the skybuilders are quick to remind others that “stone like this doesn't grow on trees.” Factually accurate, yes. Logically sound, not so much.

31212.name: pair of grade 3 skybuilders' longboots
31212.col_2: In other parts of Hydaelyn, people would consider wearing two pairs of socks ample protection against the cold. In Coerthas, it is common to wear two pairs of boots, one over the other, as well as maybe a couple more pairs of socks for good measure.

31213.name: pair of grade 3 skybuilders' gloves
31213.col_2: For those wondering what the distinction between the grade 2 and grade 3 varieties might be, they need only smell the glove.

31214.name: bar of grade 3 skybuilders' soap
31214.col_2: When strategically placed on the floor, a wet bar of soap can be used to form a makeshift death trap for offing heiresses and the like.

31215.name: grade 3 skybuilders' all-purpose infusion
31215.col_2: Whereas many concoctions are said to prevent various ailments, this one supposedly prevents all manner of accidents. In addition to drinking the recommended daily dose, one must avoid physical exertion, unnecessary excursions, and anything even remotely resembling danger to enjoy the effects of the infusion to their fullest.

31216.name: grade 3 skybuilders' bed
31216.col_2: Bed, bedder, bedst.<hex:02100103>Never let it rest.<hex:02100103>Till your bed is bedder, and your bedder bedst.

31217.name: grade 3 skybuilders' oven
31217.col_2: Large enough to fit a whole witch inside.

31218.name: grade 3 skybuilders' lamppost
31218.col_2: Keep this lamppost away from dogs, or alternatively, keep dogs away from this lamppost. Whichever is more feasible.

31219.name: grade 3 skybuilders' brazier
31219.col_2: This traditional cooking apparatus offers Ishgardians the opportunity to enjoy two of their favorite pastimes: fried meat and not freezing to death.

31220.name: set of grade 3 skybuilders' overalls
31220.col_2: Overall the best thing to wear over all of one's clothes.

31221.name: grade 3 skybuilders' awning
31221.col_2: Protects one's eyes from the glaring sunlight, should any of it manage to find its way through the layers of dense cloud that hang almost perpetually over Ishgard.

31222.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' growth formula
31222.description: bottles of grade 3 skybuilders' growth formula
31222.col_2: The original creator claims it works on almost anything, within reason. Stone, for example, stubbornly refuses to grow no matter how much formula is applied.

31223.name: pot of grade 3 skybuilders' stew
31223.col_2: The grade 3 stew actually contains ingredients with names other than “dunno” or “not sure, but it was definitely dead when I threw it in.”

31224.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' goldsmithing bench
31224.col_2: Not only is the workbench rather lavishly made, it can also be used in the crafting of further lavishly made items.

31225.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' smithing bench
31225.col_2: Suited to almost any sort of smithing besides wordsmithing, for which a regular desk will suffice.

31226.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' door
31226.col_2: “When one door closes, another one opens? Sounds like you'd have trouble keeping out the draught.”<hex:02100103>─Unknown carpenter

31227.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' chronometer
31227.col_2: Though the use of such timepieces is still fairly limited in Ishgard, this particular model includes a bell that be set to ring at a specified time, earning it the rather catchy appellation “alarum chronometer.”

31228.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' leather chair
31228.col_2: Luckily, only the upholstery is made from leather. If the inner frame were made from the same material, it would have a difficult time supporting the weight of anything heavier than a medium-sized cat.

31229.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' apron
31229.col_2: Basically a large dishcloth with a few straps attached. However, it is these straps that earn the apron the right to be called artisanal, as they will not come undone no matter how hard they are tugged by needy children begging for cookies.

31230.name: unit of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' tiled flooring
31230.description: units of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' tiled flooring
31230.col_2: The use of materials that are naturally cold to the touch in the chilly land of Coerthas may be considered a design flaw, but it is actually a designer floor.

31231.name: plate of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' luncheon
31231.description: plates of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' luncheon
31231.col_2: Though an army may march on its stomach, the skybuilders choose a more effective means of forward locomotion: walking with their legs. It is for this reason they require sustenance, and this hearty meal provides exactly that, along with enough grease to kill a sasquatch.

31232.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' switch
31232.col_2: Makes a satisfying “thwack” sound when swung through the air. On the other hand, attempting to actually hit something will cause it to break immediately, so it is reserved only for scare tactics.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31233.name: tuft of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hemp
31233.description: tufts of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hemp
31233.col_2: Compared to the grade 2 variety, this is the good shite.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31234.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' ore
31234.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' ore
31234.col_2: The first miner to discover this particular variety described it as “extra-ore-dinary” and was met with a chorus of groans from her peers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31235.name: pinch of approved grade 3 skybuilders' bomb ash
31235.description: pinches of approved grade 3 skybuilders' bomb ash
31235.col_2: Some might argue that it would be easier to locate a living bomb and wait for it to explode than to scrabble about in the dirt and undergrowth looking for particles of ash from one that had exploded previously. The problem lies in finding volunteers who are not only foolhardy enough to attempt it, but hardy enough to survive.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31236.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' ebony log
31236.col_2: Care must be taken when working with ebony wood, as its sawdust is both highly flammable and toxic. Strangely, the skybuilders failed to mention this...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31237.name: tuft of approved grade 3 skybuilders' sesame
31237.description: tufts of approved grade 3 skybuilders' sesame
31237.col_2: Sesame is not only a useful plant, but the mere mention of its name is believed to open many doors in a very literal sense.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31238.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' cotton boll
31238.col_2: Often misheard as “cotton bowl,” which has led to several nigh on useless pieces of fluffy tableware being submitted to the skybuilders.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31239.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' titanium ore
31239.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' titanium ore
31239.col_2: Unlike some other ores requested by the skybuilders, they actually deigned to give the name of the type of metal they would like in this case, rather than simply “some ore.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31240.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' rock salt
31240.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' rock salt
31240.col_2: This particular type of salt is for sprinkling on rocks to make them taste better, hence the name “rock salt.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31241.name: handful of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hardsilver sand
31241.description: handfuls of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hardsilver sand
31241.col_2: Hardsilver's inherent hardness is somewhat difficult to gauge in granular form.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31242.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' lauan log
31242.col_2: The aesthetically pleasing bark of this particular tree allows it to be used in its natural state to give a rustic feel to a home's interior. On the other hand, “rustic” is often used to mean “we can save time and effort by convincing gullible customers that having bits of rough-cut wood all over the place is somehow desirable.”

31243.name: sprig of approved grade 3 skybuilders' mistletoe
31243.description: sprigs of approved grade 3 skybuilders' mistletoe
31243.col_2: Used in a variety of medical treatments despite being highly toxic. Failure to adhere to the correct dosage may lead to symptoms far worse than the ailment it was meant to cure.

31244.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' toad
31244.col_2: One of the skybuilders has been tasked with kissing every toad they receive on the off chance of it being a cursed prince. This, however, is suspected to be one of the many tasks designed to keep troublesome workers out of mischief, along with polishing the coal and washing the soap.

31245.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' vine
31245.col_2: A naturally occurring substitute for rope, perfect for swinging through the trees while yodeling like a buffoon.

31246.name: basket of approved grade 3 skybuilders' tea leaves
31246.description: baskets of approved grade 3 skybuilders' tea leaves
31246.col_2: This variety is often used in tea leaf reading, and is said to result in a high rate of good fortunes, though most tasseomancers base their readings more on what they think the customer wants to hear than the patterns left in the cup.

31247.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron ore
31247.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron ore
31247.col_2: Though similar substances exist in other regions, the Diadem variety tends to be more highly coveted. This may simply be due to its scarcity rather than any intrinsic properties, as by and large, the more difficult something is to obtain, the more people want it.
31247.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Diadem Iron Ore

31248.name: pinch of approved grade 3 skybuilders' alumen
31248.description: pinches of approved grade 3 skybuilders' alumen
31248.col_2: In recent years, there have been calls to abandon the use of “pinches” as a unit of measurement for powders. However, the fact that an amount equal to a single pinch is rarely enough to cause even the most sensitive of scales to budge leads to difficulties when deciding on a weight-based standard.

31249.name: bottle of approved grade 3 skybuilders' spring water
31249.description: bottles of approved grade 3 skybuilders' spring water
31249.col_2: The name may indicate that there are very specific criteria to pass muster with the skybuilders, but the taste and smell are the same as almost any other type of water. That is to say: it tastes of nothing and smells of nothing.

31250.name: handful of approved grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron sand
31250.description: handfuls of approved grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron sand
31250.col_2: As is often the case with items found in the Diadem, this iron sand possesses unique properties. It is magnetically attracted not only to metallic objects, but a range of organic materials, such as skin and clothing, which means it is often gathered regardless of one's intentions.
31250.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Diadem Iron Sand

31251.name: slab of approved grade 3 skybuilders' siltstone
31251.description: slabs of approved grade 3 skybuilders' siltstone
31251.col_2: This flaky, lightweight stone is a firm favorite with street performers who demonstrate their strength by smashing through rock with their bare hands.

31252.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' cedar log
31252.col_2: Due to cedar being a natural repellent for moths─which can be both extremely large and ferocious in some parts─many adventurers have taken to carrying it about their person. Hefting around an entire log might be going a touch overboard, however.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31253.name: lump of approved grade 3 skybuilders' resin
31253.description: lumps of approved grade 3 skybuilders' resin
31253.col_2: “He tried to take it from me, or at least, he looked like he wanted to. So I cut him. Can't blame a man for keeping his resin to himself, can you?”<hex:02100103>─Excerpt from <hex:021A020203>How to Win Friends and Execute People: Climbing the Ranks of the Temple Knights<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103>by unknown author<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31254.name: sheaf of approved grade 3 skybuilders' wheat
31254.description: sheaves of approved grade 3 skybuilders' wheat
31254.col_2: May contain traces of chaff.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31255.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' gossamer cotton boll
31255.description: approved grade 3 skybuilders' gossamer cotton bolls
31255.col_2: In this case, the word “gossamer” is applied in a literal sense, as each boll is covered in a fine layer of cobweb. This is kept intact until the cotton is spun into thread, which grants it extraordinary resilience to wear and tear.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31255.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Gossamer Cotton Boll

31256.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' adder
31256.col_2: As one can imagine, there is a host of practical applications for a venomous snake in the Ishgardian reconstruction efforts. These include the production of snake wine, in which the scalekin is preserved in alcohol that gains a unique flavor and medicinal properties. In several cases, the snake has been known to spring to life after moons of being entirely submerged in the liquid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31257.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' aurum regis ore
31257.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' aurum regis ore
31257.col_2: “Kingly” is not an adjective that is often applied to metals of any sort, though in the case of aurum regis, it seems perfectly fitting, for some reason.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31257.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Aurum Regis Ore

31258.name: chunk of approved grade 3 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31258.description: chunks of approved grade 3 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31258.col_2: Many people prefer to keep such chunks whole so that they may be used as “salt rocks.” These are placed in the center of the dining table so that anyone who feels their meal is lacking in saltiness can simply lick it and carry on with their meal.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31258.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Finest Rock Salt

31259.name: bottle of approved grade 3 skybuilders' truespring water
31259.description: bottles of approved grade 3 skybuilders' truespring water
31259.col_2: Often confused with falsespring water, which is remarkably similar apart from the fact it smells like a wet dog.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31260.name: pinch of approved grade 3 skybuilders' fossil dust
31260.description: pinches of approved grade 3 skybuilders' fossil dust
31260.col_2: “Despite the creature having been dead for millennia, fossilized, and then ground to dust, I was able to extrapolate its diet, breeding habits, and susceptibility to hiccups from the single, remaining fragment of vertebrae.”<hex:02100103>─Excerpt from <hex:021A020203>On the Trail of the Thunder Lizards<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31261.name: slab of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hard mudstone
31261.description: slabs of approved grade 3 skybuilders' hard mudstone
31261.col_2: Mudstone may not be the most impressive of substances, but becoming a solid piece of rock after an extended period as a sticky semiliquid is something of an improvement.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31262.name: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' log
31262.col_2: Grade 3 and artisanal it may be, yet the name of the tree from which it came is an enigma enveloped in a mystery. Before the skybuilders and their bizarre naming conventions, it was simply...log.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31263.name: piece of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' amber
31263.description: pieces of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' amber
31263.col_2: The grade is determined by the number of vilekin encased within each piece. Fewer is generally considered to be better, unless the buyer happens to be a naturalist, in which case, the opposite is true. They have been known to pay absurd amounts for the most heavily infested specimens.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31264.name: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cotton boll
31264.description: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cotton bolls
31264.col_2: These bolls contain roughly twice the amount of cotton as the regular sort, but due to the thickness of the plant's stems, take roughly twice as much effort to harvest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31264.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Cotton Boll

31265.name: box of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' rice
31265.description: boxes of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' rice
31265.col_2: Rice remains something of a novelty in Ishgard, though the skybuilders seem to be experts on the subject regardless. Apparently, they can tell the difference between the truly artisanal and the merely humdrum.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31266.name: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' vine
31266.col_2: The artisanal vines that are chosen for the Firmament tend to stand out from the common-or-garden varieties. One could say they are vine for attention.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31267.name: chunk of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31267.description: chunks of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31267.col_2: One of the few stones light enough to float in water.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31268.name: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' basilisk egg
31268.description: approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' basilisk eggs
31268.col_2: Most recipients of such eggs would prefer them without a tiny, carnivorous scalekin inside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31268.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Artisanal Skybuilders' Basilisk Egg

31269.name: pinch of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' alumen
31269.description: pinches of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' alumen
31269.col_2: Though alumen is commonly used in the tanning of animal hide, the artisanal can supposedly be used to tan other materials, such as hair or soil. Such claims have yet to be verified, however.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31270.name: sack of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' clay
31270.description: sacks of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' clay
31270.col_2: Many apprentice potters have been known to misinterpret the meaning of “throwing a pot,” leading to hilarious capers, instant dismissal, or both.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31271.name: chunk of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' granite
31271.description: chunks of approved grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' granite
31271.col_2: Granite is said to be phaneritic, or in layman's terms, macroscopically crystalline.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31272.name: pot of approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral galewood sap
31272.description: pots of approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral galewood sap
31272.col_2: Practically pulsating with wind-aspected aether. Also has a distinct sweet taste, although one should take care when adding it to their beverages, unless the aim is to create a literal storm in a teacup.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral tempest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31272.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Umbral Galewood Sap

31273.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral tortoise
31273.col_2: In addition to its craggy hide and shell protecting it from the teeth and claws of predators, the earth-aspected aether with which it is infused causes it to taste like soil. Any creatures patient and strong enough to reach the tender meat inside are invariably left disappointed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral duststorm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31274.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral magma shard
31274.description: approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral magma shards
31274.col_2: Though the name may seem at first to be an oxymoron, each fragment actually contains magma in liquid form beneath a thin crust. Anyone foolish enough to put one of these shards in their back pocket before sitting down will cause a hole to be burned not only in their breeches, but also the chair on which they sat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral flare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31274.col_3: Approved Grade 3 Skybuilders' Umbral Magma Shard

31275.name: approved grade 3 skybuilders' umbral levinite
31275.col_2: Some scholars maintain that levinite is the result of lightning taking solid form upon striking the earth. Most other scholars, however, maintain that this theory is bollocks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during umbral levin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31276.name: grade 3 skybuilders' switch
31276.col_2: Makes a satisfying “thwack” sound when swung through the air. On the other hand, attempting to actually hit something will cause it to break immediately, so it is reserved only for scare tactics.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31277.name: tuft of grade 3 skybuilders' hemp
31277.col_2: Compared to the grade 2 variety, this is the good shite.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31278.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' ore
31278.col_2: The first miner to discover this particular variety described it as “extra-ore-dinary” and was met with a chorus of groans from her peers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31279.name: pinch of grade 3 skybuilders' bomb ash
31279.description: pinches of grade 3 skybuilders' bomb ash
31279.col_2: Some might argue that it would be easier to locate a living bomb and wait for it to explode than to scrabble about in the dirt and undergrowth looking for particles of ash from one that had exploded previously. The problem lies in finding volunteers who are not only foolhardy enough to attempt it, but hardy enough to survive.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31280.name: grade 3 skybuilders' ebony log
31280.col_2: Care must be taken when working with ebony wood, as its sawdust is both highly flammable and toxic. Strangely, the skybuilders failed to mention this...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31281.name: tuft of grade 3 skybuilders' sesame
31281.col_2: Sesame is not only a useful plant, but the mere mention of its name is believed to open many doors in a very literal sense.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31282.name: grade 3 skybuilders' cotton boll
31282.col_2: Often misheard as “cotton bowl,” which has led to several nigh on useless pieces of fluffy tableware being submitted to the skybuilders.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31283.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' titanium ore
31283.description: chunks of grade 3 skybuilders' titanium ore
31283.col_2: Unlike some other ores requested by the skybuilders, they actually deigned to give the name of the type of metal they would like in this case, rather than simply “some ore.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31284.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' rock salt
31284.description: chunks of grade 3 skybuilders' rock salt
31284.col_2: This particular type of salt is for sprinkling on rocks to make them taste better, hence the name “rock salt.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31285.name: handful of grade 3 skybuilders' hardsilver sand
31285.description: handfuls of grade 3 skybuilders' hardsilver sand
31285.col_2: Hardsilver's inherent hardness is somewhat difficult to gauge in granular form.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31286.name: grade 3 skybuilders' lauan log
31286.col_2: The aesthetically pleasing bark of this particular tree allows it to be used in its natural state to give a rustic feel to a home's interior. On the other hand, “rustic” is often used to mean “we can save time and effort by convincing gullible customers that having bits of rough-cut wood all over the place is somehow desirable.”

31287.name: sprig of grade 3 skybuilders' mistletoe
31287.col_2: Used in a variety of medical treatments despite being highly toxic. Failure to adhere to the correct dosage may lead to symptoms far worse than the ailment it was meant to cure.

31288.name: grade 3 skybuilders' toad
31288.col_2: One of the skybuilders has been tasked with kissing every toad they receive on the off chance of it being a cursed prince. This, however, is suspected to be one of the many tasks designed to keep troublesome workers out of mischief, along with polishing the coal and washing the soap.

31289.name: grade 3 skybuilders' vine
31289.col_2: A naturally occurring substitute for rope, perfect for swinging through the trees while yodeling like a buffoon.

31290.name: basket of grade 3 skybuilders' tea leaves
31290.description: baskets of grade 3 skybuilders' tea leaves
31290.col_2: This variety is often used in tea leaf reading, and is said to result in a high rate of good fortunes, though most tasseomancers base their readings more on what they think the customer wants to hear than the patterns left in the cup.

31291.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron ore
31291.description: chunks of grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron ore
31291.col_2: Though similar substances exist in other regions, the Diadem variety tends to be more highly coveted. This may simply be due to its scarcity rather than any intrinsic properties, as by and large, the more difficult something is to obtain, the more people want it.

31292.name: pinch of grade 3 skybuilders' alumen
31292.col_2: In recent years, there have been calls to abandon the use of “pinches” as a unit of measurement for powders. However, the fact that an amount equal to a single pinch is rarely enough to cause even the most sensitive of scales to budge leads to difficulties when deciding on a weight-based standard.

31293.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' spring water
31293.description: bottles of grade 3 skybuilders' spring water
31293.col_2: The name may indicate that there are very specific criteria to pass muster with the skybuilders, but the taste and smell are the same as almost any other type of water. That is to say: it tastes of nothing and smells of nothing.

31294.name: handful of grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron sand
31294.description: handfuls of grade 3 skybuilders' Diadem iron sand
31294.col_2: As is often the case with items found in the Diadem, this iron sand possesses unique properties. It is magnetically attracted not only to metallic objects, but a range of organic materials, such as skin and clothing, which means it is often gathered regardless of one's intentions.

31295.name: slab of grade 3 skybuilders' siltstone
31295.col_2: This flaky, lightweight stone is a firm favorite with street performers who demonstrate their strength by smashing through rock with their bare hands.

31296.name: grade 3 skybuilders' cedar log
31296.col_2: Due to cedar being a natural repellent for moths─which can be both extremely large and ferocious in some parts─many adventurers have taken to carrying it about their person. Hefting around an entire log might be going a touch overboard, however.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31297.name: lump of grade 3 skybuilders' resin
31297.col_2: “He tried to take it from me, or at least, he looked like he wanted to. So I cut him. Can't blame a man for keeping his resin to himself, can you?”<hex:02100103>─Excerpt from <hex:021A020203>How to Win Friends and Execute People: Climbing the Ranks of the Temple Knights<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103>by unknown author<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31298.name: sheaf of grade 3 skybuilders' wheat
31298.col_2: May contain traces of chaff.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31299.name: grade 3 skybuilders' gossamer cotton boll
31299.col_2: In this case, the word “gossamer” is applied in a literal sense, as each boll is covered in a fine layer of cobweb. This is kept intact until the cotton is spun into thread, which grants it extraordinary resilience to wear and tear.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31300.name: grade 3 skybuilders' adder
31300.col_2: As one can imagine, there is a host of practical applications for a venomous snake in the Ishgardian reconstruction efforts. These include the production of snake wine, in which the scalekin is preserved in alcohol that gains a unique flavor and medicinal properties. In several cases, the snake has been known to spring to life after moons of being entirely submerged in the liquid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31301.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' aurum regis ore
31301.description: chunks of grade 3 skybuilders' aurum regis ore
31301.col_2: “Kingly” is not an adjective that is often applied to metals of any sort, though in the case of aurum regis, it seems perfectly fitting, for some reason.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31302.name: chunk of grade 3 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31302.description: chunks of grade 3 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31302.col_2: Many people prefer to keep such chunks whole so that they may be used as “salt rocks.” These are placed in the center of the dining table so that anyone who feels their meal is lacking in saltiness can simply lick it and carry on with their meal.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31303.name: bottle of grade 3 skybuilders' truespring water
31303.description: bottles of grade 3 skybuilders' truespring water
31303.col_2: Often confused with falsespring water, which is remarkably similar apart from the fact it smells like a wet dog.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31304.name: pinch of grade 3 skybuilders' fossil dust
31304.description: pinches of grade 3 skybuilders' fossil dust
31304.col_2: “Despite the creature having been dead for millennia, fossilized, and then ground to dust, I was able to extrapolate its diet, breeding habits, and susceptibility to hiccups from the single, remaining fragment of vertebrae.”<hex:02100103>─Excerpt from <hex:021A020203>On the Trail of the Thunder Lizards<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31305.name: slab of grade 3 skybuilders' hard mudstone
31305.description: slabs of grade 3 skybuilders' hard mudstone
31305.col_2: Mudstone may not be the most impressive of substances, but becoming a solid piece of rock after an extended period as a sticky semiliquid is something of an improvement.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31306.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' log
31306.col_2: Grade 3 and artisanal it may be, yet the name of the tree from which it came is an enigma enveloped in a mystery. Before the skybuilders and their bizarre naming conventions, it was simply...log.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31307.name: piece of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' amber
31307.description: pieces of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' amber
31307.col_2: The grade is determined by the number of vilekin encased within each piece. Fewer is generally considered to be better, unless the buyer happens to be a naturalist, in which case, the opposite is true. They have been known to pay absurd amounts for the most heavily infested specimens.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31308.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cotton boll
31308.col_2: These bolls contain roughly twice the amount of cotton as the regular sort, but due to the thickness of the plant's stems, take roughly twice as much effort to harvest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31309.name: box of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' rice
31309.description: boxes of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' rice
31309.col_2: Rice remains something of a novelty in Ishgard, though the skybuilders seem to be experts on the subject regardless. Apparently, they can tell the difference between the truly artisanal and the merely humdrum.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31310.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' vine
31310.col_2: The artisanal vines that are chosen for the Firmament tend to stand out from the common-or-garden varieties. One could say they are vine for attention.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31311.name: chunk of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31311.description: chunks of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31311.col_2: One of the few stones light enough to float in water.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31312.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' basilisk egg
31312.col_2: Most recipients of such eggs would prefer them without a tiny, carnivorous scalekin inside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31313.name: pinch of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' alumen
31313.description: pinches of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' alumen
31313.col_2: Though alumen is commonly used in the tanning of animal hide, the artisanal can supposedly be used to tan other materials, such as hair or soil. Such claims have yet to be verified, however.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31314.name: sack of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' clay
31314.description: sacks of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' clay
31314.col_2: Many apprentice potters have been known to misinterpret the meaning of “throwing a pot,” leading to hilarious capers, instant dismissal, or both.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31315.name: chunk of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' granite
31315.description: chunks of grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' granite
31315.col_2: Granite is said to be phaneritic, or in layman's terms, macroscopically crystalline.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31316.name: pot of grade 3 skybuilders' umbral galewood sap
31316.description: pots of grade 3 skybuilders' umbral galewood sap
31316.col_2: Practically pulsating with wind-aspected aether. Also has a distinct sweet taste, although one should take care when adding it to their beverages, unless the aim is to create a literal storm in a teacup.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral tempest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31317.name: grade 3 skybuilders' umbral tortoise
31317.col_2: In addition to its craggy hide and shell protecting it from the teeth and claws of predators, the earth-aspected aether with which it is infused causes it to taste like soil. Any creatures patient and strong enough to reach the tender meat inside are invariably left disappointed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral duststorm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31318.name: grade 3 skybuilders' umbral magma shard
31318.col_2: Though the name may seem at first to be an oxymoron, each fragment actually contains magma in liquid form beneath a thin crust. Anyone foolish enough to put one of these shards in their back pocket before sitting down will cause a hole to be burned not only in their breeches, but also the chair on which they sat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral flare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31319.name: grade 3 skybuilders' umbral levinite
31319.col_2: Some scholars maintain that levinite is the result of lightning taking solid form upon striking the earth. Most other scholars, however, maintain that this theory is bollocks.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during umbral levin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31320.name: bag of slithersand
31320.col_2: Smooth granules of the mineral also known as green cinnabar, containing traces of quicksilver.

31321.name: vermilion paper parasol
31321.col_2: Though one might assume that paper is less than ideal for protecting oneself from the rain, this parasol has been treated with waterproof oil. The makers cannot, however, be held responsible for any puddles stepped in. Use to acquire a vermilion paper parasol.

31322.name: plum paper parasol
31322.col_2: Named for its color, not because the paper is made from the wood of a plum tree. Use to acquire a plum paper parasol.

31323.name: gold paper parasol
31323.col_2: Unfortunately not covered in gold leaf, but fool's gold leaf, which is considerably cheaper on account of its rather silly name. Use to acquire a gold paper parasol.

31324.name: calming checkered parasol
31324.col_2: Creates not only a small, portable circle of shade, but exudes a calming influence. Somehow. Use to acquire a calming checkered parasol.

31325.name: cheerful checkered parasol
31325.col_2: There is something about a white background covered in many, many straight red lines that creates a cheerful atmosphere, though scholars have yet to determine exactly why. Use to acquire a cheerful checkered parasol.

31326.name: classy checkered parasol
31326.col_2: Were one to describe this parasol's pattern as “black-and-white check” then perhaps it might conjure images of chessboards and the like. Even so, it could be argued that this design is far classier. Use to acquire a classy checkered parasol.

31327.name: Season Two writ of commendation
31327.col_2: Documentation of noteworthy accomplishments on behalf of the Ishgardian Restoration.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use to gain the “Minor Miracle” achievement for Season Two.

31328.name: Season Two writ of canonization
31328.col_2: Documentation of noteworthy accomplishments on behalf of the Ishgardian Restoration.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Use to gain the “Divine Ascension” achievement for Season Two.

31329.col_2: A heavy chest containing a weapon of item level 18 through 21.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Weapon type determined by current job or class at time of opening. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

31337.name: level 49 weapon coffer
31337.col_2: A heavy chest containing an item level 49 weapon.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Weapon type determined by current job or class at time of opening. Cannot be opened in instanced areas such as dungeons, PvP areas, or raids.

31338.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - Reproachful Rumination<hex:021A020103>
31338.col_2: An illustrated manual of how to tactfully express one's doubt or disagreement when conversing in a formal setting. Use to learn the /consider emote.

31339.name: irregular tomestone of esoterics
31339.col_2: One of only a few in existence, this Allagan tomestone contains knowledge that is clearly uncommon for a reason.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can be exchanged with itinerant moogles for certain items.

31351.name: Bozjan coin
31351.col_2: A tarnished and dented coin minted in Bozja before it became subject to imperial rule.

31352.name: box of Bozjan runner's secrets (head gear)
31352.description: boxes of Bozjan runner's secrets (head gear)
31352.col_2: Clasps, protective material, and other accoutrements that can be applied to personal equipment for increased safety and mobility on the battlefield.

31357.name: southern front lockbox
31357.col_2: A battered though still firmly sealed box discovered at the Bozjan southern front. Only a Gangos-trained locksmith might grant you access to the spoils within.

31393.name: Bozjan earring
31393.col_2: Increases EXP earned by 10% when level 80 and below. Attributes and item level vary according to class/job and current level when equipped.

31396.name: magitek hyperconveyor identification key
31396.col_2: A thin, rectangular piece of what appears to be cermet. Placing it near your magitek hyperconveyor will magically bring the machine to life.

31397.name: magicked prism (mandragora)
31397.col_2: This peculiar contraption creates illusions by weaving together myriad shades of light. Lovingly crafted by the children of Menphina's Arms.

31398.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Metaphysics of Merrymaking<hex:021A020103>
31398.description: copies of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Metaphysics of Merrymaking<hex:021A020103>
31398.col_2: An illustrated manual including impenetrable text excerpts courtesy of Far Eastern scholar Seigetsu the Enlightened. Use to learn the /wasshoi emote.
31398.col_3: Ballroom Etiquette - The Metaphysics of Merrymaking

31399.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - Floral Rearrangement<hex:021A020103>
31399.col_2: An illustrated manual of how to create a dazzling shower of petals to accompany your debut without <hex:021A020203>conspicuously<hex:021A020103> destroying whatever bouquets may be close at hand. Use to learn the /flowershower emote.

31400.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Flame Dance<hex:021A020103>
31400.description: copies of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Flame Dance<hex:021A020103>
31400.col_2: An illustrated manual of the various steps that comprise a traditional Lalafellin dance hailing from the sunny south sea isles. Use to learn the /flamedance emote.

31401.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - Uncouth Congratulations<hex:021A020103>
31401.col_2: An illustrated manual of congratulatory gestures best avoided in polite company. Use to learn the /highfive emote.

31402.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - Pointed Misgivings<hex:021A020103>
31402.col_2: An illustrated manual of how to make clear that you are keeping close watch over the whole of the banquet table, and will deliver swift retribution should anyone try to take more than the socially acceptable number of hors d'oeuvres. Use to learn the /guard emote.

31403.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - Dark Entreaty<hex:021A020103>
31403.col_2: An illustrated manual detailing how to visit an unholy fate upon your social rivals. Use to learn the /malevolence emote.

31404.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Bee's Knees<hex:021A020103>
31404.description: copies of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Bee's Knees<hex:021A020103>
31404.col_2: An illustrated manual of the various steps that comprise the bee's knees, an unobtrusive-but-delightful dance that never gets old. Skimpy attire optional (and may be frowned upon at certain functions). Use to learn the /beesknees emote.

31405.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Lali Hop<hex:021A020103>
31405.description: copies of <hex:021A020203>Ballroom Etiquette - The Lali Hop<hex:021A020103>
31405.col_2: An illustrated manual of the various steps that comprise the lali hop, a dance that─like most every dwarven custom─is tremendously rousing. Use to learn the /lalihop emote.

31406.name: copy of <hex:021A020203>Modern Aesthetics - Saintly Style<hex:021A020103>
