31578.name: grade 3 skybuilders' thunderbolt sculpin
31578.col_2: Despite the impressive and imposing pattern of a lightning bolt running down its back, this fish gives off no notable electrical discharge, much to the relief of anglers who manage to reel one in.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31579.name: grade 3 skybuilders' alligator snapping turtle
31579.col_2: To count the number of fishermen who have lost fingers and toes to this savage beast one would need─well, more digits than any of those unfortunate individuals have remaining, to say the least.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31580.name: grade 3 skybuilders' bonytongue
31580.col_2: Notwithstanding its decidedly unflattering moniker, this wavekin cuts a rather striking figure with its vivid red-hued scales, leading some to wonder whatever grudge the naturalist who named it had against the poor creature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31581.name: grade 3 skybuilders' hermit goby
31581.col_2: One glance at this unsightly wavekin and any angler will understand why it chooses to spend the majority of its life hidden from view─though recently, some aesthetes have bafflingly come to find beauty in its grotesqueness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31582.name: grade 3 skybuilders' mudskipper
31582.col_2: This amphibious fish spends the better part of its time wallowing about in mire and muck, perhaps in vain hope that making itself appear as repulsive as possible will dissuade anglers from wanting to catch it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31583.name: grade 3 skybuilders' steppe bullfrog
31583.col_2: While one might indeed wonder what a so-called “steppe” bullfrog is doing amidst the floating isles of the Diadem, one might stop to consider whether the creature in question would ask the same question of you.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31584.name: grade 3 skybuilders' golden loach
31584.col_2: One is encouraged to take especial care when reeling in this striking specimen so as not to besmirch its pristine appearance─sadly, its tendency to thrash and turn about can make this an all-but-impossible task.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31585.name: grade 3 skybuilders' bass
31585.col_2: Though it is not easily reeled in, many anglers breathe a sigh of relief when assigned this wavekin, if only for its easily-pronounced name. After all, shouting out “Fifteen grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' archaeopteryges submitted for your approval, sir!” and the like can be something of a chore.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31586.name: grade 3 skybuilders' cherax
31586.col_2: Naturalists particular about nomenclature are quick to note that the plural of “cherax” is, in fact, “cherax,” and not “cheraxes.” More practical-minded anglers are equally quick to note that knowing such trivia will not avail one in avoiding its fearsome pincers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31587.name: grade 3 skybuilders' marimo
31587.col_2: A delight to observe wherever they are encountered, the sight of these green tufts of mossy fluff dancing and darting through the clouds amidst the isles of the Diadem is particularly breathtaking to behold.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31588.name: grade 3 skybuilders' catfish
31588.col_2: Some naturalists posit that, unlike its namesake, the catfish derives a degree of pleasure from having its whiskers tickled. Whether it would still appreciate this gesture when performed by the person who plucked the creature unceremoniously from the sky is another question.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31589.name: grade 3 skybuilders' ricefish
31589.col_2: So named because it is native to the rice paddies of the Far East, one might speculate as to why this wavekin has ventured so far from home. One might also ignore such trivialities and simply reel it in, a course of action which undoubtedly would prove more fruitful.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31590.name: grade 3 skybuilders' scorpionfly
31590.col_2: Is it a scorpion, or is it a fly? Actually, it's neither─but rather a volitant species of shrimp that vaguely resembles an amalgamation of the two disparate creatures whose name it bears.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31591.name: grade 3 skybuilders' whiteloom
31591.col_2: Observing the brilliant, nigh-silken tapestry these wavekin appear to weave as they dance and twirl through the clouds in the Diadem has lent further weight to the arguments of those who claim that its current nomenclature─and not “whiteroom”─is the proper one.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31592.name: grade 3 skybuilders' pteranodon
31592.col_2: One great mystery is how these prehistoric scalekin came to take up residence in the Diadem. A still greater mystery is why procuring them is so vital to the restoration effort.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31593.name: grade 3 skybuilders' king's mantle
31593.col_2: Despite this creature's most impressive moniker─and even more impressive appearance─one is discouraged from actually attempting to wear one, as the slime and stench it exudes make it rather unsuitable as garb, for royalty or otherwise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31594.name: grade 3 skybuilders' blue medusa
31594.col_2: Take care when fishing for this spiny creature─though its gaze will not turn you to stone, the poisonous barbs that line its tentacles will have a similarly paralyzing effect.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31595.name: grade 3 skybuilders' gurnard
31595.col_2: It is said that the name of this flying wavekin is derived from the guttural grunting sound it emits as it flies through the sky, an unfortunate trait that rather detracts from its overall elegant visual aspect.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31596.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' oscar
31596.col_2: This strikingly colored wavekin with flowing fins is both beautiful to behold as it is appealing to the appetite─posing quite the dilemma for any angler who is skilled and fortunate enough to reel one in.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31597.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' blind manta
31597.col_2: One might wonder how these eyeless creatures are able to navigate the clouds of the Diadem. While some naturalists posit that heightened tactile senses allow them to feel the winds and avoid collisions with floating rocks and other obstacles, others point out that the scratches observed in some of their bodies suggest that some are more successful at this than others.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31598.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' mosasaur
31598.col_2: Despite being powerful swimmers, these massive and aggressive aquatic scalekin prefer to lie in wait, pouncing on their prey from places unseen and devouring them whole.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31599.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' storm chaser
31599.col_2: What is it that compels the storm chaser to forsake calm and welcoming skies for the danger of raging tempests and crackling thunderbolts? Perhaps it is the same as what stirs adventurers to set forth in search of trials and tribulations to overcome.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31600.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' archaeopteryx
31600.col_2: This remarkable creature serves as living proof of the relationship between common birds and the massive prehistoric scalekin that ruled both land and sky.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31601.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' wyvern
31601.col_2: Is this an <hex:021A020203>actual<hex:021A020103> wyvern, or simply a sizable wavekin that bears a remarkable resemblance to its namesake? It is not immediately clear─and neither is why the creature is so vital for the restoration effort. It <hex:021A020203>is<hex:021A020103> artisanal, though, which doubtless counts for something.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31602.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' cloudshark
31602.col_2: It is unclear how this massive, fearsome predator evolved to swim among the clouds rather than the waters preferred by its fellow wavekin, but one thing is certain─less physically imposing denizens of the Diadem doubtless wish it had not.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31603.name: grade 3 artisanal skybuilders' helicoprion
31603.col_2: These terrifying creatures are noted for their whorls of innumerous razor-sharp teeth, which allow them to shred their prey with remarkable efficiency. It is recommended to ensure the creature is duly dead before admiring these teeth whorls for yourself, lest you share a similarly grisly fate.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31604.col_2: Despite the impressive and imposing pattern of a lightning bolt running down its back, this fish gives off no notable electrical discharge, much to the relief of anglers who manage to reel one in.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Not included in the fish guide.

31630.col_2: A banded chest containing a complete set of Hraesvelgr attire.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Required level: 1. IL: 1.

31651.name: conquistador plate belt
31651.col_2: Before becoming obsolete due to advancements in tailoring, belts such as this were used for holding up trousers and the like.

31652.name: rarefied lignum vitae grinding wheel
31652.col_2: A grinding wheel so exquisite, it will set the teeth of those who behold it to grinding out of sheer envy.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31653.name: rarefied mythril hatchet
31653.col_2: When they say “bury the hatchet,” they don't mean this one. Magnificent as it is, it should always be proudly and prominently displayed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31654.name: rarefied mythril alembic
31654.col_2: “You can taste the difference! Trust me on this!”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31655.name: rarefied mythril ring
31655.col_2: “He told me to cast it into the fire and destroy it. I said, 'No.'”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31656.name: rarefied swallowskin coat
31656.col_2: Many sea swallows died to bring you this coat. <hex:021A020203>Rare<hex:021A020103> ones.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31657.name: rarefied dwarven cotton beret
31657.col_2: So beautifully crafted is this cotton beret, all dwarven folk would be proud for it to bear their name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31658.name: rarefied dwarven mythril grimoire
31658.col_2: It doesn't take a dwarf to recognize that this dwarven mythril grimoire boasts superior craftsmanship.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31659.name: bottle of rarefied lemonade
31659.col_2: Made from the rarest of ingredients and bottled in the rarest of vessels, this lemonade is certified rarefied.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※For collectable submissions only.

31706.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>Liberation<hex:021A020103>
31706.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of key players in the conflict between the Garlean Empire and its erstwhile territories Ala Mhigo and Doma. The sense of impending liberation is authentic indeed.

31707.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>The Legend Returns<hex:021A020103>
31707.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of figures from Ivalician legend old and new. The pervading orangey-brownness of the piece gives it a palpable sense of authenticity.
31707.col_3: Authentic Copy of The Legend Returns

31708.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>Rise of a New Sun<hex:021A020103>
31708.description: authentic copies of <hex:021A020203>Rise of a New Sun<hex:021A020103>
31708.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of certain employees of Garlond Ironworks and an enigmatic piece of technology. The most authentic element of this piece is undoubtedly the depiction of a bulbous-headed yellow birdlike thing.
31708.col_3: Authentic Copy of Rise of a New Sun

31709.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>Under the Moonlight<hex:021A020103>
31709.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of the erstwhile acting imperial viceroy of Doma, Yotsuyu, and those instrumental in her destruction. The depiction of these pivotal figures under the moonlight, the serious moonlight, is unmistakably authentic.
31709.col_3: Authentic Copy of Under the Moonlight

31710.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>Prelude in Violet<hex:021A020103>
31710.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of the ruthless Garlean elite and a few noble souls who sought to stop their nefarious machinations. Some have remarked that Gaius Baelsar appears to be somewhat under the weather in this piece, but those who have been in contact with the man maintain that it is an entirely authentic depiction.
31710.col_3: Authentic Copy of Prelude in Violet

31711.name: authentic copy of <hex:021A020203>Requiem for Heroes<hex:021A020103>
31711.col_2: A masterfully rendered oil depiction of a noble warrior who journeyed across many a realm to fight for the sake of the common man. The flag-to-man ratio lends it a certain air of authenticity, and evokes images of a samurai rampaging through a textiles store.
31711.col_3: Authentic Copy of Requiem for Heroes

31712.name: authentic pumpkin carriage
31712.col_2: Someday your prince (or princess) will come. Probably not in this, though. The smell, however, is said to authentically resemble that of real pumpkins, though this is seldom considered a priority by potential passengers.

31713.name: authentic All Saints' Wake MMXV advertisement
31713.description: authentic All Saints' Wake MMXV advertisements
31713.col_2: A hand-painted notice advertising the fantastical festivities of an All Saints' Wake past. Authentic down to the last brushstroke? Absolutely. Nightmare-inducing and spine-tinglingly terrifying? Not so much.
31713.col_3: Authentic All Saints' Wake MMXV Advertisement

31736.name: oddly delicate saw part
31736.col_2: The words “delicate” and “saw” are seldom seen in such close proximity.

31737.name: oddly delicate cross-pein hammer part
31737.col_2: Presumably once this delicate part is attached to the rest of the tool, it will somehow gain the ability to withstand all the hammering that is sure to follow.

31738.name: oddly delicate raising hammer part
31738.col_2: Thankfully the pot used to house the part and the protective jelly in which it is suspended are considerably less delicate. Obviously shaking or dropping it would be extremely ill-advised.

31739.name: oddly delicate lapidary hammer part
31739.col_2: A small round pot may not seem the obvious choice for the transportation of parts of any kind, regardless of their delicate nature, but perhaps the Skysteel engineers had a surplus of them lying about the manufactory.

31740.name: oddly delicate round knife part
31740.col_2: Some of the Skysteel engineers fear that due to its delicate nature, this particular part may struggle to fit in with the rather more robust components that comprise the round knife.

31741.name: oddly delicate needle part
31741.col_2: Needles, by and large, tend not to include multiple parts, but the Skysteel engineers have ever sought to defy common sense.

31742.name: oddly delicate alembic part
31742.col_2: Even a standard alembic is rather fragile to begin with, so adding an oddly delicate part will only exacerbate the problem.

31743.name: oddly delicate frypan part
31743.col_2: One can only hope that the liberal application of heat does not offend this part's delicate sensibilities.

31744.name: oddly delicate hatchet part
31744.col_2: Once the hatchet is completed, one must remember to go about their hacking and slashing with great care so as not to spoil the oddly delicate part attached to it.

31745.name: inconceivably delicate hatchet part
31745.col_2: It would probably be sensible to protect this inconceivably delicate part with rather less delicate parts.

31746.name: oddly delicate pickaxe part
31746.col_2: Time will tell whether the addition of this oddly delicate part will actually improve one's ability to smash rocks into smaller rocks.

31747.name: inconceivably delicate pickaxe part
31747.col_2: Poor workmen who blame their tools will have no excuses once this piece is attached.

31748.name: oddly delicate fishing rod part
31748.col_2: Your fellow anglers will no doubt be impressed by the length to which you have gone to improve your fishing rod. After all, showing off in front of others is what fishing is all about.

31749.name: oddly delicate fishing reel part
31749.col_2: Only the most dedicated of fishers would even consider the use of such an oddly delicate component, but the obsessive pursuit of the very best equipment available is as much a part of the hobby as actually catching the fish.

31750.name: length of oddly delicate pine lumber
31750.description: lengths of oddly delicate pine lumber
31750.col_2: Though it may seem as sturdy as any other length of lumber, it will be robbed of its intrinsic qualities if one so much as sneezes near it.

31751.name: oddly delicate silver gear
31751.col_2: Perhaps it would be prudent to match this gear with others of a similarly delicate disposition.

31752.name: oddly delicate wolfram square
31752.col_2: This delicate square must be treated with the utmost care before holding it over a blazing forge and smashing it repeatedly with a hammer.

31753.name: oddly delicate celestine
31753.col_2: The rays of light refracted by this crystal are so delicate that they can be broken simply by waving one's hand through them.

31754.name: circle of oddly delicate gazelle leather
31754.description: circles of oddly delicate gazelle leather
31754.col_2: This leather somehow managed to retain its delicacy despite being subjected to the far-from-gentle tanning process.

31755.name: bolt of oddly delicate rhea cloth
31755.description: bolts of oddly delicate rhea cloth
31755.col_2: Great care must be taken not to stretch, crumple, crease, or─if possible─touch this specimen, lest its intrinsic delicateness be marred.

31756.name: bottle of oddly delicate holy water
31756.description: bottles of oddly delicate holy water
31756.col_2: Most water is delicate by its very nature, this sort even more so.

31757.name: bottle of oddly delicate shark oil
31757.description: bottles of oddly delicate shark oil
31757.col_2: The treatment to which the shark was subjected to extract its oil was anything but delicate.

31758.name: oddly delicate pine log
31758.col_2: Yes, this is a delicate log. Oddly so, in fact.

31759.name: chunk of oddly delicate silvergrace ore
31759.description: chunks of oddly delicate silvergrace ore
31759.col_2: For all its delicacy, this is nevertheless a chunk of ore, and quite capable of leaving a nasty mark when thrown at someone's head.

31760.name: chunk of oddly delicate scheelite
31760.col_2: While standard scheelite is certainly rare, the oddly delicate variant is scarce to the point of being practically nonexistent.

31761.name: oddly delicate raw celestine
31761.col_2: This chunk of unrefined crystal is not itself especially delicate, but has the potential to produce pieces of remarkable delicacy. Whether this is beneficial in any way whatsoever, however, remains to be seen.

31762.name: oddly delicate gazelle hide
31762.col_2: Rest assured that the gazelle to which this once belonged was slaughtered in the most delicate way possible.

31763.name: stalk of oddly delicate rhea
31763.col_2: Rhea this oddly delicate is reserved for the production of oddly delicate rhea cloth. It is then, in turn, used to make all sorts of cloth-based items, provided that they are not hindered in any way by being oddly delicate, which rules out practically everything.

31764.name: sprig of oddly delicate mistletoe
31764.col_2: If one happens to eat one of these poisonous berries, they may find that their stomach also becomes oddly delicate.

31765.name: oddly delicate hammerhead shark
31765.col_2: The “oddly delicate” part refers not to the shark's physical attributes, but to its demeanor. Due to being dead, however, this is something of a moot point.

31766.name: oddly delicate feather
31766.col_2: For all the feathers adorning a cloudkin's body, only a rare few could be considered oddly delicate. Those are generally found around the wingpit, the avian equivalent of an armpit, obviously.

31767.name: oddly delicate birch log
31767.col_2: Oddly delicate for a birch log, though still fairly hefty by most people's standards.

31768.name: chunk of oddly delicate adamantite ore
31768.description: chunks of oddly delicate adamantite ore
31768.col_2: Adamantite, as the name would suggest, is anything but delicate, though this particular sample is perhaps ever-so-slightly less than “practically indestructible.”

31769.name: piece of oddly delicate raw jade
31769.description: pieces of oddly delicate raw jade
31769.col_2: Hopefully not so delicate that it will shatter into a thousand pieces at the first attempt to refine it.

31770.name: flintstrike
31770.col_2: The glow it emits when swimming through the ocean depths is reminiscent of sparks flying from a struck flint. Thankfully, it does not present an actual fire hazard, despite what some may think.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be caught when equipped with a skysung fishing rod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

31771.name: pickled pom
31771.col_2: Closely resembling a moogle's pom-pom, apart from the strange odor. Saying it smells pickled is a rather charitable description.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be caught when equipped with a skysung fishing rod.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]
