31903.col_2: A salad featuring chunks of golden pineapple tossed with a flavorsome frantoio oil dressing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

31904.name: serving of zefir
31904.col_2: An irresistibly soft and airy confectionary made from whipped twilight apple purée.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

31905.name: serving of twilight popoto salad
31905.col_2: Shredded twilight apples give this popoto salad a crunchy texture and fruity tang.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

31906.name: serving of broad bean curry
31906.col_2: Broad beans stewed with fragrant spices, served with a side of steamed rice.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

31907.name: lemon muffin
31907.col_2: A sweet and zesty muffin made by mixing lemonette rind and juice into the dough.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103><hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>EXP Bonus:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> +3% <hex:024804F201F803><hex:024904F201F903>Duration:<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> 30m<hex:02100103>(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

31908.name: slice of mozzarella
31908.col_2: A fresh, springy cheese made from buffalo milk.

31909.name: chicken thigh
31909.col_2: The thigh of a breed of chicken known for the superior flavor and texture of its flesh.

31910.name: golden pineapple
31910.col_2: A golden-hued variety of pineapple touted for its tart flavor.

31911.name: twilight apple
31911.col_2: A sweet-sour variety of apple named for the gentle gleam of its peel.

31912.name: handful of cardamom
31912.col_2: Boasting a unique fragrance, these seeds are the secret spice in myriad recipes.

31913.name: length of grade 4 skybuilders' plywood
31913.col_2: The skybuilders are known for plying their trade by applying plies to provide supplies of plywood. Now try saying that ten times fast with a mouthful of porridge.

31914.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' alloy
31914.col_2: A marvelous mixture of malleable metals melded into magnificently molded...blocks.

31915.name: grade 4 skybuilders' steel plate
31915.col_2: To be fair is rare, and to be square even rarer, but to be both fair and square is miraculous indeed.

31916.name: grade 4 skybuilders' ingot
31916.col_2: It is believed in certain circles that the word “ingot” is derived from the verb “to inget” meaning “to breathe in and out simultaneously, causing the air to become trapped in the larynx, creating a sound akin to a hiccupping buffalo.”

31917.name: circle of grade 4 skybuilders' leather
31917.col_2: The time and effort spent on cutting each hide into perfect circles would have been better spent on...well, anything else. Not to mention the amount of wasted leather now lying in a pile of offcuts. However, one thing can be said of the skybuilders: there is madness in their method.

31918.name: length of grade 4 skybuilders' rope
31918.col_2: While this may seem like a good choice for a children's skipping rope, it is weighty enough to leave a painful welt on either the temples or ankles of those with a poor sense of timing. Still, some might say that only adds to the fun.

31919.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' ink
31919.col_2: The grade 4 variety of ink is said to be especially quick-drying, which helps to prevent smudging. Some claim, however, that the ink dries before it even has time to reach the parchment, which does rather defeat the purpose of the ink in the first place.

31920.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' hemp milk
31920.description: bottles of grade 4 skybuilders' hemp milk
31920.col_2: “We challenged Ishgardians to taste the difference between hemp milk and a leading dairy-based competitor. Eight in ten participants claimed they tasted exactly the same, while the remainder complained of a stomachache from drinking too much milk.”<hex:02100103>─Culinarians' Guild researcher

31921.name: grade 4 skybuilders' crate
31921.col_2: “If you see a crate, try looking inside. There may be a small amount of gil or even potions or medicinal herbs inside. Don't worry about the owners catching you pilfering their wares; you'd be surprised how many are willing to turn a blind eye, especially if you're carrying a big sword.”<hex:02100103>─<hex:021A020203>Adventuring for Fun and Profit, First Edition<hex:021A020103>

31922.name: handful of grade 4 skybuilders' nails
31922.col_2: In traditional Doman carpentry, the wooden pieces are carefully carved to allow them to snugly interlock and remain steadfast for years to come. In Ishgard, however, the wood is considerably less cooperative, and must have little metal spikes driven through it to stay where it is told.

31923.name: handful of grade 4 skybuilders' rivets
31923.col_2: Although being covered in rivets tends to make basically anything look a lot more sturdy, the act of driving them in to begin with probably compromises the object's structural integrity to some degree. It certainly has that effect on a person's skull.

31924.name: handful of grade 4 skybuilders' rings
31924.col_2: Those who cannot afford proper metal gauntlets can try threading these metallic rings onto their fingers to produce a similar effect. Just be sure to keep your fists clenched to stop them falling off.

31925.name: bundle of grade 4 skybuilders' leather straps
31925.description: bundles of grade 4 skybuilders' leather straps
31925.col_2: The artisans responsible for the creation of such wares are often described as “strapping,” but usually in a literal rather than figurative sense.

31926.name: bolt of grade 4 skybuilders' cloth
31926.col_2: How long is a bolt of cloth? Twice as long from the middle to the end.

31927.name: phial of grade 4 skybuilders' plant oil
31927.description: phials of grade 4 skybuilders' plant oil

31928.name: grade 4 skybuilders' sesame cookie
31928.col_2: Ishgardian parents often tell their children that the sesame seeds are in fact dead flies that were trapped in the batter prior to baking. Not only does this have the effect of keeping the young ones' hands out of the cookie jar, it also leads them to a few raised eyebrows in regard to their parents' choice of confectionery.

31929.name: grade 4 skybuilders' spinning wheel
31929.col_2: One of the few wheels that can turn all day and not move an ilm.

31930.name: grade 4 skybuilders' hatchet
31930.col_2: A common choice of weapon in civilian uprisings, though it leaves much to be desired in the “long and pointy” stakes, unlike the ever-popular pitchfork.

31931.name: grade 4 skybuilders' cookpot
31931.col_2: Almost identical to the grade 3 version but with a better warranty, providing cover against “irremovable stains except for in cases where strange or unusual ingredients have been used, such as Lalafell fat.”

31932.name: grade 4 skybuilders' embroidery frame
31932.col_2: A frame so intricately detailed and immaculately crafted that it threatens to upstage the embroidery it is designed to keep in place.

31933.name: grade 4 skybuilders' leather sack
31933.col_2: The leather of this sack once held the flesh, bones, and organs of a large beast, but has now been granted the opportunity to store a much wider and more interesting range of objects. Unless, that is, it is purchased by a butcher, in which case the contents may end up being largely the same as its previous incarnation.

31934.name: grade 4 skybuilders' broom
31934.col_2: Combatants who claim they will “sweep the floor” with their opponent should try one of these brooms instead. Twice the cleanliness with none of the violence.

31935.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' holy water
31935.description: bottles of grade 4 skybuilders' holy water
31935.col_2: “Why's this called holy water? I don't see any holes in it.”<hex:02100103>─A confused and somewhat illiterate skybuilder

31936.name: cup of grade 4 skybuilders' tea
31936.col_2: Contains so much sugar that some claim the smell alone is enough to make one's teeth fall out.

31937.name: grade 4 skybuilders' stepladder
31937.col_2: “Takes just as many steps to climb up as it does to climb down” is the slogan used by the skybuilders when pitching their stepladders to potential customers, though any sales made tend to be in spite of said slogan rather than because of it.

31938.name: grade 4 skybuilders' crosscut saw
31938.col_2: Strangely enough, it is not particularly well suited to cutting crosses.

31939.name: grade 4 skybuilders' mesail
31939.col_2: As any smith will attest, the heat of the forge can be overwhelming. Were it not for the conveniently placed air holes, their heads would be baked inside their mesails like cow-brain pies (an Ishgardian delicacy).

31940.name: grade 4 skybuilders' stone
31940.col_2: Since ancient times, man has sought to move exceedingly large blocks of stone from one location to another. In the past, methods such as conveying the material atop a series of rolling logs or ferrying it on extremely buoyant rafts were employed, whereas all it requires these days is one plucky volunteer with bottomless pockets.

31941.name: pair of grade 4 skybuilders' longboots
31941.col_2: It is said that over the years, the design for longboots grew longer and longer, until the two boots eventually met in the middle and lost the part covering the foot entirely─perhaps to save on materials─and became what are now known as trousers.

31942.name: pair of grade 4 skybuilders' gloves
31942.col_2: Long have gloves waged war in the marketplace against mittens, their archrivals, though the wearer's ability to move each finger individually has proved to be a deciding factor in securing their popularity.

31943.name: bar of grade 4 skybuilders' soap
31943.col_2: In a stroke of sheer genius, the skybuilders have succeeded in inventing a variety of soap that floats on water, much to the delight of the people of Ishgard─those who actually wash, that is.

31944.name: grade 4 skybuilders' all-purpose infusion
31944.col_2: A remarkable concoction that is able to treat any ailment the salesperson is able to imagine. The lack of complaints following purchase indicates that the customer is either entirely satisfied with the effects, or dead from poisoning.

31945.name: grade 4 skybuilders' bed
31945.col_2: The mattress is made from a spongelike material to help absorb any...nocturnal spillages.

31946.name: grade 4 skybuilders' oven
31946.col_2: Sometimes, the phrase “she's got a bun in the oven” is meant to be taken literally. In fact, this common saying has led to all sorts of hilarious misunderstandings, particularly in cases where the woman in question likes to bake her own bread.

31947.name: grade 4 skybuilders' lamppost
31947.col_2: Spare a thought for the poor souls whose job it is to light each of the lanterns that line the streets of the Firmament every evening. Perhaps one day, someone will be so kind as to invent a system whereby they may be lit and extinguished remotely. Unfortunately, many of Ishgard's civic engineers are preoccupied with far more frivolous pursuits, such as imbuing tools with mystic energy using oddly specific materials.

31948.name: grade 4 skybuilders' brazier
31948.col_2: One must take great care not to confuse this with the similarly named ladies' undergarment.

31949.name: set of grade 4 skybuilders' overalls
31949.col_2: While it is common for mud, paint, and other stains to collect on overalls, some of the skybuilders have taken to deliberately dirtying their clothing to fool others into thinking they have been hard at work. Since a skybuilder's pay is largely based on their performance, however, those who attempt such tricks are normally left with naught but soiled overalls and empty pockets.

31950.name: grade 4 skybuilders' awning
31950.col_2: Is there anything more pleasant than yawning in the morning as day is dawning, beneath an awning?

31951.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' growth formula
31951.description: bottles of grade 4 skybuilders' growth formula
31951.col_2: There are rumors that claim the remarkable height of Elezen is due to doses of growth formula being slipped into their morning porridge from a young age. Attempts to reproduce such an effect on the Lalafells who willingly volunteered as test subjects have yet to yield results, other than an unnatural aversion to porridge.

31952.name: pot of grade 4 skybuilders' stew
31952.col_2: Many culinarians believe the secret to a good stew is to never allow the pot to become empty by constantly topping it up with fresh ingredients. This may in fact be an elaborate ploy to avoid ever having to wash the pot, not to mention that some parts of the stew may have been in the mix for several years without being served. Diners are advised to “eat around” anything that seems a bit suspicious.

31953.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' icebox
31953.col_2: Though such a device would seem to have little use in Ishgard, where foodstuffs may be kept chilled simply by placing them outside, the icebox does offer protection from rats and crows. But then again, so would any other type of box.

31954.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' chocobo weathervane
31954.col_2: If it starts spinning wildly, it means the wind is blowing in all of the directions at once.

31955.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' company chest
31955.col_2: This communal deposit relies on the honesty of not only every member of the company─to give what they can and take only what they need─but every other person who passes through the Firmament, as it is left completely unlocked at all times. The members of said companies are often surprised to find the chest completely empty upon opening it, while opportunistic thieves enjoy their easy pickings.

31956.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' astroscope
31956.col_2: Such devices are often found pointing in the direction of the open-air baths, which is in keeping with the letter─rather than the spirit─of its intended purpose, that being “the observation of heavenly bodies.”

31957.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' tool belt
31957.col_2: While it may not seem especially voluminous, this belt is capable of holding up to thirty-five primary tools and the same number of secondary tools. One might have trouble actually moving with an entire shed's worth of heavy equipment hanging from one's waist, however.

31958.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' vest
31958.col_2: Far more luxurious than most other garments of its kind, with a price to match. Most would think twice before investing in this vest.

31959.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' tincture
31959.col_2: “Should you find any mysterious phials of liquid, be sure to take them with you. After all, the clinking of glass from all the potions, ethers, and elixirs an adventurer is known for carrying about their person is one of the easiest ways for a potential client to distinguish them from a marauding barbarian.”<hex:02100103>─<hex:021A020203>Adventuring for Fun and Profit, First Edition<hex:021A020103>

31960.name: cup of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' sorbet
31960.description: cups of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' sorbet
31960.col_2: Although a lot of care and effort went into the preparation of this sweet treat, a similar effect could easily be achieved by leaving a glass of fruit juice outside in the cold Ishgardian air for half a bell or so.

31961.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' switch
31961.col_2: As many Ishgardian schoolchildren will attest, telling one's detractors “Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words shall never harm me” is an open invitation to be assaulted with said objects.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31962.name: tuft of approved grade 4 skybuilders' hemp
31962.description: tufts of approved grade 4 skybuilders' hemp
31962.col_2: Since time immemorial, this robust plant has helped many a convicted criminal dance the hempen jig.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31963.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' iron ore
31963.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' iron ore
31963.col_2: Any smith worth their salt will have a vast amount of ores, ingots, rivets, rings, and plates at their disposal, although finding space to store it all can prove most bothersome. Some have even taken to employing retainers for the sole purpose of lugging their surplus junk around.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31964.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' iron sand
31964.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' iron sand
31964.col_2: Primarily used as a vital component in a children's toy whereby hair and a beard may be applied to a picture of a man's face by means of an ingenious magnetic wand. (For ages three and up.)<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31965.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' mahogany log
31965.col_2: Used in the construction of various musical instruments and believed to imbue the music with a certain ethereal quality. This may or may not be due to the souls of elementals trapped within the wood, which brings a whole new meaning to the phrase “haunting melody.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31966.name: tuft of approved grade 4 skybuilders' sesame
31966.description: tufts of approved grade 4 skybuilders' sesame
31966.col_2: The sesame plant is robust enough to grow in even the most inhospitable environments, including those in which the botanists tasked with gathering said plant are incapable of surviving. As valuable as sesame is, most would agree it is not worth risking life and limb for, not that the skybuilders seem particularly bothered by this when making their requests...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31967.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' cotton boll
31967.col_2: A freshly picked cotton boll with the stem still attached is the perfect implement for cleaning one's ears, though it is likely that the skybuilders will notice if that same cotton boll is submitted to them after being used. They tend to object to that sort of thing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31968.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' ore
31968.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' ore
31968.col_2: Only a true skybuilder could look at a nondescript lump of grey, slightly metallic rock and say, “Yes, this is definitely grade 4 skybuilders' ore,” though it could be argued that this is because they are the ones who named it to begin with.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31969.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' rock salt
31969.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' rock salt
31969.col_2: “But Mother, can we not break the salt rock into smaller chunks to save us all from having to lick the same piece? It seems awfully unhygienic.”<hex:02100103>“No, my sweet prince, that would not be proper. Now lick the rock and put it back on the table.”<hex:02100103>─Typical Ishgardian mealtime conversation<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31970.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mythrite sand
31970.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mythrite sand
31970.col_2: A popular choice for hourglasses as the speed at which the sand falls is directly affected by how much those in close proximity are enjoying themselves. With a mythrite sand hourglass, time really does fly when one is having fun.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31971.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' spruce log
31971.col_2: Spruce is the wood of choice in all manner of carpentry projects, from enormous load-bearing beams to tiny intricately carved ornaments. So versatile is it that one wonders why the skybuilders even bother with the other types of timber.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31972.name: sprig of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mistletoe
31972.description: sprigs of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mistletoe
31972.col_2: A prominent feature in many Starlight Celebration decorations, mistletoe is much loved by the people of Ishgard. Most people would probably view it rather differently, however, if they knew that the plant is in fact a voracious parasite that mercilessly drains the life from its host.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31973.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' toad
31973.col_2: You had best treat this warty little creature kindly as it may be a ninja's hellfrog in disguise. “Burned to death by flaming frog vomit” is hardly the sort of remark one wants in their obituary.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31974.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' vine
31974.col_2: Although such vines make perfectly adequate replacements for rope, it seems that the skybuilders have more than enough actual rope to make the use of this plant somewhat redundant.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31975.name: basket of approved grade 4 skybuilders' tea leaves
31975.description: baskets of approved grade 4 skybuilders' tea leaves
31975.col_2: “There are few problems that cannot be resolved─or at least, forgotten about─over a nice cup of tea.”<hex:02100103>─Ishgardian aphorism<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31976.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' electrum ore
31976.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' electrum ore
31976.col_2: A naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver, though many would argue that it is worth less than the sum of its parts. Those expecting it to possess some sort of lightning-aspected aetherial properties due to the name are sure to be disappointed, although that has not prevented several unscrupulous merchants from advertising it as such.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31977.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' alumen
31977.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' alumen
31977.col_2: Another in a seemingly endless list of powdered substances that are of vital importance to alchemists, goldsmiths, and the like, but mean─to quote the common vernacular─bugger all to everyone else. Luckily, laymen need only know how much it will fetch at market and whether or not one must face any life-endangering peril to obtain it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31978.name: bottle of approved grade 4 skybuilders' spring water
31978.description: bottles of approved grade 4 skybuilders' spring water
31978.col_2: A number of stringent tests are performed to determine the grade assigned to spring water, including the measurement of time taken to evaporate when poured into a shallow dish and placed next to a hot pig.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31979.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' gold sand
31979.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' gold sand
31979.col_2: Each grain of gold sand was once a whole nugget that has been gradually eroded over many thousands of years, which is a rather extreme example of depreciating value.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31980.name: slab of approved grade 4 skybuilders' ragstone
31980.description: slabs of approved grade 4 skybuilders' ragstone
31980.col_2: Due to being formed from compressed layers of sediment, ragstone may contain rare and precious fossils. The skybuilders, however, care not a jot about any of that and will happily use it to whet their blades and so forth, much to the woe of naturalists throughout Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

31981.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' white cedar log
31981.description: approved grade 4 skybuilders' white cedar logs
31981.col_2: White cedar is known to be one of the most longevous species of tree, with one particular specimen estimated to be 1,852 years old, according to the number of growth rings. Of course, it probably would have lived a lot longer if not for a glory-seeking, axe-happy botanist.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31981.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Skybuilders' White Cedar Log

31982.name: lump of approved grade 4 skybuilders' primordial resin
31982.description: lumps of approved grade 4 skybuilders' primordial resin
31982.col_2: Made from congealed primordial soup.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31983.name: sheaf of approved grade 4 skybuilders' wheat
31983.description: sheaves of approved grade 4 skybuilders' wheat
31983.col_2: Ishgardian bakers organize a gathering known as a “wheat and greet,” in which they discuss a range of topics, such as the perfect method for wafting the smell of freshly baked bread into the streets to maximize profits.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31984.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' gossamer cotton boll
31984.description: approved grade 4 skybuilders' gossamer cotton bolls
31984.col_2: When it comes to cotton bolls, this is the sovereign of softness, the commandant of comfort, the liege lord of loveliness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31984.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Skybuilders' Gossamer Cotton Boll

31985.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' tortoise
31985.col_2: Those who believe dogs are man's best friend have obviously never met a tortoise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31986.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' gold ore
31986.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' gold ore
31986.col_2: “The ambassador's receptions are noted in society for their host's exquisite taste that captivates his guests. The tray of gold nuggets his butlers pass around, however, often leads to confusion and broken teeth when said guests mistake them for chocolate treats.”<hex:02100103>─<hex:021A020203>The Highs and Lows of Ishgardian High Society<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31987.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31987.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' finest rock salt
31987.col_2: This particular variety of rock salt has proved so popular with Ishgardian diners, that many choose to forgo their meal altogether and spend the evening licking the communal salt rock instead.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.
31987.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Skybuilders' Finest Rock Salt

31988.name: bottle of approved grade 4 skybuilders' truespring water
31988.description: bottles of approved grade 4 skybuilders' truespring water
31988.col_2: The advertising slogan, “Spring water never tasted so true,” has left many Ishgardians both impressed and baffled in equal measure. Merchants are hopeful that this will cause just the right amount of confusion to distract from the fact it is essentially identical to the grade 3 variety. And any other type of water, for that matter.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31989.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mineral sand
31989.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' mineral sand
31989.col_2: When the skybuilders were quizzed as to exactly what type of mineral comprises this sand, the reply was, “That information is on a need-to-know basis.” One would assume that those mining the stuff would need to know what they are supposed to be looking for, but the skybuilders move─and think─in mysterious ways.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31990.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' bluespirit ore
31990.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' bluespirit ore
31990.col_2: Not only is this rock imbued with a spirit, but that spirit is feeling particularly blue. Perhaps being smashed repeatedly with a chisel will cheer it up.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31991.name: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' log
31991.col_2: The word “log” fails to amply convey the undeniable majesty of this immaculate specimen. Unfortunately, there are no suitable substitutes, unless one is content to call it a “tree with all the sticky-outy bits cut off.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31992.name: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' raspberry
31992.col_2: Being rather small, it is unusual for raspberries to be handled individually rather than by weight. This may also be because fruiterers are keen to avoid counting anything other than coins.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31993.name: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' caiman
31993.col_2: In this case, “artisanal” refers to the caiman itself rather than the person tasked with procuring it. This scalekin is particularly gifted in the art of nest building, or at least it was before being clobbered over the head and dragged off to the skybuilders.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31994.name: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cocoon
31994.col_2: As the skybuilders neglected to specify the exact type of cocoon they would like delivered, its contents remain unknown. It could be home to anything from a wamoura pupa to the larva of a parasitic wespe. Nothing good, in other words.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31995.name: clump of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' barbgrass
31995.description: clumps of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' barbgrass
31995.col_2: The countless tiny barbs at the tips of this hardy plant are believed to deter grazing beastkin. However, to counteract this, those creatures have developed an especially tough lining to the inside of their mouths, and could probably bite down on a handful of broken glass without so much as batting an eyelid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31996.name: chunk of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31996.description: chunks of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
31996.col_2: According to certain scholars, the islands of the Sea of Clouds are kept suspended in the air by large amounts of cloudstone. It is therefore advised not to mine too much of this valuable resource as it may cause the island to plummet from the sky.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

31997.name: bottle of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
31997.description: bottles of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
31997.col_2: Spring water is said to result from a series of complex processes that unfold deep underground. But in a place like the Diadem, where the normal laws of nature appear to be ignored entirely, it is impossible to say exactly where this water comes from.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31997.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Artisanal Skybuilders' Spring Water

31998.name: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' ice stalagmite
31998.description: approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' ice stalagmites
31998.col_2: Be sure to hold this the right way up or it could be mistaken for a stalactite.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
31998.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Artisanal Skybuilders' Ice Stalagmite

31999.name: sack of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' silex
31999.description: sacks of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' silex
31999.col_2: Similar─though rather less artisanal─sacks of silex are sold to the participants in Ul'dah's Coliseum. A well-aimed handful of the stuff can temporarily blind the opponent, though it is only a matter of time until these customers realize that the same is true of the sand that lines the arena floor, which is available for free.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32000.name: chunk of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' prismstone
32000.description: chunks of approved grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' prismstone
32000.col_2: Shines with all the colors of the rainbow, and even a few extra, like luminous black and fluorescent beige.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32001.name: approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral galewood branch
32001.description: approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral galewood branches
32001.col_2: The billowing wind-aspected aether that surrounds this branch might lead some to think it would be the ideal material from which to make a magic wand. Unfortunately, the energies within it are so powerful, the wielder would struggle to even hold on to it long enough to cast any spells before it blows right out of their hands.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral tempest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.
32001.col_3: Approved Grade 4 Skybuilders' Umbral Galewood Branch

32002.name: clump of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral dirtleaf
32002.description: clumps of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral dirtleaf
32002.col_2: One of the only plants known to grow its leaves underground before allowing them to surface. The fine covering of dirt seems to have the adverse effect of hindering the leaves from doing...whatever it is leaves do, which may explain the shrub's rather short stature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral duststorm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32003.name: chunk of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral flarerock
32003.description: chunks of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral flarerock
32003.col_2: Each chunk of flarerock is capable of releasing enormous amounts of fire-aspected aether. Unfortunately, for that to occur, it must first be warmed for three days under a medium-sized duck, which limits its usefulness somewhat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral flare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32004.name: pinch of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral levinsand
32004.description: pinches of approved grade 4 skybuilders' umbral levinsand
32004.col_2: Exactly like any other type of sand, apart from the fact it is bright purple and may or may not electrocute those who get too close.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during umbral levin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32005.name: grade 4 skybuilders' switch
32005.col_2: As many Ishgardian schoolchildren will attest, telling one's detractors “Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words shall never harm me” is an open invitation to be assaulted with said objects.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32006.name: tuft of grade 4 skybuilders' hemp
32006.col_2: Since time immemorial, this robust plant has helped many a convicted criminal dance the hempen jig.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32007.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' iron ore
32007.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' iron ore
32007.col_2: Any smith worth their salt will have a vast amount of ores, ingots, rivets, rings, and plates at their disposal, although finding space to store it all can prove most bothersome. Some have even taken to employing retainers for the sole purpose of lugging their surplus junk around.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32008.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' iron sand
32008.description: pinches of grade 4 skybuilders' iron sand
32008.col_2: Primarily used as a vital component in a children's toy whereby hair and a beard may be applied to a picture of a man's face by means of an ingenious magnetic wand. (For ages three and up.)<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32009.name: grade 4 skybuilders' mahogany log
32009.col_2: Used in the construction of various musical instruments and believed to imbue the music with a certain ethereal quality. This may or may not be due to the souls of elementals trapped within the wood, which brings a whole new meaning to the phrase “haunting melody.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32010.name: tuft of grade 4 skybuilders' sesame
32010.col_2: The sesame plant is robust enough to grow in even the most inhospitable environments, including those in which the botanists tasked with gathering said plant are incapable of surviving. As valuable as sesame is, most would agree it is not worth risking life and limb for, not that the skybuilders seem particularly bothered by this when making their requests...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32011.name: grade 4 skybuilders' cotton boll
32011.col_2: A freshly picked cotton boll with the stem still attached is the perfect implement for cleaning one's ears, though it is likely that the skybuilders will notice if that same cotton boll is submitted to them after being used. They tend to object to that sort of thing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32012.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' ore
32012.col_2: Only a true skybuilder could look at a nondescript lump of grey, slightly metallic rock and say, “Yes, this is definitely grade 4 skybuilders' ore,” though it could be argued that this is because they are the ones who named it to begin with.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32013.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' rock salt
32013.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' rock salt
32013.col_2: “But Mother, can we not break the salt rock into smaller chunks to save us all from having to lick the same piece? It seems awfully unhygienic.”<hex:02100103>“No, my sweet prince, that would not be proper. Now lick the rock and put it back on the table.”<hex:02100103>─Typical Ishgardian mealtime conversation<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32014.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' mythrite sand
32014.description: pinches of grade 4 skybuilders' mythrite sand
32014.col_2: A popular choice for hourglasses as the speed at which the sand falls is directly affected by how much those in close proximity are enjoying themselves. With a mythrite sand hourglass, time really does fly when one is having fun.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32015.name: grade 4 skybuilders' spruce log
32015.col_2: Spruce is the wood of choice in all manner of carpentry projects, from enormous load-bearing beams to tiny intricately carved ornaments. So versatile is it that one wonders why the skybuilders even bother with the other types of timber.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32016.name: sprig of grade 4 skybuilders' mistletoe
32016.col_2: A prominent feature in many Starlight Celebration decorations, mistletoe is much loved by the people of Ishgard. Most people would probably view it rather differently, however, if they knew that the plant is in fact a voracious parasite that mercilessly drains the life from its host.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32017.name: grade 4 skybuilders' toad
32017.col_2: You had best treat this warty little creature kindly as it may be a ninja's hellfrog in disguise. “Burned to death by flaming frog vomit” is hardly the sort of remark one wants in their obituary.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32018.name: grade 4 skybuilders' vine
32018.col_2: Although such vines make perfectly adequate replacements for rope, it seems that the skybuilders have more than enough actual rope to make the use of this plant somewhat redundant.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32019.name: basket of grade 4 skybuilders' tea leaves
32019.description: baskets of grade 4 skybuilders' tea leaves
32019.col_2: “There are few problems that cannot be resolved─or at least, forgotten about─over a nice cup of tea.”<hex:02100103>─Ishgardian aphorism<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32020.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' electrum ore
32020.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' electrum ore
32020.col_2: A naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver, though many would argue that it is worth less than the sum of its parts. Those expecting it to possess some sort of lightning-aspected aetherial properties due to the name are sure to be disappointed, although that has not prevented several unscrupulous merchants from advertising it as such.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32021.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' alumen
32021.col_2: Another in a seemingly endless list of powdered substances that are of vital importance to alchemists, goldsmiths, and the like, but mean─to quote the common vernacular─bugger all to everyone else. Luckily, laymen need only know how much it will fetch at market and whether or not one must face any life-endangering peril to obtain it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32022.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' spring water
32022.description: bottles of grade 4 skybuilders' spring water
32022.col_2: A number of stringent tests are performed to determine the grade assigned to spring water, including the measurement of time taken to evaporate when poured into a shallow dish and placed next to a hot pig.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32023.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' gold sand
32023.description: pinches of grade 4 skybuilders' gold sand
32023.col_2: Each grain of gold sand was once a whole nugget that has been gradually eroded over many thousands of years, which is a rather extreme example of depreciating value.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32024.name: slab of grade 4 skybuilders' ragstone
32024.col_2: Due to being formed from compressed layers of sediment, ragstone may contain rare and precious fossils. The skybuilders, however, care not a jot about any of that and will happily use it to whet their blades and so forth, much to the woe of naturalists throughout Eorzea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32025.name: grade 4 skybuilders' white cedar log
32025.col_2: White cedar is known to be one of the most longevous species of tree, with one particular specimen estimated to be 1,852 years old, according to the number of growth rings. Of course, it probably would have lived a lot longer if not for a glory-seeking, axe-happy botanist.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32026.name: lump of grade 4 skybuilders' primordial resin
32026.description: lumps of grade 4 skybuilders' primordial resin
32026.col_2: Made from congealed primordial soup.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32027.name: sheaf of grade 4 skybuilders' wheat
32027.col_2: Ishgardian bakers organize a gathering known as a “wheat and greet,” in which they discuss a range of topics, such as the perfect method for wafting the smell of freshly baked bread into the streets to maximize profits.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32028.name: grade 4 skybuilders' gossamer cotton boll
32028.col_2: When it comes to cotton bolls, this is the sovereign of softness, the commandant of comfort, the liege lord of loveliness.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32029.name: grade 4 skybuilders' tortoise
32029.col_2: Those who believe dogs are man's best friend have obviously never met a tortoise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32030.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' gold ore
32030.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' gold ore
32030.col_2: “The ambassador's receptions are noted in society for their host's exquisite taste that captivates his guests. The tray of gold nuggets his butlers pass around, however, often leads to confusion and broken teeth when said guests mistake them for chocolate treats.”<hex:02100103>─<hex:021A020203>The Highs and Lows of Ishgardian High Society<hex:021A020103><hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32031.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' finest rock salt
32031.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' finest rock salt
32031.col_2: This particular variety of rock salt has proved so popular with Ishgardian diners, that many choose to forgo their meal altogether and spend the evening licking the communal salt rock instead.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32032.name: bottle of grade 4 skybuilders' truespring water
32032.description: bottles of grade 4 skybuilders' truespring water
32032.col_2: The advertising slogan, “Spring water never tasted so true,” has left many Ishgardians both impressed and baffled in equal measure. Merchants are hopeful that this will cause just the right amount of confusion to distract from the fact it is essentially identical to the grade 3 variety. And any other type of water, for that matter.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32033.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' mineral sand
32033.description: pinches of grade 4 skybuilders' mineral sand
32033.col_2: When the skybuilders were quizzed as to exactly what type of mineral comprises this sand, the reply was, “That information is on a need-to-know basis.” One would assume that those mining the stuff would need to know what they are supposed to be looking for, but the skybuilders move─and think─in mysterious ways.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32034.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' bluespirit ore
32034.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' bluespirit ore
32034.col_2: Not only is this rock imbued with a spirit, but that spirit is feeling particularly blue. Perhaps being smashed repeatedly with a chisel will cheer it up.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32035.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' log
32035.col_2: The word “log” fails to amply convey the undeniable majesty of this immaculate specimen. Unfortunately, there are no suitable substitutes, unless one is content to call it a “tree with all the sticky-outy bits cut off.”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32036.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' raspberry
32036.col_2: Being rather small, it is unusual for raspberries to be handled individually rather than by weight. This may also be because fruiterers are keen to avoid counting anything other than coins.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32037.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' caiman
32037.col_2: In this case, “artisanal” refers to the caiman itself rather than the person tasked with procuring it. This scalekin is particularly gifted in the art of nest building, or at least it was before being clobbered over the head and dragged off to the skybuilders.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32038.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cocoon
32038.col_2: As the skybuilders neglected to specify the exact type of cocoon they would like delivered, its contents remain unknown. It could be home to anything from a wamoura pupa to the larva of a parasitic wespe. Nothing good, in other words.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32039.name: clump of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' barbgrass
32039.description: clumps of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' barbgrass
32039.col_2: The countless tiny barbs at the tips of this hardy plant are believed to deter grazing beastkin. However, to counteract this, those creatures have developed an especially tough lining to the inside of their mouths, and could probably bite down on a handful of broken glass without so much as batting an eyelid.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32040.name: chunk of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
32040.description: chunks of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' cloudstone
32040.col_2: According to certain scholars, the islands of the Sea of Clouds are kept suspended in the air by large amounts of cloudstone. It is therefore advised not to mine too much of this valuable resource as it may cause the island to plummet from the sky.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32041.name: bottle of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
32041.description: bottles of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' spring water
32041.col_2: Spring water is said to result from a series of complex processes that unfold deep underground. But in a place like the Diadem, where the normal laws of nature appear to be ignored entirely, it is impossible to say exactly where this water comes from.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32042.name: grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' ice stalagmite
32042.col_2: Be sure to hold this the right way up or it could be mistaken for a stalactite.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32043.name: sack of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' silex
32043.description: sacks of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' silex
32043.col_2: Similar─though rather less artisanal─sacks of silex are sold to the participants in Ul'dah's Coliseum. A well-aimed handful of the stuff can temporarily blind the opponent, though it is only a matter of time until these customers realize that the same is true of the sand that lines the arena floor, which is available for free.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32044.name: chunk of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' prismstone
32044.description: chunks of grade 4 artisanal skybuilders' prismstone
32044.col_2: Shines with all the colors of the rainbow, and even a few extra, like luminous black and fluorescent beige.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32045.name: grade 4 skybuilders' umbral galewood branch
32045.col_2: The billowing wind-aspected aether that surrounds this branch might lead some to think it would be the ideal material from which to make a magic wand. Unfortunately, the energies within it are so powerful, the wielder would struggle to even hold on to it long enough to cast any spells before it blows right out of their hands.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral tempest.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32046.name: clump of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral dirtleaf
32046.description: clumps of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral dirtleaf
32046.col_2: One of the only plants known to grow its leaves underground before allowing them to surface. The fine covering of dirt seems to have the adverse effect of hindering the leaves from doing...whatever it is leaves do, which may explain the shrub's rather short stature.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral duststorm.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32047.name: chunk of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral flarerock
32047.description: chunks of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral flarerock
32047.col_2: Each chunk of flarerock is capable of releasing enormous amounts of fire-aspected aether. Unfortunately, for that to occur, it must first be warmed for three days under a medium-sized duck, which limits its usefulness somewhat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during an umbral flare.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32048.name: pinch of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral levinsand
32048.description: pinches of grade 4 skybuilders' umbral levinsand
32048.col_2: Exactly like any other type of sand, apart from the fact it is bright purple and may or may not electrocute those who get too close.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Can only be gathered during umbral levin.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Used in expert crafting recipes.

32049.name: moonlight guppy
32049.col_2: A queen among platinum guppies, and lady of the waters of the rusted reservoir.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32050.name: Steel Fan
32050.col_2: A king among noble's fans, and lord of the waters of White Oil Falls.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32051.name: henodus grandis
32051.col_2: A king among henodus, and lord of the waters off the eastern Kholusian coast.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32052.name: sunken tome
32052.col_2: A king among spotted ctenopoma, and lord of the waters of the Haughty One.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32053.name: pearl pipira
32053.col_2: A queen among diamond pipira, and lady of the waters of the Red Chalice.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32054.name: the Ondotaker
32054.col_2: A queen among Ondobane, and lady of the waters of Where the Dry Return.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

32055.name: tortoiseshell crab
32055.col_2: Somewhere out there is bound to be a crabshell tortoise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32056.name: lady's cameo
32056.col_2: Initially named after a famous piece of jewelry, it has since become a favorite among goldsmiths crafting pieces of their own.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32057.name: metallic boxfish
32057.col_2: Although this wavekin only inflates to a box shape when threatened, having a fisher's hook through its lip seems to be enough to trigger this response. As a result, they are rarely seen in a deflated state.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32058.name: goobbue ray
32058.col_2: While this wavekin has much in common with the goobbues from which it gained its name, perhaps most noticeable is the expression of gormless contentment permanently etched on its face.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32059.name: watermoura
32059.col_2: While it moves with undeniable grace, the effect is rather spoiled by its brutish appearance.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32060.name: king cobrafish
32060.col_2: As a general rule, fish named after snakes are best left well alone.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32061.name: mamahi-mahi
32061.col_2: Its decidedly maternal-sounding name alludes to its remarkable fecundity.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32062.name: lavandin remora
32062.col_2: Often confused with the similarly named lavender remora, but considering that they both taste more or less the same, this is little cause for concern.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32063.name: spectral butterfly
32063.col_2: Some believe their appearance to be an omen of considerable riches on the horizon. Considering that these wavekin fetch a pretty gil at market, perhaps there is some truth to it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 1 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32064.name: Cieldalaes geode
32064.col_2: The true beauty of this wavekin is on the inside, whereas on the outside, it looks like a coblyn in a bad mood.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32065.name: titanshell crab
32065.col_2: Those wishing to sample the succulent meat inside must first contend with its near-impenetrable shell. Or alternatively, have the fishmonger do that part for them beforehand.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32066.name: mythril boxfish
32066.col_2: Valued more for its boxlike remains than for its meat, which is astonishingly mediocre.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32067.name: Mistbeard's cup
32067.col_2: Judging by its volume, perhaps “Mistbeard's flagon” would have been a more apt name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32068.name: anomalocaris saron
32068.col_2: At a certain point in history, this wavekin simply stopped evolving. Its lackluster appearance would suggest that this is not due to having achieved unsurpassable perfection, but rather a lack of ambition on the part of the species as a whole.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32069.name: flaming eel
32069.col_2: Sought more for its oil than for its meat, which is─as one might expect─rather oily.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32070.name: jetborne manta
32070.col_2: Clever fishers will often latch onto one of these wavekin and use its extraordinary propulsion to pull their ships. Once it grows tired, they can repay its kindness by hauling it out of the water and eating it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32071.name: devil's sting
32071.col_2: It is best to catch this vicious wavekin before it catches you.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32072.name: callichthyid
32072.col_2: Being extremely heavy and covered in armored plates, attempting to catch and eat this wavekin is often more trouble than it is worth. Many fishers will cut their lines upon realizing they have snagged one.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

32073.name: meandering Mora
32073.col_2: Content to simply drift through life with barely a care in the world, this fish is so lazy that it feeds by opening its mouth on the off chance that something edible might find its way inside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32074.name: Hafgufa
32074.col_2: This man-eating wavekin is so vast and ferocious that catching it seems more like a task for hardened warriors than amateur fishers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

32075.name: Thaliak crab
32075.col_2: Something of an anomaly among crabs as it spends its life moving back and forth between salt- and freshwater. Its flavor differs according to where it is caught.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32076.name: Star of the Destroyer
32076.col_2: Believed by some to be living fragments of Rhalgr's beacon, their gentle glow from beneath the waves is a welcome sight to many a sailor.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32077.name: true scad
32077.col_2: Let none doubt the trueness of this scad.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32078.name: blooded wrasse
32078.col_2: Fishers should not feel guilty for the bloodstains on the fish's head, as these are largely self-inflicted. They can instead feel guilty about the hook through the mouth, as well as the gutting and cleaning that comes shortly after.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32079.name: bloodpolish crab
32079.col_2: These wavekin cover their claws in blood to make themselves presentable to potential mates. Though this may seem odd, perhaps it is best not to attempt to understand the inner workings of a crab's mind.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32080.name: blue stitcher
32080.col_2: Considering its thin legs are often likened to needles, one cannot expect to get much meat from them. The torso, on the other hand, is a firm favorite among seafarers.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32081.name: bloodfresh tuna
32081.col_2: Its blood red meat is the centerpiece of many expensive dishes, though some claim it is chosen more for its appearance than its taste.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32082.name: sunken mask
32082.col_2: Though inanimate objects are seldom a welcome sight on a fisher's line, the goblin owner of this mask would no doubt be prepared to pay a small fortune to have it returned.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32083.name: spectral eel
32083.col_2: Do not be fooled by its heavenly aura, for there is naught mystical about this wavekin. In fact, it should be battered over the head before it has the chance to bite someone.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32084.name: bareface
32084.col_2: Said to resemble an unmasked goblin, not that most people would know what that looks like...<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32085.name: oracular crab
32085.col_2: While bloodpolish crabs are certainly frightening, this larger and more violent relative is nothing less than a nightmare come to life.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32086.name: Dravanian bream
32086.col_2: With all the hellish waterborne fiends and bizarre creatures that seem like the product of a fever dream, sometimes it makes a welcome change to meet a nice, normal fish.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32087.name: Skaldminni
32087.col_2: Though it is said that this wavekin is the instrument of a fabled bard given life, the awkward flopping sound it makes when landed is anything but musical.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32088.name: serrated clam
32088.col_2: While this clam may look far more imposing than most, one must remind oneself that it is still only a clam, and only capable of causing a very limited amount of harm. Still, it is best to watch one's fingers, all the same.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32089.name: beatific vision
32089.col_2: After too long at sea, even this horrendously ugly fish can seem almost like a visitation from a divine being. Almost.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32090.name: exterminator
32090.col_2: Experienced fishers will make sure this insatiable wavekin is well and truly dead before putting it anywhere near their other catches, otherwise it will devour them in a matter of moments.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32091.name: gory tuna
32091.col_2: To survive amongst such vicious company, this fish needs to be tough, which some would say is reflected in the texture of its meat.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32092.name: ticinepomis
32092.col_2: This fish moves so slowly that most other wavekin barely even realize it is alive, and pay it little heed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32093.name: quartz hammerhead
32093.col_2: This shark possesses extraordinarily strong neck muscles, which it needs to stop itself being dragged down to the seabed by its weighty head.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on extra large canvases.]

32094.name: seafaring toad
32094.col_2: The first sailors to spy one of these odd creatures at sea thought they had taken leave of their senses, or at the very least, had taken a wrong turn and somehow ended up in a pond.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32095.name: crow puffer
32095.col_2: Though it may be both feared and revered by its ocean-dwelling neighbors, even the most potent of natural defenses means little when dangling from a fisher's line.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32096.name: strip of Rothlyt kelp
32096.col_2: There are far easier ways to gather kelp than by reeling it in clump by clump, but most fishers will gladly accept such a “catch” rather than throw it back into the sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32097.name: living lantern
32097.col_2: A living lantern has a number of uses, assuming one can keep it alive. After all, it only retains its lantern-like qualities while it is living, hence the name.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32098.name: honeycomb fish
32098.col_2: It is remarkable how much this fish resembles a bee's nest, given that it has probably never even seen one before.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32099.name: godsbed
32099.col_2: One should refrain from attempting to use this bivalve as a bed, since this tends to reduce its value in the eyes of potential buyers. If they find out about it, that is.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32100.name: lansquenet
32100.col_2: Something of a mercenary among fish, it offers protection to smaller fish, though it seems to receive little in return. Perhaps it eats a few of them when the others are not looking?<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for display in aquariums tier 2 and higher.]<hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32101.name: Thavnairian shark
32101.col_2: Although there are countless species of shark, the main concern among fishers is “How likely is it to eat me?”<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32102.name: nephrite eel
32102.col_2: Some experts believe that the young nephrite eel's coloration helps it to hide among seaweed, which protects it from larger predators and offers a place from which to ambush prey of its own.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32103.name: spectresaur
32103.col_2: Eyewitnesses claim it to be the spirit of a long-dead seabeast. In truth, it is very much alive, which is probably a lot worse than if it were a ghost.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32104.name: ginkgo fin
32104.col_2: This minute wavekin cunningly disguises itself as a ginkgo leaf. This would be even more cunning, however, if ginkgo trees actually existed anywhere near the open sea.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32105.name: garum jug
32105.col_2: Those able to fight their way past the ink-like liquid emitted by this fish in defense will be rewarded with a tasty snack and a useful container.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32106.name: smooth jaguar
32106.col_2: While there are many wavekin named after lions and tigers, the majestic jaguar is criminally underrepresented.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32107.name: Rothlyt mussel
32107.col_2: Many fishmongers pride themselves on using every part of the creatures in which they deal. In the case of the mussel, however, there are only two parts to worry about: the shell and the...squishy thing inside.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32108.name: levi elver
32108.col_2: Of all the species of eel, levi elvers are said to most closely resemble Leviathan, although their much-reduced size does make them rather less imposing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32109.name: pearl bombfish
32109.col_2: Although bombfish do not actually explode in the same way as their namesakes, they look as if they could were they so inclined, which is enough to deter many would-be predators.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32110.name: trollfish
32110.col_2: Catching one of these brutes would be doing a great service to the other wavekin who share their waters.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32111.name: Panoptes
32111.col_2: The myriad dots that resemble eyes are said to confuse certain predators. This only works, however, if said predator actually cares whether it has been seen.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32112.name: crepe sole
32112.col_2: The story goes that it was named after an item of footwear. Whether or not this is true, the fact remains that it looks like it has been stepped on.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on small canvases.]

32113.name: knifejaw
32113.col_2: Must be handled with extreme care after being reeled in. Many fishers keep a long blade nearby to give it a good stabbing before even attempting to handle it.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on medium canvases.]

32114.name: placodus
32114.col_2: While its teeth specialize in crushing shellfish, it will not think twice before doing the same to a fisher's hands.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>[Suitable for printing on large canvases.]

32132.name: Emerald totem
32132.col_2: A metallic idol forged in the likeness of the Emerald Weapon.

32133.name: helm of lost antiquity
32133.col_2: A winged helmet forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Two helms can be traded for special headgear.

32134.name: suit of armor of lost antiquity
32134.description: suits of armor of lost antiquity
32134.col_2: Emblazoned armor forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Four suits can be traded for special body gear.

32135.name: pair of gauntlets of lost antiquity
32135.description: pairs of gauntlets of lost antiquity
32135.col_2: Wrought-iron gauntlets forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Two pairs can be traded for special arm gear.

32136.name: pair of chausses of lost antiquity
32136.description: pairs of chausses of lost antiquity
32136.col_2: Heavy chausses forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Four pairs can be traded for special leg gear.

32137.name: pair of greaves of lost antiquity
32137.description: pairs of greaves of lost antiquity
32137.col_2: Tarnished greaves forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Two pairs can be traded for special foot gear.

32138.name: belt of lost antiquity
32138.col_2: An ornamented belt created by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise. Alas, advancements in trouser technology have rendered it worthless.

32139.name: bangle of lost antiquity
32139.col_2: An extravagant bangle forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>One bangle can be traded for a special accessory.

32140.name: copy of the <hex:021A020203>Book of Umbra<hex:021A020103>
32140.col_2: A short apocryphal tome presumably created by Eden for recordkeeping purposes.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Copies of the same Eden's Promise apocrypha can be traded for special gear.

32141.name: copy of the <hex:021A020203>Book of Litany<hex:021A020103>

32150.col_2: A banded chest containing a piece of Edenmorn attire. Due to advancements in trouser technology, the belt within this chest is no longer worth the trouble of opening it.

32154.name: Edenmorn ring coffer (IL 530)

32155.name: blade of lost antiquity
32155.col_2: A golden blade forged by some ancient civilization, recovered from Eden's Promise. Though such weapons were once considered highly valuable, demand has dried up and they are now essentially worthless.

32156.name: flask of crypt ester
32156.col_2: An unwholesome-looking yet effective potion concocted by the innovative artisans of the Crystalline Mean. When applied with exacting care, this pungent solvent removes impurities from cryptlurker weapons, allowing their finer attributes to rise more fully to the surface. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

32157.name: spool of crypt twine
32157.col_2: An unwholesome-looking yet effective thread woven by the innovative artisans of the Crystalline Mean for the purpose of enhancing the attributes of cryptlurker vestments. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

32158.name: phial of crypt dusting
32158.col_2: This unwholesome-looking yet effective powder, devised by the innovative artisans of the Crystalline Mean, can be used to coat cryptlurker accessories with an eldritch dusting that enhances their attributes. However, advances in crafting technology have rendered it obsolete.

32159.name: Mowen's token (revelation)
32159.col_2: A note of promise received from Mowen for the delivery of Allagan tomestones of revelation. However, due to the House of Splendors changing its policies, it is now worth less than the paper on which it is scribed.

32160.name: defragmented tomestone
32160.col_2: An artifact of Allagan technology, this tomestone was constructed to extremely exacting fifth-generation specifications. Data extraction can be completed in a mere fraction of the time required by other, less-advanced information storage units. This particular variety is not as highly sought as it once was, and may no longer be exchanged for other wares.

32161.name: venture coffer
32161.col_2: Your retainer returned home with this unopened treasure chest, the contents of which remain an enticing mystery...

32162.col_2: A single, unidentified memory of the lost.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>Resistance rank required for appraisal: 10<hex:02100103>Potential memory contained: Lost Perception
